> (`SGIRE_W_PRIM_OP = 1 << 9`).  Live `exit(1)` in `dev_sgi_re.c`: **13 -> 12**.
>
> **Witnessed both directions** (`witness_20260831.out` / `..._POSTFIX.out`): TRIANGLE and POINT
> go `exit 1` -> `exit 0` with `-- declined.  (once)`; the RECTANGLE control is unchanged.
>
> **Detector `regress/sgi_de_primop_probe.py`, 21 rows, gate-wired**, every survival row PAIRED
> with a positive post-draw observable because exit status cannot distinguish declined-and-quit
> from died-with-status-0.  Six mutants measured: floor clause (a) 5/21; the `exit(0)`
> reinstatement 14/21 (red on the `live` rows only); the two latch mutants 13/21 and 18/21; a
> bit-alias onto `#498`'s bit 18/21; and a widened op mask 19/21.
>
> **THREE OF THOSE MUTANTS ARE EACH KILLED BY A SINGLE ROW, AND NONE OF THOSE THREE ROWS WAS
> WRITTEN BY THE AUTHOR** -- they exist because glm corrected which latch mutant escapes, kimi
> pointed out every row ran in a fresh session, and opus5 measured a one-hex-digit mask widening
> that swept the detector clean.
>
> **A2's inertness is the correction to carry forward**: the witness's reset-value case used `x`,
> which is not a debugger command, so it never touched memory in EITHER build and its own grep
> filtered the error.  The detector's `reset` rows supersede it by asserting the DRAW message.


`draw_primitive()` reads its op straight from a guest-written register:

```c
uint32_t op = d->de_reg[(CRIME_DE_PRIMITIVE - 0x2000) / sizeof(uint32_t)];
...
switch (op & 0xff000000) {
case DE_PRIM_LINE:       ...
case DE_PRIM_RECTANGLE:  ...
default: fatal("[ sgi_de: UNIMPLEMENTED drawing op = 0x%08x, ... ]"); exit(1);
}
```

The switch discriminates on the **top byte only**, so the domain is 256 values, two are
implemented, and **254 of 256 end the host process.**

**Reached by two ordinary stores:** write the op into `CRIME_DE_PRIMITIVE` — nothing filters it,
the `case` in the register switch only `debug()`s — then write any DE register with bit `0x800`
set, which makes the handler's tail run `if (startFlag) draw_primitive(cpu, d);`.

> **AND IT IS NOT 254 GARBAGE VALUES.** `crmfbreg.h` defines FOUR primitive types —
> `DE_PRIM_POINT` 0x00000000, `DE_PRIM_LINE` 0x01000000, `DE_PRIM_TRIANGLE` 0x02000000,
> `DE_PRIM_RECTANGLE` 0x03000000. The model implements **two**. So a **correct driver drawing a
> POINT or a TRIANGLE — documented hardware, well-formed value — kills the host.** That needs no
> malformed input at all.

**`DE_PRIM_POINT` is `0x00000000`, which is also the reset value** (`memset(d, 0, sizeof ...)` at
construction). The register's power-on state names a documented primitive the model dies on.

**That coincidence settles a detector disagreement between two seats.** fable5 held a survival
oracle cannot see a spurious `draw_primitive` (the host stays alive); kimi held that against a
pristine register file it dies in `default:` and *is* catchable. **Both are right, conditioned on
register state** — at reset the top byte is POINT, so the draw kills and a startFlagged survival
row catches it; with LINE or RECTANGLE programmed it draws silently and survival sees nothing. A
detector must pin the state it relies on, or the row's channel varies with what the guest did
before it.

**It also raises the stakes on `sgidewidth`.** That round must not copy `#497`'s splice because
this tail draws — and the thing it would draw with is lethal on 254 of 256 ops. A naive splice
does not merely cause a spurious primitive; it gives a *declined* access a near-certain host kill.

**Not covered by `sgirekills`**, which scopes itself to terminating calls *inside a
`DEVICE_ACCESS`*; this one is in a plain function and sits in the census's other bucket.

*Found by reading the kimi seat's 133 KB answer, whose verdict line was the literal words
"verdict line first." — a format miss `seat_verdicts.py` files as "answered, no verdict line",
and which I nearly recorded as a non-answer. No other seat engaged with `draw_primitive`'s default
arm. Third instance this session where the body carried what the verdict line did not.*

*No rung-3 witness yet: the reachability above is **read**, not booted. The lifecycle ruling wants
the attempt before this is recorded as unwitnessed.*

### `gxprobepccache` (med) -- a detector row that could not fail, in the shared probe harness

`gxprobe` skips a redundant register assignment when `cache_regs` is on. `_exec_at()` pops
the cached `pc` after stepping — but a driver calling `send("step")` **directly** did not, so
its next `set_reg("pc", a)` was dropped as redundant and the guest executed **nops at the
addresses the row believed it was probing**.

> A clause-(d) latch mutant swept **14/14** against the row written to catch it. The row
> performed one device access and two nops, so it **could not count to two, and therefore
> could not fail.**

**All three explanations were checked rather than one being picked**, as the
mutant-that-will-not-die rule requires: mis-built? no — the diff removes exactly the two
`d->warned |=` lines and all nine variant binaries have distinct md5s. Target dead? no —
measured directly, three unmapped writes give the fix **1** message and the mutant **3**.
Row mis-cut? **yes**, and the cause was in the instrument.

**It bit only rows reusing one instruction word.** A driver alternating two different words
gets a cache miss on `pc` and works by accident — which is why eight of nine variants scored
plausibly and nothing looked wrong. *A vacuous row reads exactly like a passing row.*

**Blast radius, measured — and my first measurement was wrong.** I grepped for probes calling
`send("step")` and found **fourteen**; then checked whether they use gxprobe at all, and
**none does** — every one rolls its own pty plumbing. A grep for the symptom found the wrong
population; the discriminator was whether the file imports the harness.

**Fixed at source rather than documented.** The seat proposed a rule (*any driver stepping
without `_exec_at()` must pop the pc cache*). Removing the footgun is better: the
invalidation now lives in `send()`, so any command that advances the guest invalidates `pc`
wherever it is sent from. Controlled — `step`, `step 3`, `continue`, `c`, `s` fire it;
`print pc`, `reg`, `put w` and the empty string do not.

*And a separate finding fell out: **`gxprobe.py` is not in version control.** `git ls-files`
matches zero; it lives only in `_scratchpad/`. The carrier tells every round to use it rather
than hand-roll pty plumbing — so the tree's recommended instrument is untracked, covered by no
gate, one accident away from being lost, and this defect would have been invisible to
`git log` forever.*

    row                marker      strictly-later?   same-date siblings
    ns16550            2026-08-22        no                 1

### `holdmarkermulti` (med) -- the hold-marker check cannot fire on its largest cases

`gen_codex_wall.py` exists because section I requires that every `[HELD AWAITING SEAT: ...]`
marker is also named in the queue — its own docstring: *holding a stage and queueing it are ONE
action, not two*. **Its regex accepts a single `[a-z0-9_]+` seat name.** A marker naming two or
more seats contains commas, fails the match, and is neither counted nor required to appear.

> **So the enforcement is strongest on the smallest holds and absent on the biggest.** A stage
> awaiting one seat is policed; one awaiting all seven is not — and a seven-seat hold is, by
> construction, the one carrying the most owed work.

**Measured, not argued:** `sgirekills` is held awaiting `opus5, codex, grok, kimi, glm,
deepseek, minimax` and is reported in no count.

**The fix is a strict token grammar, and the character class this entry first prescribed was
refuted by the panel.** `[a-z0-9_]+(?:[ \t]*,[ \t]*[a-z0-9_]+)*` — not
`[a-z0-9_,\s]+`, which was **measured to span newlines** and, in a ledger holding quoted
markers, manufactures phantom holds. The grammar also kills a `split(", ")` separator mutant
that survived the character class.

> **This entry also called a quotation in `ledgerstatelies` a "built-in negative control". That
> control is VACUOUS** — the row has zero entries and its quotation sits in a row-level field
> `held_rows()` never reads, so the permissive class this entry forbade passes every control and
> renders byte-identically. *A row filed to document a check-that-cannot-fail shipped with a
> check that could not fail.* Caught pre-ship by four seats independently.

**Known limits, stated rather than discovered later:** a marker wrapped across lines stays
invisible (deliberate — admitting newlines re-opens the phantom surface), and a hyphenated
transport id (`kimi-k3`) would be invisible. No ledger seat id needs one today — checked.

**And the real detector is `--check`, not the controls.** Of nine mutants a seat built, only
reverting the comma is killed by the controls; section I2 kills three more.

*Found while defanging stale markers: the count did not move for the multi-seat ones, and a count
that does not move is not thereby correct — the same tell the carrier records from the stuck 27.*

### `otherkilldeath` (med) -- a DEATH-ONLY oracle, and the round fixed its mirror image
### while shipping this one

`sgi_re_width_probe.py`'s catch-all row captures the transcript and **throws it away** --
`row("other kill", how, "exit1", ...)` uses only how-it-died -- while its six `ld kill`
siblings twelve lines above compute a text membership test and report `exit1+txt`.

> **So the row's note claims IDENTITY — *the catch-all is untouched* — on an oracle that
> observes only DEATH.** Any edit keeping the arm fatal while changing what it *is* passes.

**Measured**, with the prediction filed before building: altering the catch-all's message text
while leaving `exit(1)` untouched scores **35/35 — zero red rows.** The matched control
(altering one *read* arm's text) scores **34/35**, reddening `tlb_a ld kill`. The pair is the
point: it proves the six siblings are failable and this one is not.

**It is the `d_returnzero` lesson mirrored onto the death side.** That was a survival-only
oracle where survival is the shared answer; this is a death-only oracle where death is. Same
shape, opposite polarity — and the round repaired the first while shipping the second.

**Finding it discharged an obligation the two tables never did.** Across all 41 preserved probe
outputs, **seven rows were red under no mutant in either table**. `PRETABLE.out` names their
channel, but no mutant exercising it was ever built — so for those seven the CHANNEL line was
satisfied **on paper**. Six are now measured failable; **one remains blind, and it is this row.**

**Coverage debt, not a floor breach**, and the reasoning is recorded so nobody re-argues it:
(a), (b), (c) pass and the row does red on a null medium; the catch-all is not a predicate the
fix *depends on*, so the bounded (d) closure does not reach it; and clause (e)'s contract says
*silent **removal***, which this mutant is not — **the contract is precise even though the
row's inline note overclaimed.**

*Fix is one line — the text membership test its siblings already carry. Deliberately not done
in-round: editing a shipped detector row means re-measuring, and the stopping rule fixes only
measured false passes and wrong records. This is a row weaker than its note claimed, and the
note has been corrected to say so.*

### `gatedevicesplit` (low) -- filed because a comment already claimed it was

The `#497` gate comment ended *"the right answer is a `gate_devices.sh` split ... **Filed,
not done**"* -- **and it was not filed.** No ledger row, no queue entry, under any
phrasing. Caught by the pass-2 seat while that comment was still **staged**.

> *That is the gap-closes-itself shape: a claim that a process step is complete, shipping
> in the same commit as the thing it excuses. A future reader greps for the row, finds
> nothing, and cannot tell whether the split was considered and rejected or forgotten.*

**And the precedent claim was one step short**, which the same seat measured. I wrote that
`gate_arm.sh` already runs footbridge and PIT probes, *"neither an ARM instruction test"*
-- true, **but both run `-E cats`, this gate's own ARM machine**, and the PIT wiring
comment says outright that it was placed there *because* "this is the only gate whose
machine it shares." So `#497`'s probe is **not** the third instance of an existing
accretion -- it is the **first probe in this gate on a foreign machine AND CPU family.**
My words were true; my implication was generous to my own decision.

**Forcing criterion, so this cannot sit forever:** *the next device probe wired into
`gate_arm.sh` converts this from FILED to OWED.* The accretion story guarantees each
addition makes the next cheaper, which is how a least-bad accommodation becomes permanent.

**Operational cost, named rather than left to be discovered:** a red row in `gate_arm` can
now mean an SGI/MIPS device regression -- an attribution trap for whoever reads the
battery output.

### `agyreservation` (med) -- the owner's ruling lives in the carrier as PROSE, and
### `panel.sh` fired the seat anyway within two hours

The owner ruled on 2026-08-30 that **agy is RESERVED FOR MEASUREMENT and held out of routine
panels** — it is the only compile-and-measure seat *not* behind the Agent-tool transport, and
therefore the roster's insurance against the outage that once cost a round all its measuring
capacity at once.

**The ruling was written into the carrier. `panel.sh` was not touched.**
`grep -ci 'reserved for measurement' panel.sh` returns **0**, its AGY block is unconditional,
and `panel_20260830_214531/agy.txt` is an 11 KB answer from a routine panel fired *after* the
ruling.

> *This is the carrier's own structure-first finding, measured against itself: knowing a rule
> and having it fire on the right object are different problems, and only the second is solved
> by writing more. A rule that earns its second instance while sitting in that file has proven
> it was mis-filed as prose. **This one earned its first in under two hours.***

**The fix follows the `OLLAMA4` precedent, and that precedent's warning is the load-bearing
part:** a variable, plus a conditional **banner, launch, seat check and verdict roster**. The
carrier records why all four — blanking the variable alone once left a *phantom seat that
answered the seat check*. The agy hazard inverts: a missing seat would read as a **failure**
where the truth is a deliberate omission.

**And that distinction is the ruling's whole cost clause:** a seat *deliberately not fired* is
a different thing from a seat *failure*, and a different thing again from *agreement*.
Conflating them is what the seat ledger exists to refuse — so the check must print
**DELIBERATELY NOT FIRED** by name, every panel.

*Deferred, not forgotten: a panel was running when this was found, and bash reads scripts
incrementally by byte offset, so editing `panel.sh` mid-run corrupts that run. The urge to
edit arrives exactly when you are watching it run, which is why the rule exists.*

### `witnesssilent` (low) -- 13 witnesses are ungated by design, so a rotted one looks
### exactly like a working one

`check_probe_wiring.py` reports **13 witnesses correctly ungated** -- and *correctly* is
the right word. Gating a witness would **manufacture** a regression, because a witness is
built to INVERT after its fix: `#496`'s reads 15/15 pre-fix and 11/15 post-fix, and its
record says so.

> **But ungated means unrun, and unrun means a witness whose arms rot is indistinguishable
> from one that works.**

`n6` supplies the concrete instance: `fbpending_witness.py` scores a row on a death at the
very site `n6`'s ACCEPT round removes, and **no gate runs it** -- so when that round ships,
the witness breaks on disk and nothing anywhere says so.

**The remedy is not an invention.** `fbpending_drain_probe.py` already carries `EXPECT_CAP`
defaulting to `-1 = report only`, its scoring gated on `EXPECT_CAP >= 0`. Run-but-do-not-
score exists, is understood, and supplies the transferred warrant the addition licence
requires -- that plus a measured instance, never *it cannot hurt*.

**And it is harder than it looks, which is why this is filed rather than built.** A witness
is *supposed* to change score after its fix lands, so report-only output is **noisy by
construction**: a flipped row is the expected inversion, or a real break, and the raw
output cannot tell them apart. Making it useful means each witness recording its
**expected post-fix score** -- a change to what every witness in the tree must carry, which
is an owner decision rather than a round's.

*Ranked LOW deliberately: apparatus about apparatus, competing with four open HIGH rows
that are live host kills. Filed so `n6` can name it rather than discover it.*

### `fbfiqsilent` (med) -- the FIQ column lies quietly where the IRQ column kills

`n6` is about to ACCEPT the `+0x188` IRQEnable read on the warrant that the DC21285 prose
makes it a documented read-only register. **That same prose covers `188h` and `288h`
jointly** — and `case FIQ_ENABLE_SET:` has a write arm and then `break;`, with **no read arm
at all**. Verified by opening the file. A guest that sets FIQ bits and reads them back gets
**zero: wrong value, no kill, no announce.**

> **It is not in the eight-kill census, and that is the point.** Same semantic class, same
> one-line fix shape, same row shape — differing only in that the IRQ column *kills* where
> the FIQ column *lies quietly*. Shipping the IRQ accept while leaving its FIQ twin silently
> wrong and unnamed is exactly the asymmetry the sibling-parity line exists to catch.

**And it is a COLUMN, not a site:** `FIQ_ENABLE_CLEAR`'s read side is also a silent constant
zero while its IRQ twin kills. Worth **one sentence** in the decline round's `PRETABLE.out`
rather than five separate discoveries later.

*Found by the sibling-parity check firing at DESIGN time, which is where it is supposed to
fire — while adjudicating a different question about round ordering.*

### `sgideoob` -- ~~WITHDRAWN~~: a FALSE out-of-bounds, filed and refuted the same evening
### found it

> *** WITHDRAWN. The arithmetic below skips one line and that line refutes it. ***
> `relative_addr &= ~CRIME_DE_START` (`0x0800`) runs **immediately before** the index
> computation, so `relative_addr` is capped at `0x7ff`, `regnr` at **511**, and
> `regnr+1` at **512** -- in a `[DEV_SGI_DE_LENGTH / sizeof(uint32_t)]` = `[1024]`
> array. **512 slots of headroom.** The `mte_reg` twin is identical.
>
> **The real class is narrower and better stated:** *is the array sized to the INDEX
> RANGE or to the FULL WINDOW?* Sized to the index range and the `+1` overflows
> (`re_linear_a[32]`, `re_tlb_x[256]`); sized to the full window and the over-sizing is
> what prevents it. Kept rather than deleted so the next reader finds the refutation
> instead of re-filing the row.

The original text follows.

`DEVICE_ACCESS(sgi_de)`'s `len==8` arm writes **both** `de_reg[regnr]` and `de_reg[regnr+1]`
into `uint32_t de_reg[DEV_SGI_DE_LENGTH / sizeof(uint32_t)]`. At the top of the window,
`regnr+1` indexes one past the end.

**Same shield and same trap as `sgilinearoob`.** Guest paths cannot reach it — an 8-byte
access must be 8-aligned and the top offset is only 4-aligned — but the debugger's `put d`
prints a warning and **proceeds**. That does **not** give this row a witness; **it takes one
away.** A `put d` reproduction bypasses the guest instruction path entirely and would be
laundering rather than witnessing.

> **The shape is now a class, not a coincidence.** `sgilinearoob` (`re_linear_[ab][tlbi+1]`
> into a `[32]`), the TLB arms' unmasked loop increment, and now `de_reg[regnr+1]`: three
> sites, one form — **a store whose arity is fixed by the ACCESS WIDTH while its index is
> bounded only by the OFFSET MASK.** A future round should ask whether the bound belongs at
> the index computation rather than at each store.

*Surfaced by the adjudicating seat while designing `sgidewidth`, and explicitly kept out of
it: that round's decline does not touch the `len==8` arm, so folding it in would be scope
creep rather than adjacency.*

### `exitcensus` (med) -- the reachability bucket over-counted by 14.4%, and I had just
### declared this tool free of exactly this defect

`exit_census.py`'s **per-file totals are correct**. Its **BY-ENCLOSING-CONSTRUCT split was
not**, and that is the half that ranks.

`MARK` is `^(DEVICE_ACCESS|DEVINIT|DEVICE_TICK|static\s)`. A plain **non-static** function
definition -- `void draw_primitive(...)`, `void do_mte_transfer(...)` -- is therefore not a
boundary, so every terminating call inside one was attributed to the preceding
`DEVICE_ACCESS`.

> **That bucket is a REACHABILITY CLAIM used to rank defects** -- the tool tags it, in its own
> words, *"on a guest access path BY CONSTRUCTION"*. Over-counting it over-states how many
> host kills a guest can actually reach.

Measured tree-wide over `src/devices` (118 files, 172 live calls):

```
DEVICE_ACCESS    97 -> 83     a 14-call, 14.4% over-count
static           51 -> 13     the same defect from the other side: a plain function
                              FOLLOWING a static one was inheriting `static`
```

**Controlled against a hand-derived fixture.** `dev_sgi_re.c`'s true split was derived by hand
and independently reproduced by two seats: `DEVICE_ACCESS` **15** (sgi_re 13 + sgi_de 1 +
sgi_mte 1), plain functions **6** (draw_primitive 1 + do_mte_transfer 5). Before the fix the
tool put all 21 in `DEVICE_ACCESS`; after it, exactly 15/6.

**The first draft of the fix had a defect of its own, caught before shipping**: the new
pattern also matched `DEVICE_ACCESS(foo)` lines, giving two marks at one offset. Harmless
*today* -- at equal offset the `DEVICE_ACCESS` label sorts last and wins -- but that is a
silent dependence on sort order inside a tool whose output ranks defects. Excluded; duplicates
measured 0 across five files.

**Consequence already in the tree:** `sgirekills`' title read *"21 terminating calls inside
DEVICE_ACCESS"*, taken faithfully from the wrong figure. Corrected.

*The honest shape: I diagnosed this defect correctly by hand this evening, then wrongly
concluded the shipped tool did not have it -- because I checked the number people quote
(per-file) rather than the number that ranks (per-construct).*

### `sgireunmapped` (high) -- the widest door in the device, and no row covered it

> ### *** STATUS 2026-08-31: THE FIX IS SHIPPED AND CLOSED (`a643e18 9f666a8`).  WHAT IS OPEN
> ### IS ITS DETECTOR, AND THE CHAIN IS ON ITS FOURTH PASS. ***
>
> **The product fix is not in question and is not reopened.** The catch-all is a per-direction
> latched decline falling through to the function's common tail; live `exit(1)` in that file
> went 14 -> 13.  Every pass since has been about the DETECTOR that ships with it.
>
> | pass | on | what it found |
> |---|---|---|
> | 1 | `9f666a8` | two mutants sweeping the 28-row detector CLEAN |
> | 2 | `938b328` | the repair reproduced the SAME GAP one level down |
> | 3 | `4daa506` | **two MEASURED clean sweeps** (`M1` direction, `M2` position) and a **RED GATE ON A GREEN PROBE** |
> | 4 | `de1a0de` | the CLASS closure -- **50** rows, the state space enumerated once, plus an L2 repair of pass 4's OWN floor breach |
>
> **THREE BREACHES, ONE CLASS, THREE TIMES.**  Each was a cell of the catch-all's state space
> left empty, repaired at exactly the address the mutant had used, leaving the symmetric cell
> open for the next pass.  Pass 1 found *width* unpinned, pass 2 *component*, pass 3 *direction*
> AND *position*.  The measuring seat's warning is the reason pass 4 is shaped differently:
> *"adding two more rows at the corner I just named will produce a fourth."*
>
> So pass 4 does not patch cells.  It enumerates the catch-all's FIVE INPUTS -- `relative_addr`
> (component AND position within it), `writeflag`, `len`, `idata`, `d->warned` -- closes every
> cell in one diff, and writes into the probe's CONTRACT which cells are covered and which are
> **deliberately not**, so a later escape is *"outside the contract, as stated"* rather than a
> fourth breach.
>
> **GATE, at 50 rows, run ALONE and IN FULL: PASS -- 506 checks, 0 FAIL, rc=0, with
> `sgi_re unmapped rows emitted/green/red` at 50/50/0 and both L2 repair rows green.**  Log at
> `regress/artifacts/sgireunmapped/killtable_20260831/pass4/gate_arm_pass4_50rows.log`.  That was
> the round's one KNOWN GAP -- the gate had passed at 48 rows and had not been re-run after the L2
> repair -- and it is now closed.  Pass 4 owes only its pass 5.
>
> **`M2` is this project's own newest rule un-transferred by one hop**, and that is the part
> worth carrying: the carrier says an accept row at a window's BASE tests the near bound twice
> and the far bound never.  That was applied to the six named windows IN THIS VERY FILE and not
> to the catch-all's first component, whose four rows all sat at the base.  One hex digit --
> `>= CRIME_RE_LINEAR_A` to `- 0x10` -- swept 36 rows clean.
>
> **And the gate defect is the one a green probe could never show.**  Both rows added by pass 2
> were named exactly 16 characters; the probe prints names through `%-16s` and the gate's
> per-row pattern needs two spaces.  `got=0` against `want=1` **on a fully green build** --
> found by two seats independently, and shipped because the gate SCRIPT was never run after the
> rows were added, only the probe.  Repaired structurally: `row()` now asserts
> `len(name) <= 15`.


`DEVICE_ACCESS(sgi_re)`'s final `else` -- the unmatched-address arm -- prints a `fatal()`
per direction and then `exit(1)`, **with no width predicate at all.** Every other kill in
that handler needs the guest to choose an unusual access WIDTH (the six `len != 8` arms) or
a DIRECTION (the six read arms). This one needs neither: **any width, either direction, any
unmatched address.**

**The door, derived rather than asserted.** `memory_device_register` covers
`baseaddr + 0x1000` for `DEV_SGI_RE_LENGTH` = `0x1000`, and the handler restores the full
offset with `relative_addr += 0x1000`, so the dispatched range is `0x1000-0x1fff`. The six
windows occupy `0x1000-0x17ff` with one internal gap:

```
  TLB_A     0x1000-0x11ff        TEX       0x1600-0x16df
  TLB_B     0x1200-0x13ff        LINEAR_A  0x1700-0x177f
  TLB_C     0x1400-0x15ff        LINEAR_B  0x1780-0x17ff

  UNCOVERED 0x16e0-0x16ff   (32 bytes)
            0x1800-0x1fff   (2048 bytes)   = 2080 bytes -> exit(1)
```

Guest KSEG1: a single `lb` at **`0xb5001800`** ends the host process.

> *** IT SURVIVES BOTH ROUNDS THAT LOOK LIKE THEY WOULD FIX IT, WHICH IS WHY IT IS FILED
> BEFORE THE NEXT COMPLETENESS SENTENCE SHIPS. *** `#497` repairs the six WIDTH guards and
> never reaches this arm. `sgirekills` as scoped repairs the six READ arms *inside* the
> windows and never reaches it either. A reader of either round record could reasonably
> conclude the device no longer kills on a stray access. **It does.**

**Its fix cannot be ACCEPT**, and that is what keeps it out of `sgirekills`' round rather
than a scheduling preference: nothing backs an unmapped address, so there is no stored value
to return. DECLINE plus a latched `(once)` announce -- a different fix design, so the
round-scope rule's same-fix-design arm fails.

**Witness: none yet, and it is ONE ROW on an existing script.** The machine, window and
harness all exist from `widthkillclass`'s witness (`-E sgi -e ip32`); add one `lb` at
`0xb5001800` and expect `exit1` with `[ sgi_re: unimplemented read from address 0x1800 ]`.

*Found by the adjudicating seat while RANKING the other four `sgi_re` rows -- not by looking
for it. An earlier audit had listed this arm as "1 unhandled offset fallback" and never
asked whether it was reachable. **A census that enumerates a site without ranking it is how
the widest door stays open.***

### `sgidewidth` (high) -- a SEVENTH live width kill, one guest `sb` away

The scope question on `#497` was hiding it. `grep -n 'len = %i not implemented'
src/devices/dev_sgi_re.c`:

```c
	} else {
		fatal("sgi_de: len = %i not implemented\n", len);
		exit(1);
	}
```

The `else` of an accept set of `{4, 8}` — so **len ∈ {1,2,3,5,6,7} ends the host process**,
and a single guest `sb` to the DE window does it.

**It does not join `#497`, and the reason is the joining clause working rather than being
dodged:** different registered device (`sgi_de`, its own `memory_device_register`), accept set
`{4,8}` not `{8}`, and — the part that settles it — **its registers are READABLE**, so its
accept rows read back through `odata` while `sgi_re`'s read back through debug lines. Second
fix shape, second row species.

> **But it MUST be named in `#497`'s PRETABLE and round record.** A round called
> `widthkillclass` that fixes six of seven live width kills *in the same file* and does not say
> so writes the false-unanimity record the late-dissent rule forbids.

The four handlers share one `struct sgi_re_data` from a single malloc, so whatever latch
infrastructure `#497` lands is already reachable here — the fix is cheap once the witness
exists, and the witness is one row away using `#497`'s own script.

### `sgimtewidth` (med) -- a one-byte store silently ZEROES the adjacent register

`if (len == 4) {…} else if (len != 4) {…} else {…}`. The second arm is reached by **every**
width that is not 4, including 1 and 2:

```c
	d->mte_reg[regnr+1] = idata >> 32;
	d->mte_reg[regnr]   = idata;
```

For a one-byte store `idata` is a byte, so `idata >> 32` is **0** — the store clobbers
`mte_reg[regnr+1]` with zero. No diagnostic, no decline: the device quietly loses a register
the guest never addressed. A mis-service, not a kill, which is why it is med.

> ### The trap, and it is why this is filed now rather than when someone touches it
>
> The dead third arm is `fatal("[ sgi_mte: UNIMPLEMENTED read/write len %i ]"); exit(1);` —
> unreachable for every integer `len`, as `sgirekills` records. **It documents an intent to
> reject unusual widths.** A naive future repair of the unreachable-arm defect — reordering to
> `len==4 / len==8 / else` — would **resurrect that `exit(1)` as a live width kill.**
>
> So when the unreachable arm is worked it must land as a DECLINE, never a revived exit.

*Two defects in one arm structure pointing opposite ways: today it serves widths it should
refuse, and the obvious tidy-up would make it kill on widths it currently serves.*

### `sgilinearoob` (med) -- the width guard `#497` removes is holding an OOB WRITE shut

Found by the opus5 seat while auditing whether `len != 8` should be declined or *implemented*.
Every element re-verified by opening the file.

Both LINEAR arms compute `int tlbi = ((relative_addr & 0x7f) >> 2) & 0x1f;` — so `tlbi` ranges
**0..31** — then write **both** `[tlbi]` and `[tlbi+1]` into `uint32_t re_linear_a[32]` /
`re_linear_b[32]`. **At `tlbi == 31` the second store writes index 32, one past the end.**

> **It is unreachable today for exactly one reason: `len == 8` forces 8-byte alignment.** [2026-11-02, records: the reason is misstated -- the guard tests LENGTH, and width does not imply alignment; on guest paths `tlbi` is kept even by CPU-side alignment (ld/sd raise ADES/ADEL before `memory_rw`, and the unaligned helper masks the address), while the host debugger's `put d` can deliver an unaligned `len == 8` (987cb596 `dev_sgi_re.c:640-671`, `:735-741`)]
> `(0x78 & 0x7f) >> 2` = 30, so the largest reachable `tlbi` is 30 and `tlbi+1` is 31 — the
> last valid index. Permit `len == 4` and offset `0x7c` gives `(0x7c & 0x7f) >> 2` = **31**,
> and index 32 is written.

From the declaration order (`re_tlb_a`, `re_tlb_b`, `re_tlb_c`, `re_tex`, `re_linear_a[32]`,
`re_linear_b[32]`, `de_reg[]`): `re_linear_a[32]` overlays `re_linear_b[0]`, and
`re_linear_b[32]` overlays the start of `de_reg[]` — **a different engine's registers**. That
is a layout fact, not a guarantee: a struct reorder changes *which* field is hit, not whether
the write is out of bounds.

**This is why `#497` must DECLINE rather than IMPLEMENT**, and it converts a stylistic
preference into a measured-from-source argument. The brief asked whether `len != 8` is
"secretly an IMPLEMENT case." It is not — implementing narrower widths at the LINEAR arms
would **make this OOB live**.

**And it is the second such fact in the same audit.** The TLB/TEX store loop reads
`data[hwi]*256 + data[hwi+1]`, so a `len == 1` access reads `data[1]` — one byte past the
*caller's* buffer. Two different over-reads, both held shut by the same guard, neither noticed
until a seat was asked whether the guard could be relaxed.

**The round owes a sentence, not a row.** `#497` does not touch these lines and cannot make
the OOB live — a latched decline keeps `len == 8` mandatory. What it owes is a comment at the
site saying *why* the guard is mandatory, so a future round reading "unimplemented width" as
an invitation to implement one is warned where the decision happens.

*Source-derived, not measured: no probe has driven a 4-byte LINEAR access, because the shipped
code kills the host before reaching the store [2026-11-02, records: true at 83477305; since `#497` (821eb83b) an access whose len is not 8 is declined -- a latched `fatal()`, then the common tail's `return 1` -- so the emulator keeps running and the store is still not reached (987cb596 `dev_sgi_re.c:640-686`)]. It cannot be witnessed without first
introducing the defect.*

### `lcaconfwidth` (low) -- filed 2026-08-31: the kill diagnostic can name a value that would not have killed

`dev_lca.c`'s `LCA_IOC_CONF` guard is:

```c
if (idata & ~1) {
        fatal("TODO: Write to unimplemented bit of IOC_CONF: 0x%x\n", (int)idata);
        exit(1);
}
```

`idata` is 64-bit. A write of `0x100000000` has `idata & ~1` TRUE, so the host dies — while
`(int)idata` truncates to zero and the diagnostic prints `0x0`. **The message names a value that
would not have triggered it**, so a future reader debugging the death is told the wrong cause.

That is a WRONG RECORD emitted by product code at the exact moment of the kill, which is the one
place a wrong record is hardest to recover from: the process is gone and the log is all that is
left. The fix is the printf specifier, not the guard.

> #### *** THIS LINE NAMED THE WRONG SPECIFIER **AND** CLAIMED IT WAS THE FILE'S OWN IDIOM.
> #### Both halves are false.  Corrected 2026-09-07, caught by the grok seat answering the
> #### witness-design brief and verified here by reading the file. ***
>
> It said the fix is `` `0x%llx` with a `(long long)` cast, the file's own idiom elsewhere ``.
> **`dev_lca.c` uses `PRIx64` five times and `%llx` never.**  The five sibling arms twelve to
> ninety lines away -- TB_ENA, W_BASE0, W_MASK0, W_BASE1, W_MASK1 -- all read:
>
> ```c
> 				fatal("TODO: LCA_IOC_TB_ENA value "
> 				    " (0x%" PRIx64") has unimplemented "
> 				    "bits.\n", (uint64_t)idata);
> ```
>
> **Note they KEEP the cast** -- `(uint64_t)idata`, widening rather than narrowing.  An earlier
> draft of the design brief said to *drop* the cast, which would have been a third wrong form.
> **The correct repair is the sibling line, copied:** `0x%" PRIx64` with `(uint64_t)idata`.
>
> *A record that names a fix AND asserts it matches the surrounding code is the most costly
> kind to get wrong: it discourages the one check -- reading a sibling -- that would catch it.
> Verified safe to change: no gate, hygiene grep or probe in `regress/` matches on this
> message's text.*

**Deliberately NOT folded into `lcabadval`**, which is about the guards themselves. They interact
and the ordering matters: `lcabadval`'s rows must match the `fatal()` TEXT rather than the exit
status (see that row's confound), so any row written against this arm inherits this bug's output.

*Found by the `lcabadval` rung-3 seat as an aside while answering a different question, and
re-verified by reading the arm.*

> ### *** CENSUSED THE SAME DAY: THIS IS A CLASS, NOT A SITE.  Widened low -> med. ***
>
> **The derivers, because the two numbers answer different questions and only one of them is a
> defect count:**
>
>     grep -rc '(int)idata\|(int) idata' src/devices/*.c | grep -v ':0$'
>
> plus a window scan for those casts that sit in a diagnostic at a site which then `exit(1)`s.
> On 2026-08-31 the first gave **309 casts across 70 device files** and the second **45 host-kill
> sites**, about twenty carrying an explicit full-width guard.
>
> **MOST OF THE 309 ARE NOT DEFECTS AND SAYING SO IS THE POINT** — an 8- or 16-bit register loses
> nothing through `(int)`. The defect needs BOTH halves: a guard testing the FULL 64-bit value
> (`idata & ~MASK`, `idata != CONST`) AND a diagnostic printing the truncated one. Then a write
> whose only distinguishing bits are above bit 31 dies while the message reports a value that
> would have been accepted.
>
> *** THE SHARPEST INSTANCE, verified by computation and by reading the arm: `dev_pvr.c`'s
> `if (writeflag == MEM_WRITE && idata != 0x0cff0000)` paired with `(int) idata`. *** A guest
> writing `0x1_0cff0000` fails the 64-bit compare and the host dies — and the message prints
> `0x0cff0000`, **exactly the value the code says is acceptable**. The diagnostic tells a
> maintainer the guest wrote the correct value and died for it.
>
> **Severity, reasoned rather than assumed:** none of this changes *whether* the host dies — the
> guards are unchanged. It changes what the log says about *why*, at the one moment the log is all
> that survives. A records-correctness defect in product code, not a control-flow one.
>
> **NOT a one-line sweep.** Which sites are genuinely reachable with a >32-bit datum depends on
> register width and the guest paths that reach them, and a blanket edit to 45 diagnostics is the
> unlicensed addition this project refuses. The honest first round is the ~20 full-width-guard
> sites, ordered by whether a guest can deliver a >32-bit write at all.

### `mtetlbflood` (low) -- filed 2026-08-31: an unlatched guest-drivable `fatal()` in the MTE

`dev_sgi_re.c`'s MTE `switch (dst_tlb)` implements TLB A/B/C and LINEAR_A/LINEAR_B. `dst_tlb` is
a **3-bit guest-controlled field** — `(mode & 0x1c) >> 2` — so values 3 (`MTE_TLB_TEX`), 6
(`MTE_TLB_CLIP`) and 7 reach `default:`.

That arm is a bare `fatal()` with **no `exit(1)`**, so it is *not* a host kill — but it carries
**no latch either**, so a guest looping over MTE operations floods host stdout without bound.
`floodclass` family. The house idiom is `N = 1` per device instance with the suppression marker
in the message text; **derive the marker's spelling and count rather than quoting one** — that
figure has been wrong in this file twice.

**Distinct from `sgideprimop`**, which is the drawing-op switch in the same file and *does*
`exit(1)` [2026-11-02, records: no longer -- `#500` (840f3d0a) made that arm a latched decline that breaks out of the switch (987cb596 `dev_sgi_re.c:1150-1163`)]. Both are guest-driven `switch` defaults in `dev_sgi_re.c` and a round touching one
should say explicitly that it is not touching the other.

*Found by the `sgitexindex` seat as a residual while checking an unrelated question, and
re-verified by reading.*

### OPEN -- filed 2026-09-01 from `#500`'s pass-4 panel: three residuals the panel raised and
### DECLINED to reopen in-round, plus one cell disclosed as uncoverable

Filed under the stopping rule: none is a MEASURED FALSE PASS against the shipped detector's
floor, and none is a WRONG RECORD.  The grok seat named the first three and said plainly it
was not asking for them to be reopened; recording them so a future round does not rediscover
them as findings.

**`sgideprimopdraw`** -- *** THE DETECTOR HAS NO DRAWING ORACLE, AND ONE MASK CELL IS
THEREFORE UNCOVERABLE RATHER THAN UNCOVERED. ***  Narrowing the `draw_primitive()` selector
mask at bit 24 or 25 -- `op & 0xff000000` -> `& 0xfd000000` -- collapses the two IMPLEMENTED
cases onto each other (LINE `0x01000000`, RECTANGLE `0x03000000`) instead of restoring a host
kill.  Every row stays green, **correctly**: both values are still accepted and the guest still
runs.

Seeing it needs an oracle for what was DRAWN, and there is none to build at reset.  Verified
by reading rather than taken from the seat that raised it: `horrible_getputpixel` returns
early at `if (!(tileptr & 0x80000000))` in `dev_sgi_re.c`, and for `tlb_mode` 0-2 the pointer
is `d->re_tlb_a[tile_nr] << 16`, which is zero on a reset machine.  **So even a *successful*
draw writes nothing any row could watch.**

> *This is a MISSING CHANNEL, not a missing row, and the distinction decides the disposition:
> adding rows cannot close it, so it is DISCLOSED in the probe contract and in the pass-5 kill
> table -- which builds the mutant anyway and PREDICTS ITS ESCAPE IN WRITING, before the run.
> A predicted escape is a measurement; an unpredicted one is a breach.*

A round that gives this device a drawing oracle -- a guest that programs a TLB entry with the
valid bit set, then reads back the tile memory -- closes this cell and the two below at once.
That is the round to file, not more rows.

**`sgideprimrdpair`** -- `rd surv` is the file's one survival row with no positive companion.
The `print v0` in that session IS the START-aliased read, and no row consumes it, so
`draw_primitive(); if (writeflag == MEM_READ) exit(0);` keeps both `rd` rows green.  That is
the `exit0oracle` class -- exit status cannot distinguish *declined and quit* from *died with
status 0* -- applied to the one arm this detector left unpaired.  Settled design rather than
this diff, but it is true of the shipped composite and should be said out loud.

**`sgideprimemptybody`** -- `case DE_PRIM_RECTANGLE: break;` with an emptied body scores
`count(DRAW) == 0` and the guest runs on, so every accept row passes.  The `* liv` companions
catch DEATH, not a silent NO-OP.  Same drawing-oracle gap as `sgideprimopdraw`; it is the
accept side of the same missing channel.

*Provenance: `_scratchpad/panel_20260901_192203_500p4` (grok, codex, kimi).  All three were
raised by seats that explicitly declined to reopen them in-round, which is the disposition the
stopping rule asks for and is recorded here as such.*

blocks) and `warned_unimpl` (#501) are per-instance fields, but every probe session is a fresh process, so no

pcc2 instances in one process and announces from each once would.  Shared with the width chain; filed, not owed.

**`pcc2defaultkill` PROMOTED TO HIGH (2026-09-04 fix review; Fable 5.1 adjudicating, GPT-6 Astra concurring).**
The unimplemented offsets are REAL PCC2 registers the one in-tree guest driver writes: OpenBSD 2.2
`if_ie.c:609` stores `pcc2_lancirq` (IEICR, 0x2a), `:612` `pcc2_lancerrirq` (0x2b), `:655`
`pcc2_lancerrstat` (IEERR, 0x28) -- verified by grep in `_guest-src-openbsd22` -- plus GPIO_ICR 0x18,
SCSIERR 0x2c, the printer block 0x30-0x37, SPEED 0x38 and SCCTXIACK 0x25; none has a `case`, so any
access, READ included, reaches `default:` and its `exit(1)`.  Ranked FIRST, above `pcc2c040kill`, because
that one needs a GENCTL write the in-tree guest never makes.  **RE-BASED 2026-09-05 (Fable design seat,
verified from the tree): `if_ie` NEVER ATTACHES on the emulated mvme187** -- `machine_mvme88k.c:106` installs
`unreadable` at 0xfff46000, the ie0 address, and `if_ie.c:407-409` fails its match on `badpaddr()` there, so
the driver's PCC2 writes never run on this model.  The ranking rests on the RUNG-3 WITNESS and severity (one
guest byte load or store to any of 43 offsets ends the host), not on the driver.  Witness (measured
2026-09-05, `regress/artifacts/pcc2defaultkill/witness_20260905/`): a GUEST `st.b` or `ld.bu` to IEICR ->
exit 1 with the arm's own 'unimplemented' line first; the debugger's `put b` does NOT reach the arm.  Option set for pass 1: DECLINE + latched announce / BACKED ACCEPT (the register array
already backs every offset and the memcpy read path already serves it) / FAULT.

Found by the adjudicating seat while ranking `pcc2widthkills`, and it is filed rather than
folded into that round because the predicate class differs: **offset decode, not access
width.**  The round-scope rule takes one site and admits a second only in the same semantic
class under one fix design; these are two classes in one file.

> **The reason it matters that it has NO ROW, rather than merely being unfixed:** without one,

### `clausedbound` -- RULE QUESTION: does clause (d)'s DEPENDS-ON bound admit enclosing-function values?

**2026-09-03, filed by `#500` pass 14 at the measuring seat's request.**  Not a code defect; a
question about the carrier's own rule, and one the seat declined to rule on alone.

The bound, as written: *"predicates DOMINATING the diff's edited lines, walked up only to the
ENCLOSING FUNCTION BOUNDARY; and operand swaps drawn ONLY from fields the guarded BODY reads."*

The case: `|| (drawmode & DE_DRAWMODE_XFER_EN)` on `draw_primitive()`'s latch guard swept the
shipped 47-row detector clean (MEASURED, with a control both ways).  `drawmode` is read by the
enclosing FUNCTION, three times above the switch, and not by the guarded body.  **By the
letter of the bound it is outside clause (d).**

**But the carrier's own exemplar of a qualified condition is `if (X) -> if (X && writeflag ==
MEM_WRITE)` -- and `writeflag` is likewise an enclosing-function value, neither a dominating
predicate nor a body-read field.**  So the rule's own illustration falls outside the bound as
written.  That is the documented exemplar-vs-rule tension, and it decides whether a measured
clean sweep of this shape is an L2 floor breach (repair in-round) or coverage debt (file).

**The detector was repaired REGARDLESS** (`dec regs`, pass 14): the fix is one session and the
flood is guest-reachable on an ordinary path.  What is filed is the RULE, not the fix.

**Proposed reading, for adjudication, not adopted:** DEPENDS-ON includes every value the
enclosing function has computed or read BEFORE the guard executes -- which is what the
`writeflag` exemplar already assumes -- bounded still by the enclosing function.  The cost is a
wider (d) enumeration per fix; the benefit is that the bound stops excluding its own example.

### `tablebasenotfull` -- a kill-table driver that proceeds past a BASE below full score

**2026-09-03, second measured instance.**  Severity LOW (harness practice).

Pass 13 found the table-11 driver's negative control was a comment with no refusal behind it.
Pass 14's driver then measured **BASE 49/50** -- a real instrument defect in the frozen probe --
and proceeded through all nine remaining cells.  In this instance proceeding was RIGHT (one
known row, nine valid cells, and the canary had done its job), so the disposition is not
simply "die on BASE < full".

**What a driver should do, for adjudication:** say LOUDLY that BASE is not full and name the
rows; continue; and mark every subsequent cell's score as *read with N rows subtracted*.  A
`die` throws away valid cells; a `say` alone is the check-that-cannot-fail shape.  The middle
form -- announce, continue, annotate -- is what pass 14 did by hand and should be the driver's.

*** THE FROZEN-INSTRUMENT RULE IS WHY THIS WAS RECOVERABLE: the live probe was corrected while
the table ran, the table kept scoring its frozen copy, and the two never mixed. ***

### `pcc2c040kill` (HIGH) -- a LEGAL byte write to GENCTL ends the host

> *** [2026-11-02, records] FIXED by #512 (9fa07fe9, 2026-09-08; CHANGELOG.md:9457 at 987cb596). The text below is
> kept as the record of what was found. ***

**2026-09-03, surfaced by the `pcc2widthkills` pass-1 panel (fable5 and kimi, independently);
the panel found it while auditing the width fix and noted that "ten kills removed" would read as
"file clean" unless this one is cited.**

`dev_pcc2.c`, `reassert_interrupts()` (around `:189-195` [at 987cb596: `reassert_interrupts()` is `dev_pcc2.c:289` and the C040 test is `:390-397`, a latched decline since `#512` -- no `exit(` is left on that path]): if GENCTL has bit `0x04` set
(C040), the function does `fatal("pcc2: C040 interrupt assertions... TODO"); exit(1);`.  GENCTL
is written by the guest through its own arm at the LEGAL width (`ld.b`/`st.b`), and that arm
calls `reassert_interrupts()` on every write.  So **a single byte store of `0x04` to
`0xfff42002` ends the host** -- no width trick, no misalignment, an ordinary register write.

It was mentioned once in prose under `widthkillclass` as "a BADVAL reachable by a byte write"
with no row id, which is the same gap `pcc2defaultkill` closed for the offset kill.  Filed now
with an id so the width round's contract can point at it.

**ROW-DESIGN TRAP for the width round, recorded here because it is where a reader looks:**
every GENCTL lane value in a width-round row must keep bit `0x04` CLEAR, or a DELETE /
fall-through mutant trips THIS kill and the row dies for a reason not under test.

Witness owed (rung 3, one session): `st.b 0x04` to `0xfff42002` on the committed build ->
`exit1`.  Not yet run; the width round's witness is the template.

### `pcc2counter8` (MED) -- the counter/compare arm accepts an 8-byte write and raw-copies through neighbours

**2026-09-03, found by the codex seat on the `pcc2widthkills` pass-1 panel.**

The `T1CMP / T2CMP / T1COUNT / T2COUNT` arm does `memcpy(d->pcctwo_reg + relative_addr, data,
len)` for any `len` within `PCC2_SIZE`.  The hardware guide lists 8/16/32-bit cycles only.  An
8-byte write at `T2COUNT (0x10)` raw-copies through `PSCALE (0x14)`, `PSCALEADJ (0x15)`,
`T2CTL (0x16)` and `T1CTL (0x17)` -- bypassing the per-register write semantics those arms
implement (masks, read-modify-write, COVF clear, `reassert_interrupts`).  A guest can set timer
control bits through a path that skips their arm.

Not a host kill; a semantic bypass.  Deliberately NOT folded into the width round -- it is a
different defect (accepts too much, rather than kills) in a different arm.  Reachability: `st.d`
to `0x10` is 8-aligned, so it is guest-reachable by construction.


*2026-09-04 (Opus seat, pcc2widthkills pass 8): the labels above were swapped (the header says 0x16 = T2CTL,
0x17 = T1CTL); corrected in place.  And the path is GUEST-reachable: 0xfff42010 is 8-aligned, so a
guest `st.d` lands raw bytes on both timer-control registers -- the width detector's `rb t*ctl b27'
rows now use exactly this path to hold TxCTL bits 2-7 set, and say so.*
### `checkcunwired` -- check C (commit message vs diff) can never run from the hook that exists

**2026-09-03, found while retrying a blocked commit.**  Severity LOW (harness), but it is the
enforcer of mechanical rule 1 -- *write commit messages from the diff, never from intent* --
and it has been reporting `no commit-message file passed -- check C skipped, NOT passed` on
EVERY commit this session, as a soft WARN that nobody reads.

**The mechanism, verified by reading:** `precommit_check.sh` takes the message file as `$1`
(`MSGFILE=${1:-}` at :32) and only runs check C when it is present (:1137 [at 987cb596: `:1239`]).  The installed
`.git/hooks/pre-commit` calls `bash "$ROOT/tools/precommit_check.sh"` with NO argument.  A
pre-commit hook has no message to pass -- git has not collected it yet -- so from that hook
the check is unreachable BY CONSTRUCTION, not by omission.

**This is the check-that-cannot-fail shape with a twist: the check CAN fail, but the road to
it is never taken, and its "skipped" line is soft, so the commit proceeds.**  Passing a
message via `git commit -F <file>` does not help; the hook still does not forward it.

**What works today:** run `bash tools/precommit_check.sh <msgfile>` BY HAND before committing.
**The fix is a `commit-msg` hook** (which does receive the file as `$1`) invoking the same
script -- a harness change owing two negative controls (a message citing an untouched path
must FAIL; a message citing only touched paths must PASS).  Its own round.

### `pcc2widecompose` (LOW) -- per-lane composition of a wide PCC2 write, the faithful upgrade to DECLINE

**Filed 2026-09-03 -- and the round's own record had said "FILED" for hours before it was.**
The codex seat on `pcc2widthkills` pass 2 found the claim in the code comment and the
CHANGELOG with no entry anywhere.  A "filed" that names no row is a wrong record.

`pcc2widthkills` shipped writes as DECLINE + latch because every write arm uses `idata`,
which is the addressed byte only at `len == 1`, and eight arms have per-register semantics
(masks, read-modify-write, clears; seven of the twelve blocks call `reassert_interrupts()`).  The faithful
alternative the pass-1 panel named is COMPOSE: decompose a wide write into `len` byte
accesses, each dispatched through its own arm with its own semantics and side effects.

**Warrant in the tree:** `mvme_pcctworeg.h` says the registers accept 8/16/32-bit cycles;
the read side already composes lanes in address order; the counter arms already accept wide
writes by memcpy.  **Warrant against, measured by a seat:** `_guest-src-openbsd22/sys/arch/
mvme88k/dev/pcctworeg.h:8` declares these registers `volatile u_char`, and the driver code
uses byte accesses -- one real OS shows NO demand for wide writes to the byte registers.

**Hazard, named by the seat that proposed it:** COMPOSE must live INSIDE the byte-register
arms.  Applied before the switch it would route bytes +1..+3 of a legal word write to a
counter register through `default:`, a NEW kill on a working path.

**Reopen condition:** a measured guest (a driver trace, a PROM disassembly) that wide-writes
one of the twelve byte registers.  Until then DECLINE is the honest model and this is the
recorded upgrade path, not a defect.

### `pcc2pscaleflood` (MED) -- PSCALEADJ's write-side `fatal()` is unlatched and guest-drivable

**Filed 2026-09-03 by the Opus seat on `pcc2widthkills` pass 3, while verifying something
else.**  `dev_pcc2.c`'s PSCALEADJ write arm prints `[ pcc2: write to PSCALEADJ ignored (value
0x..) ]` on EVERY byte write.  Byte accesses skip the m88k alignment check, so `st.b` to
`0xfff42015` in a loop floods the log at any verbosity -- `fatal()` has no early-out, so `-q`
cannot silence it.  The round converted IPL's and MASK's `#119` latches to per-instance and
left this one alone.  `floodclass` family; the house idiom is a per-instance latch with an
explicit `(once)` marker.  Not this diff's business; filed.

### `pcc2assertflood` (LOW, floodclass) -- the interrupt (de)assert trace prints on every tick while a pcc2 interrupt is pending

**Filed 2026-09-03 while hand-verifying the `pend2 *' row shape for `pcc2widthkills` pass 6.**
`reassert_interrupts()` in `dev_pcc2.c` prints `[ pcc2: IPL = 1, MASK = 0 => ASSERT ]` each time
it runs with an unmasked interrupt pending -- and it runs from `DEVICE_TICK(pcc2)` every 2^14
instructions plus on every qualifying register access.  A guest that arms timer 2 (compare 1,
count 0, IEN, CEN) and spins saw six of these lines in a two-second free-run at quit; a guest
that leaves an interrupt pending indefinitely floods the log for as long as it runs.  The line
is printed by `debug()` (`dev_pcc2.c`, the `=> %s` line in `reassert_interrupts()`): verbosity-gated at
default settings, so it floods under `-v` and while single-stepping, where `debug()` prints -- a
narrower exposure than a `fatal()` flood, which is why this is LOW.  `floodclass` family; the house idiom is a per-instance latch with an
explicit `(once)` marker, or printing only on a CHANGE of the asserted state (the ASSERT/DEASSERT
edge), which is what the message's own wording suggests it was meant to be.  Not the width
round's business; filed.  Witness available: the `pend2 *' session in `regress/pcc2_width_probe.py`
reaches the state on unmodified `mvme88k -e mvme187`.

### `pcc2latchwidth48` (LOW, coverage debt) -- the latch-SET decision is pinned at width 2 only

**Filed 2026-09-03 from `pcc2widthkills` pass 6 (codex, from the pass-5 record).**  `rb2 *' proves
that a wide write arriving with the block's latch already SET is still refused, but only at
`len == 2` (`st.h` / `put h`).  The qualified-guard shape `&& !(d->warned & bit)' is
width-agnostic, so the len-2 rows kill it and its 4- and 8-byte repeats are coverage debt rather
than a floor cell -- a guard that consulted the latch only for len 4 or 8 (`&& !(len > 2 &&
(d->warned & bit))') would escape.  Eighteen sessions if closed at every storing block; a
plausible future edit is doubtful, so filed below the live defects in the same file
(`pcc2c040kill`, `pcc2counter8`, `pcc2pscaleflood`).  The contract in the probe discloses it.

### `pcc2iclrdec` (LOW, coverage debt) -- the TxICR interrupt-clear decrement is exercised by no row in the tree

**Filed 2026-09-04 by the kimi-k3:cloud substitute seat on `pcc2widthkills` pass 7 (packet-fed,
reasoning from the inlined TxICR arm).**  The arm's clear branch, `if (ICLR && (reg & INT) &&
pending_timer2_interrupts > 0) pending_timer2_interrupts--;` (and the timer-1 twin), runs only for
a BYTE write carrying ICLR while an interrupt is pending -- and the width detector's `pend* *`
rows hold that state only at WIDE writes, which the guard declines before the body runs.  So `>
0` -> `>= 0`, or `--` -> `++`, inside either branch is unobserved by every row in the tree: the
count goes to -1 (or 2) while INT is cleared, and nothing reads it afterwards.  Outside the width
round's clause-(d) closure (the branch does not dominate the diff's edited lines; it is
pre-existing body logic), so filed rather than repaired there.  A row is cheap now that the
free-running shape exists: arm timer 2, poll to INT, `st.b` ICLR|IEN|IL1 (0x19) to T2ICR, then
observe that a second poll never sees INT again (pending consumed) -- and its twin with a
SECOND fired interrupt to distinguish `--` from `= 0`.  Belongs to a timer-semantics round, not
to this one.

## 2026-09-06 — `83df95c` pass 2: the review that commit never got, and what it found

**`wdcconsumedattempts` (MEDIUM).**  In `dev_wdc.c`'s ATAPI accounting arm,
`int consumed = len == 4 ? 4 : (len >= 2 ? 2 : 1);` is computed **from `len` alone** — it counts the helper
CALLS the arm makes, not the pops that succeeded.  `wdc_get_inbuf()` returns `(uint64_t) -1` on an empty ring
and returns **before advancing the tail** (verified by reading: the early return sits three lines above the
advance), so with `q` bytes queued a width-`w` access pops `min(q, calls)`.  When the ring under-runs
mid-access, `consumed` over-counts and `atapi_len` is decremented by more than the guest received.

*** That is the exact defect `#341` exists to fix, quoted three lines above the expression: *"the count
reported has to be the count that happened."* ***  `#341` replaced `len` with this expression, which is right
whenever the ring holds enough bytes and wrong in precisely the residual case the same round was reasoning
about.  **DERIVED, NOT MEASURED** — no witness shows a guest reaching an under-run mid-access on the ATAPI
path, and the over-read is already announced by the `warned_inbuf_overread` latch, so the silent-corruption
claim is unproven.  A round owes the rung-3 attempt.  *Worse observable, unanalysed: the arm accumulates with
`odata += (wdc_get_inbuf(d) << 8)`, so a failed pop folds the sentinel's bits into the value the guest reads,
not only into the count.*

**Corrected in place (L4), product comment.**  The census shipped by `83df95c` stated the eight pop counts
unconditionally; they are **call counts** and hold only while bytes remain.  Now qualified, with the mechanism
and the `consumed` caveat named.  *Two seats derived the same expression and neither noticed it counts
attempts — the seat that went to the helper found it.*

**And a nuance that makes the original round's claim weaker, from the kimi seat:** the wording `83df95c`
replaced — *"a 3- or 8-byte access consumes 1 or 2"* — was **vague, not false**.  The true value is 2, and 2 is
a member of the set `{1, 2}`.  So the shipped trailing note reads as a correction of a falsehood when it is
really the sharpening of an imprecise sentence.

**Claim settled that nobody else could reach:** the ring predicate after `#484` **holds** — `N = 512*513`, the
`(head+1)%N == tail` guard refuses the store, both producers respect it, occupancy stays in `0..N-1`, so full
and empty are distinguishable and `head == tail` means empty.  **No detector row depends on the old wording**,
checked across all four files the commit touched.

## 2026-09-06 — filed from the Codex passes (five briefs, five substantive answers)

**`irqassertedunread` (LOW — filed HIGH off one grep, de-escalated the same hour by the pass it was filed
pending).**  Six CPU families set `cpu->cd.<arch>.irq_asserted`; exactly three are consumed (arm, m88k, ppc).
**alpha, i960 and riscv have no reader anywhere**, and there is no alternate delivery mechanism.  But the three
are not alike: **i960 and riscv are DEAD SCAFFOLDING** — neither executes a second instruction (i960's switch is
only `default: goto bad;`; riscv implements compressed NOP/ADDI and sends the 32-bit branch to `bad`) — so there
is no guest to miss an interrupt and the disposition is scaffold cleanup.  **alpha is a genuine hole at the
CPU/PAL level**: `kentry` is stored with no reader and `PAL_OSF1_rti` is named but unimplemented, so removing
`lcabadval`'s two interrupt exits leaves *both* forwarding and delivery unfinished.  *Corrected my census:
`cpu_dyntrans.c` also delivers MIPS and SH interrupts through differently-named state, invisible to a
single-identifier grep — the correlate-not-the-class shape.*  Source-derived, no guest boot run.

breach — the bit-trick does not *read* like the same check, and every single-token weakening of that bound is
rowed and dies.  **Closure is one `-n 3` session and closes the whole family**; check first that `-n 3` boots the
committed rig.

## 2026-09-07 — three rows filed from the `#504` triage pass

**`sgirebufuninit` (HIGH — `dev_sgi_re.c`: `uint8_t buf[8]` is never initialised, and the guest picks how
many of its bytes are used).**  `horrible_getputpixel()` declares the buffer with no initialiser and no
`memset`.  Two independent fields of ONE guest-written mode word decide how much of it is used —
`color_mode = mode & DE_MODE_TYPE_MASK` (bits 4-7) says how many bytes an arm FILLS, and
`bufdepth = 1 << ((mode >> 8) & 3)` (bits 8-9) says how many are TRANSFERRED — and **nothing anywhere makes
them agree**; `grep -rn '>> *8) *& *3' src/devices/` finds the decode, its own `#100` comment and the two
XFER siblings, and no guard.  Two reachable paths in opposite directions: a **PUT** writes bytes no colour
arm assigns into guest-visible memory, and a **GET** builds a 32-bit colour out of bytes the read never
filled, which `draw_primitive()` then stores.

*** THE PROVENANCE IS THE SHARPEST PART: `#95` WAS THIS FORK'S "central uninit-leak fix" CLAIMING TO CLOSE
*THE WHOLE CLASS*, AND `#100` IN THE SAME BATCH EDITED THIS EXACT ARRAY. ***  `#100` grew it `buf[4]`→`buf[8]`
because the guest can demand 8 bytes — fixing a stack OVERFLOW — and never asked what fills the bytes it had
just added.  `#95` zeroes device **READ** buffers for `len` bytes, so it cannot reach a `MEM_WRITE` and cannot
reach bytes past `len`.

**PASS 1 CORRECTED MY OWN FRAMING, AND THE CORRECTION MADE IT WORSE.**  The brief drove the PUT path with mode
`0x1320` (depth field 3).  The grok seat objected that the header documents only `DE_MODE_BUFDEPTH_8/16/32`
and **field 3 is undocumented** — verified against `crmfbreg.h` before being accepted — so my vehicle was the
weak one, while `DE_MODE_TYPE_CI` (colour type **zero**, the reset value) assigns only `buf[0]` and
`BUFDEPTH_32` transfers four, making **`0x1200` a fully documented leak of `buf[1..3]`**.  The same seat
settled the question the brief had left open: **the destination is RAM, not a device**, so `#95`'s pre-zero
does not run *at all* on either path.  Severity is under active adjudication — grok argues MEDIUM, and that
call is held until the full roster lands rather than taken from one seat.

**`sgiwidthwiredobl` (LOW — `sgi_re_width_probe.py`'s contract states an obligation that was discharged in the
commit that wrote it).**  Its `other decl` contract closes *"…which MUST BE GATE-WIRED — unwired, that coverage
exists nowhere."*  Measured: it **is** wired, by `9f666a8`, **the same commit**; `gate_arm.sh` runs the probe,
its row list checks all three named rows by name, and the block reports 50 rows emitted, 50 green, 0 red.  So a
reader concludes coverage exists nowhere when it is wired and passing.  That is the carrier's
present-tense-description class, and it is worse than an ordinary stale line because it reads as an
**outstanding obligation** — a future round could redo finished work.  Repair is to DEMOTE it in place, since
the reasoning (unwired coverage exists nowhere) is exactly why the wiring was done.  **Deliberately not fixed
on the spot: the gate was running and about to execute that probe, and Python reads a script whole at startup,
so an edit between runs hands two runs different instruments** — a records-only change would have been
invisible in the diff and visible in the measurement, which is the worst combination.

**`codexsubjectrefusal` (LOW — a codex content-filter refusal survived neutralisation, and the trigger is not
what it first appeared).**  Filed earlier in this session and recorded here so the queue and the ledger agree.
The first diagnosis — that the refusal keyed on the SUBJECT — was wrong; re-testing showed **design briefs are
answered while witness briefs are refused**, so the trigger is the reach-the-defect FRAMING rather than the

## 2026-09-07 — two new defects from the `sgirebufuninit` pass-1 panel, both found by the codex seat on a brief about something else

Both arrived under the standing *"if, while verifying a claim, you found something ELSE — say so"* licence, and
both were **verified at HEAD before filing**.  The seat's verdict was **GO-WITH-CHANGES**, and it sits at the
END of a 317 KB answer, which is why the extractor scored it a format miss — *a seat with no verdict line gets
its body read, and this is the third time that has paid.*

**`sgirergbroundtrip` (MED — the RGB colour arms are off by one byte position).**  The two arms disagree about
which byte holds which channel:

    PUT  case DE_MODE_TYPE_RGB:   buf[0] = *color >> 24;  buf[1] = *color >> 16;
                                  buf[2] = *color >> 8;   buf[3] = 0;
    GET  case DE_MODE_TYPE_RGB:   *color = (buf[1] << 24) + (buf[2] << 16) + (buf[3] << 8);

PUT stores the top three bytes at indices **0,1,2**; GET recombines from **1,2,3**.  Storing `0x11223300` gives
bytes `11 22 33 00`, which GET reads back as **`0x22330000`** — a round trip through the model's own RGB mode
does not return what was written.

*** WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THE BUG: EVERY ANALYSIS THIS WEEK, MINE INCLUDED, CALLED THE FOUR IMPLEMENTED COLOUR
ARMS "CORRECT" AND SUSPECTED ONLY THE `default:` ARMS. ***  The `sgirebufuninit` brief says it outright —
*"NO colour arm writes `buf[4..7]` — not one of the five, including the four CORRECT ones"*.  codex:
*"Calling all implemented color arms 'correct' is unwarranted."*  The phrase had been repeated unchecked across
three documents.  **Which side is wrong is deliberately NOT decided here**: RGBA is symmetric 0–3 on both
sides and ABGR is reversed on both, so RGB is the lone asymmetric pair — but whether the hardware packs RGB at
the low or high three bytes is a datasheet question, and a round taking this owes that reference or a real
framebuffer comparison.

**`sgimtedepth4dead` (LOW — `do_mte_transfer()`'s `if (depth == 4)` can never be true).**
`depth = 8 << ((mode & MTE_MODE_DEPTH_MASK) >> MTE_DEPTH_SHIFT)`, with mask `0x00000300` and shift 8 — a
two-bit field, so `depth` is only ever **8, 16, 32 or 64**.  The guarded block is dead code.  codex reads the
dead block as the intended RGBA construction, leaving *"its helper calls retain CI"*; **that half is not
verified here** and is what a round would have to establish.  *** IT ALSO REFUTES A PREMISE OF
`sgirebufuninit`: that brief asks whether callers constrain the (colour type, depth) pair, and this is a caller
that TRIES to and FAILS SILENTLY. ***  LOW because a dead branch corrupts nothing by itself; the severity lives
in the missing construction, which is unestablished.

**And a correction to `sgirebufuninit`'s own scope claim, from the same seat.**  Its class scan reported six
unpinned-length and five stack-buffer-write sites and concluded `dev_sgi_re.c` is the class's only member.
Codex found **four write sites both scanners missed** — `dev_dec21143.c` descriptor writebacks (nested argument
commas defeat the comma-splitting, which the brief *had* disclosed as a limit) and `dev_dreamcast_maple.c`
response writes (casts prevent recognition of the buffer argument, which it had **not**).  All four are safe,
**so the conclusion survives and the denominator does not** — different claims, which the brief conflated.
The sharp part is methodological: *"Agreement between scanners sharing parsing limitations is not exhaustive
corroboration."*  Both scanners split arguments with the same regex, so **they are one deriver run twice** —
the identical lesson this project already paid for on the `sgirekills` count, where two agreeing greps both
counted comment lines.

**`m88kexcdetectorl2` (HIGH — four `implemented = true` sites sit on exception classes the 59-row detector
never drives).**  Predicted independently by **two** seats, on **two different mutants**, neither of which

* **the `kimi-k3:cloud` substitute** — *"a one-line deletion of `implemented = true;` on an unprobed exception
  class re-opens `#502` exactly, and every probe row named in this packet stays green."*

**Kimi's is the cheaper mutant AND the harder to dismiss**, because its premise is checkable by reading — no

    implemented = true sites          11   (not the 7 the round's narrative implies)
      RESET                 line 700   <-- the probe drives no such row
      INTERRUPT             line 705   <-- the probe drives no such row
      INSTRUCTION_ACCESS    line 710   <-- the probe drives no such row
      DATA_ACCESS           line 715   <-- the probe drives no such row
      the seven fixed arms  720-750, ALL probed

The probe's 59 rows drive bounds / div0 / error / misalign / ovf / priv / unimpl / sfu1 and the trap family.

*Worth recording about the seat rather than the bug: a PACKET-FED transport that can read neither the probe nor

**`sgigbeconvover` (LOW — `dev_sgi_gbe.c`'s tile-line conversion loop runs past what was read).**  Raised by
the codex seat as a narrowing of one of my own SAFE verdicts in the `sgirebufuninit` class scan, and verified:

    cpu->memory_rw(..., buf, len, MEM_READ, ...);      /* fills len bytes   */
    for (int i = 0; i < 512; i += bytes_per_pixel)     /* reads 512 -- not len */

`len < 512` is reachable on the last tile column (`partial_pixels * bytes_per_pixel`), so up to 511
uninitialised bytes are fed through `get_rgb()`.  **Scope kept to what is demonstrable, matching the seat's own
hedge:** only `fb_len = (len / bytes_per_pixel) * 3` bytes are forwarded, so the pixels built from the
uninitialised tail are **computed and discarded** — undefined behaviour and an ASAN-class defect, *not* a guest
disclosure.  The fix is one token, `i < len`.

*The neighbouring OB-14 clamp shows someone already reasoned about this loop's bounds once — and bounded the
READ while leaving the CONSUMPTION at a literal.  That is the third instance tonight of a round bounding one
side of a length relationship and not the other; `#100` grew `buf[4]`→`buf[8]` without asking what fills the
new bytes, and `#95` zeroed device reads for `len` without covering writes or the bytes past `len`.*
