### `ubsanshiftlane` (med) -- filed 2026-09-07: a UBSAN differential would pin the shift repairs a
### value probe provably cannot

`#510`'s pass 2 (grok) showed two one-line regressions that re-open real undefined behaviour and
score FULL MARKS on a 12-row guest-value probe:

    `1U' -> `1' in the mask ternary                     re-opens C99 6.5.7p4 at width 31
    restore `topBitMask = 1 << (width-1)' above the if  re-opens the second UB

**Neither is killable by any row, and the reason is structural rather than a gap in the row set:**
both are DEFINEDNESS repairs, and definedness has no guest-visible value on a non-trapping host.
`1 << 31` and `1U << 31` yield the same mask after the `- 1`; and with a correct 32-bit mask
`x |= ~mask` is `x |= 0`, so `s w32` pins the MASK and not `topBitMask`.

**BUT UBSAN IS ALREADY IN THIS TREE**, which I established after writing "unchecked" about it:

    build-asan/Makefile      -fsanitize=address,undefined
    build-asan/src/Makefile  -fsanitize=address,undefined
    regress/gate_asan_sweep.sh   exists

**THE SHAPE, and it is a differential rather than a row:**

    build-asan/gxemul + FIXED source     -> expect NO shift diagnostic
    build-asan/gxemul + `1U'->`1' mutant -> expect "shift exponent" / "left shift of" on stderr

That is the two-direction control this project demands, and it converts a DISCLOSED escape into a
COVERED one for a whole class -- `lcashiftub`, `sgirebufshiftub`, `m88k_rot:513`,
`cpu_mips_instr.c:1757` and the two `is_userpage` sites are all the same species, and all of them
are equally invisible to a value oracle.

**WHY IT IS NOT BOLTED ONTO `#510`:** it is a NEW MEASUREMENT LANE -- a second binary, and a
STDERR oracle instead of a value oracle -- and `#510`'s pass 2 has already run. A lane added after
a pass is a lane nobody reviewed. It owes its own round, its own pass, and two negative controls.

*Cost note, because it is the reason to want this: the shift-UB class now stands at EIGHT sites
across three CPUs, and a value probe can see NONE of them directly. It sees only the consequences
that happen to differ on this host's lowering -- which for width 32 was a wrong register value,
and for width 31 was nothing at all.*


### `ledgersevmissing` (WITHDRAWN 2026-09-07, same day) -- DUPLICATE of `queueunrated`
###
### *** Filed and withdrawn within the hour.  `queueunrated` was already open with the same
### finding, sharper numbers (73 rows UNRATED **and already witnessed**) and a better
### diagnosis -- that a keyword scan over titles is a CORRELATE, since what makes a row high
### is reachability and no keyword tests that.  The one thing this added -- that rows are
### STILL being created without a rating, so the writer-side check must land BEFORE the
### backfill -- is folded into `queueunrated`.  Kept as a heading rather than deleted so the
### record shows the duplicate was made, not that it never existed. ***

FILED 2026-09-07 by the main loop, from a survey run while picking the next round -- NOT from a
seat.  Found by trying to sort the open queue by severity and having the sort DIE on a KeyError.

**THE NUMBERS, DERIVED (re-run the deriver; do not quote these):**

    C:/.../python.exe -c "import json,io; L=json.load(io.open('tools/pipeline/ledger.json',encoding='utf-8'));
      rows=L['rows']; m=[r['id'] for r in rows if 'sev' not in r];
      print(len(rows), len(m), len([i for i in m if next(x for x in rows if x['id']==i)['state'] in ('open','in work')]))"

On the day of filing that printed **410 rows, 261 with no `sev` field at all, 78 of them open or in
work** -- against 62 low + 54 med + 11 high that DO carry one.  So the severity-bearing population
is a MINORITY of the live queue.

**WHY IT MATTERS, and it is not tidiness.**  Every triage this project runs -- "what is the next
round", "what are the critical bugs", the owner's own standing instruction to *prioritise critical
bugs and easy ones* -- is a severity sort.  A row with no `sev` is not sorted LAST; depending on
the tool it is **omitted entirely or crashes the sort**.  Both were observed on the day of filing.
That is the seat-failure-counted-as-agreement shape moved into triage: the row does not appear as
low-priority, it does not appear at all, so nothing ever says it was skipped.

**AND IT IS NOT A UNIFORM LEGACY BLOCK, which is what makes it worth a row rather than a sweep.**
The missing set spans the whole history -- `d1`/`a4`/`n1`..`n6` from the earliest rounds, but also
`wdcdataoutdrain`, `gdromlatchcross`, `divratchetband` and other rows opened in the last fortnight.
So it is not "old rows used an old schema"; **rows are STILL being created without it today**,
which means a one-off backfill fixes the past and not the cause.

The same survey found `witness` missing on a smaller set and `opened` missing on a large one; those
are recorded here but are NOT the same severity, because nothing sorts on them.

**DELIBERATELY NOT FIXED IN THE ROUND THAT FOUND IT.**  Assigning a severity to 78 rows is a
judgment call per row, not a mechanical default -- and defaulting them all to `med` would be worse
than the gap, because it would make 78 unassessed rows indistinguishable from assessed ones.  That
is this project's oldest rule about blanks: an unrun check and an inapplicable one must not render
the same.

**THE SHAPE OF A FIX, for whoever takes it:** (1) a writer-side check, the `check_cited_artifacts`
idiom -- forward-only from a cutoff, so a NEW row without `sev` fails and the 78 legacy ones warn;
(2) the backfill as its own pass, severity by severity, with the unassessable ones marked
explicitly rather than guessed.  (1) before (2), because (1) stops the bleeding and (2) without it
just refills.

*Not escalated to high: no measured decision has yet been lost to it -- the rows I have picked this
week came from OUTSTANDING_BUGS's dated tail and from panel residuals, not from a severity sort.
But that is luck about my habits, not a property of the ledger.*


### `refilingclass` (med) -- filed 2026-09-07: five already-recorded findings re-derived in one
### session, one of them filed as a duplicate row

FILED 2026-09-07 by the main loop, about the main loop.  **FIVE instances in ONE session**, every one
of them work that was already recorded, and I found none of them by checking -- I found them by
accidentally tripping over the record afterwards.

    1  "twelve of sixteen colour encodings reach the random arm"   already in a COMMITTED artifact,
                                                                   regress/artifacts/sgirandomcolour/
                                                                   codex_design_20260907.txt, with a full table
    2  "depth 8 transmits uninitialised stack bytes"               already in codex_pass1_20260907.txt AND
                                                                   already an open row, [[sgirebufuninit]]
    3  "`lin_b diag once' does not assert the (once) marker"       already an open row, [[randompixdiagonce]]
    4  "half the queue carries no severity"                        already an open row, [[queueunrated]] --
                                                                   and I FILED A DUPLICATE, [[ledgersevmissing]],
                                                                   into the ledger AND OUTSTANDING_BUGS before
                                                                   noticing.  Withdrawn same day.
    5  "the GET half consumes more bytes than it reads"            already in [[sgirebufuninit]]'s own note,
                                                                   almost verbatim

**THIS IS THE UNREAD-REVIEW CLASS, BUT NOT THE VERSION THE CARRIER DESCRIBES.**  That class is about
PANEL ANSWERS NOBODY OPENED -- a seat file sitting in a panel dir.  Every instance here is different and
worse: the knowledge was in **committed files** and **open queue rows**, i.e. in the two places this
project treats as its own memory.  Instance 4 is the sharpest, because the duplicate row PASSED THE
PRECOMMIT GATE and would have sat in the queue indefinitely as a second entry for one defect.

**THE COST IS NOT ONLY TIME.**  Instance 1 and 2 consumed a codex invocation on questions a committed
artifact had already answered -- against a standing directive to spend codex on the queue.  And a
duplicate row inflates the backlog the owner is trying to prioritise, which is the opposite of what
[[queueunrated]] is for.

*** WHAT MAKES IT A CLASS RATHER THAN CARELESSNESS: THE INVESTIGATION IS WHAT HIDES THE RECORD. ***
In every instance I reached the finding by READING SOURCE, and a source reading gives no signal that a
row exists.  The record lives under a row id I would only search for if I already suspected the answer.
Instance 3 is the clean demonstration: I derived the `(once)` gap from the probe, wrote it up as new,
and the row `randompixdiagonce` had been filed EARLIER THE SAME DAY under a name I would never have
guessed from the code.

**PROPOSED STRUCTURAL FIX, and it is deliberately two things because they catch different halves:**

* **(a) WRITER-SIDE, mechanical -- a duplicate check on ADDED ledger rows.**  When a commit adds a row,
  compare its title's content words against every open/in-work row's title and REPORT the nearest
  matches for a human to dismiss.  It cannot auto-reject (titles are prose and near-misses are real
  rows), so it warns; the value is that it fires at the moment of filing.  Forward-only from a cutoff,
  the `check_cited_artifacts` idiom.  **Owes two negative controls -- a genuine near-miss pair must NOT
  be reported as a duplicate, and an actual duplicate MUST be -- so it ships as its own harness round,
  not as a rider.**
* **(b) READER-SIDE, a habit with a command -- before investigating a device or a probe, list what is
  already open against that FILE.**  This is the half that would have caught instances 1, 2 and 5,
  which were never going to be caught at filing time because I never filed them.  The command is one
  line and the artifacts directory is the other half of it:

      grep -l "<file>" regress/artifacts/*/*.txt
      python -c "...print rows whose title or note names <file>..."

**HONEST LIMIT: (b) IS PROSE, AND THIS FILE'S OWN FINDING IS THAT PROSE DOES NOT FIRE.**  I am not
claiming it will.  It is recorded because (a) genuinely cannot catch instances 1, 2 and 5 -- there is no
filing event to hook -- and saying "no structure reaches this half" is more useful than pretending a
habit is a control.  If a later session finds a mechanical trigger for the reader side, that supersedes
this.

*Severity med, not high: nothing shipped wrong.  Every instance was caught, four of them within the
hour, and the one that reached the ledger was withdrawn the same day.  The cost is wasted effort and an
inflated backlog, not a defect in the emulator.*


### `lcaconfbus1kill` (high) -- filed 2026-09-07: an ACCEPTED write to LCA_IOC_CONF arms a
### host kill in a different function

FILED 2026-09-07.  Surfaced while verifying a claim in the grok seat's `lcabadval` pass-1 BODY (its
verdict line did not carry it) -- and **verified to be sharper than the seat stated it**, by opening
both functions.

**THE DEFECT: an ACCEPTED write to one register arms a host kill in a DIFFERENT function.**

`DEVICE_ACCESS(lca_ioc)`, `case LCA_IOC_CONF`:

    d->ioc_conf = idata;
    /*  Only bit 0 is implemented so far, the PCI bus 0 vs
        bus non-0 selection bit.  */
    if (idata & ~1) {
            fatal("TODO: Write to unimplemented bit of IOC_CONF: 0x%" PRIx64 "\n", ...);
            exit(1);
    }

**`0x1` PASSES that guard.**  `idata & ~1` is 0, so the write is accepted, stored, and the arm's own
comment describes bit 0 as the implemented selector.

`DEVICE_ACCESS(lca_pci_conf)` then consumes it:

    bus = d->ioc_conf & 1;
    if (bus == 0) {
            for (dev=0; dev<21; dev++)
                    if (tag & (0x800 << dev))
                            break;
            if (dev >= 21) {
                    /*  fatal("[ LCA: No bus 0 device? TODO ]\n");
                    exit(1);  */
                    dev = 0;
            }
    } else {
            fatal("TODO. Non-zero bus.\n");
            exit(1);
    }

So: **guest writes 1 to IOC_CONF (accepted), then performs any PCI configuration-space access, and
the host process exits.**  Two guest accesses, both to registers the model implements, neither of
them rejected.

*** WHY IT IS ITS OWN ROW AND NOT PART OF [[lcabadval]]. ***  Every kill `lcabadval` covers is a
guard REFUSING a value it does not recognise.  **This one fires on a value the guard ACCEPTS**, in a
different function, on a later access.  The acceptance and the kill are separated in both code and
time, which is why a per-arm audit of `lca_ioc` walks straight past it -- as mine did, twice.

*** AND THE SEAT'S FRAMING NEEDED CORRECTING, WHICH IS THE PART WORTH RECORDING. ***  grok wrote
that this exit becomes *"newly reachable from a CONF extra-bit write that also sets bit 0; today
that write dies in the CONF guard first."*  That is true of an EXTRA-BIT write (e.g. `0x3`), and it
made the kill sound like a CONSEQUENCE of adopting option A.  **It is not: `0x1` alone reaches it
today, with no fix applied.**  A widens which CONF values arrive here; it does not open the door.
The door is open now.  *Checked by reading both arms rather than by accepting the seat's sentence --
which is this project's own rule, and the seat was right about the site while being wrong about the
timing.*

**THE IRONY, and it is a design signal rather than a joke:** the `bus == 0` branch is the file's own
graceful-degradation PRECEDENT -- a commented-out `fatal()`/`exit(1)` with `dev = 0;` substituted --
and [[lcabadval]] cites that very loop as a transferable in-tree warrant.  **The `else` five lines
below it is a bare kill.**  Same function, opposite dispositions, no comment explaining why.

**REACHABILITY, stated honestly rather than assumed.**  Bit 0 is a bus SELECTOR, so a guest reaches
this by selecting a bus the model does not implement and then doing config access -- plausible for
firmware or an OS that probes beyond bus 0, and trivially reachable by a probe.  **Whether any
shipped guest on `alphabook1` actually does it is NOT established here**, and the row does not claim
it.  What is established is that no guard stands between an accepted write and the kill.

**WITNESS: a rung-3 probe is available and most of it already exists.**  `device_add(machine, "lca")`
is `ST_ALPHABOOK1` ONLY (`machine_alpha.c`), and `regress/lca_confwidth_probe.py` ALREADY drives a
guest `stq`/`ldq` at `LCA_IOC_CONF` (`0xfffffc0180000020`, K0SEG | physical) on unmodified
`alphabook1`.  This row needs one more session: `stq 0x1` to CONF, then a PCI config-space access.
**Three traps that probe already paid for:** debugger `dump` skips `DM_DEFAULT` handlers; a debugger
`put d` of a killing value IS a host kill but is NOT a guest instruction, so it does not witness; and
HAE at window offset 0 silently succeeds, so a miss control must not use `LCA_IOC_BASE+0`.

**DISPOSITION, not yet adjudicated:** it is the same de-fatalisation family, but the option set
differs because the kill is not a value refusal -- the honest members here are DECLINE THE CONFIG
ACCESS (return without dispatching, with a latched announce) or IMPLEMENT bus != 0.  **Note the
architecturally correct error path is blocked for the same reason grok gave on the sibling row:
`LCA_IOC_STAT0`/`STAT1` have no case at all and hit the `default:` arm's `exit(1)`, so LCA cannot
report a device error through the register the header designates for it.**

sev HIGH: a guest-drivable host kill, reached by two ordinary accesses with no rejected value
anywhere on the path.


### `lcairqstubkill` (high) -- filed 2026-09-07: the LCA interrupt handlers are
### `fatal()+exit(1)` with no guard, and DEVINIT wires the ISA/IDE bus straight to them

FILED 2026-09-07.  **NOT a new discovery of the SITE** -- [[lcabadval]]'s eleven-kill census already
enumerated `:73` and `:85` and called them *"plausibly the most severe of the eleven"*.  What was
missing is a ROW: the census names them inside a row titled for VALUE GUARDS, which is the census's
own closing lesson (*a row named after one class hides the members of the others*), and
`OUTSTANDING_BUGS.md` mentioned them **zero** times.

**THE SITE, verbatim -- there is no predicate at all:**

    void lca_interrupt_assert(struct interrupt *interrupt)
    {
            fatal("lca_interrupt_assert: TODO\n");
            exit(1);
    }

    void lca_interrupt_deassert(struct interrupt *interrupt)
    {
            fatal("lca_interrupt_deassert: TODO\n");
            exit(1);
    }

*** THE WIRING, DERIVED BY READING `DEVINIT(lca)` -- AND IT IS WHAT MAKES THIS SEVERE. ***

    memset(&interrupt_template, 0, sizeof(interrupt_template));
    interrupt_template.line = 0;
    interrupt_template.name = interrupt_path;                        /*  "<machine>.lca"  */
    interrupt_template.extra = d;
    interrupt_template.interrupt_assert   = lca_interrupt_assert;
    interrupt_template.interrupt_deassert = lca_interrupt_deassert;
    interrupt_handler_register(&interrupt_template);

    bus_isa_init(devinit->machine, interrupt_path,
        BUS_ISA_IDE0 | BUS_ISA_IDE1, LCA_ISA_BASE, LCA_ISA_MEMBASE);

**The stubs are registered as the handlers for `<machine>.lca`, and `bus_isa_init` is handed THAT
SAME PATH together with `BUS_ISA_IDE0 | BUS_ISA_IDE1`.**  So the ISA bus -- both IDE controllers
included -- routes its interrupts into a function whose entire body is `fatal()` + `exit(1)`.  The
file's own comment above the stub says *"Line 0 = ISA interrupt."*

**WHY IT IS PLAUSIBLY THE WORST KILL IN THE FILE.**  Every other terminating call in `dev_lca.c`
needs a guest to write a value the model does not expect.  **This one needs only that an interrupt
is asserted** -- i.e. ordinary disk activity on a machine whose DEVINIT attaches two IDE channels.
No unusual value, no undocumented register, no firmware revision.

*** WHAT IS ESTABLISHED AND WHAT IS NOT -- read this before quoting the row. ***
* **ESTABLISHED, by reading:** the stubs terminate unconditionally; they are registered as the
  interrupt handlers; `bus_isa_init` receives the same interrupt path with both IDE channels.
* **NOT ESTABLISHED:** that any guest actually reaches them.  **No measurement has been made.**  A
  device could conceivably never assert on this path, and `interrupt_handler_register` semantics
  have not been read here.  The row does NOT claim "alphabook1 cannot boot"; it claims the wiring
  is present and the handler is a kill.

**NEXT STEP IS A RUNG-3 ATTEMPT, and the apparatus already exists.**
`regress/lca_confbus_probe.py` (shipped 2026-09-07 for [[lcaconfbus1kill]]) already boots
unmodified `alphabook1` under the debugger with a disk image attached and drives guest `ldq`/`stq`
through real decode.  The question is whether a guest access can make an IDE channel assert while
single-stepping -- **and the carrier's rule cuts against it: a step-based probe sees a SYNCHRONOUS
assert (a device handler reached inside the guest's own store) but NOT one that depends on a
host-timer callback.**  So the honest first question is *what produces the assert*, and if the
answer is `timer_add`, this needs a free-running probe rather than a stepped one.

**DISPOSITION: option-set MEMBER 7 (IMPLEMENT), and the set's other members do not apply.**  There
is no value being refused and nothing to decline, accept, mask or fault -- it is an entire path
stubbed out.  The carrier added member 7 on 2026-09-06 from this very file, using these very
functions as its example.  A cheaper interim is member 3 (decline + LATCHED announce): return
without asserting, announce once, and let the guest see a missing interrupt rather than a dead host
-- **but that trades a host kill for a silently lost interrupt**, which is the readback-lie shape
[[lcabadval]] is currently held on, so it is a design question and not an obvious win.

**TRANSFERABLE PRECEDENT, already closed in this tree:** [[lunaabsentcpu]] -- *"dev_luna88k.c
reassert_interrupts() calls the NULL interrupt callback of an UNCONFIGURED cpu slot"* -- same family
(a terminating/absent interrupt callback reached by ordinary operation), fixed, and closed with a
rung-3 probe witness (`regress/luna_absentcpu_probe.py`).  Read that round before designing this one.

sev HIGH on the wiring; it would be CRITICAL if a witness lands, and the row says so rather than
pre-judging it.


### `uninorthdevscan` (med, pending a reachability answer) -- filed 2026-09-07:
### a sign-extended mask can select the wrong PCI device on macppc

FILED 2026-09-07, split out of [[shiftubcensus]] item (A) because it is the only member of that
census with a **GUEST-VISIBLE CONSEQUENCE** rather than a language-level one, and it therefore owes a
witness the others do not.

**THE SITE**, `dev_uninorth.c`, in the PCI address-register write path:

    :56    uint64_t idata = memory_readmax64(cpu, data, len | MEM_PCI_LITTLE_ENDIAN);
    ...
    :60    d->cur_addr = idata;
    :70    for (dev=11; dev<32; dev++)
    :71        if (idata & (1 << dev))
    :72            break;

**`idata` is `uint64_t` and `1 << dev` is an `int`.**  At `dev == 31` that is `0x80000000`, which as
a signed `int` is NEGATIVE, so converting it for the `&` against a `uint64_t` **SIGN-EXTENDS it to
`0xffffffff80000000`**.

> **CONSEQUENCE IF `idata` CARRIES ANY BIT IN 32..63: the loop matches at `dev == 31` when no
> device bit is set there, and the scan selects the WRONG DEVICE.**  The repair (`1U << dev`) is
> therefore NOT behaviour-preserving here -- unlike its sibling in `dev_v3.c`, where the operand's
> high bits are provably zero and the same edit changes nothing.

**REACHABLE AS A DEVICE:** `machine_macppc.c:68` calls
`dev_uninorth_init(machine, machine->memory, 0xe2000000, ...)`, and `dev_uninorth.c:141` registers
`"uninorth_pci_addr"` at `addr + 0x800000` = **0xe2800000**.  macppc is a supported machine here.

*** WHAT IS NOT ESTABLISHED, AND IT IS THE WHOLE QUESTION: CAN `idata` ACTUALLY CARRY BITS 32..63? ***
`memory_readmax64(cpu, data, len | MEM_PCI_LITTLE_ENDIAN)` returns a value whose width follows the
ACCESS WIDTH.  On a 4-byte store -- the ordinary way a guest writes a PCI config address -- the
result cannot exceed 32 bits, the sign-extended ones meet only zeros, and **nothing observable
happens**.  The defect needs an **8-byte** access to that register.

**So the row is HELD at the reachability question, not at the arithmetic.**  A codex analysis is out
on exactly this (`regress/artifacts/shiftubcensus/UNINORTH_brief.md`), asking: what does
`memory_readmax64` return per width; what widths reach this handler on macppc; and -- the premise I
am least sure of -- whether `MEM_PCI_LITTLE_ENDIAN`, which is OR'd into the `len` PARAMETER, can
perturb the length itself rather than only the byte order.

**SEVERITY DELIBERATELY LEFT AT `med` PENDING THAT ANSWER.**  If an 8-byte access reaches the
handler this is a guest-drivable mis-decode on a supported machine and should be HIGH; if it cannot,
this collapses into the same language-level hygiene as the other two census members and should be
LOW.  *Grading it before the answer would be picking the number I prefer.*

**THE REPAIR IS ONE TOKEN EITHER WAY** (`1U << dev`), and it is correct under both outcomes -- the
question is only what the round may CLAIM, and whether it owes a witness.


### `guestsrcunknown` (low) -- filed 2026-09-07: a contemporary guest OS source tree
### sits at the project root and nothing in the carrier mentions it

FILED 2026-09-07.  **NOT a defect -- a RESOURCE this project has and does not know it has**, filed
because I declared a hardware question unanswerable from this machine one paragraph before a seat
answered it from a file on disk.

*** `_guest-src-openbsd22/` SITS AT THE PROJECT ROOT AND CONTAINS THE ACTUAL GUEST OS SOURCE. ***
Derived rather than transcribed:

    8,138  .c files
    architectures: alpha  amiga  arc  arm32  atari  hp300  i386  kbus  m68k  mac68k  mvme68k
                   mvme88k  pc532  pmax  powerpc  sparc  sun3  vax  wgrisc

**Six of those are this fork's own emulation targets** -- `alpha` (alphabook1), `arc`, `arm32`,
`mvme88k` (the m88k/luna family), `pmax` (DECstation) and `powerpc` (macppc).  It is OpenBSD 2.2,
dated 1997, i.e. CONTEMPORARY with the hardware these device models emulate.

**IT IS NOT IN THE REPO.**  It lives at the project root, outside `GXEMUL-SEC/`, untracked -- which
is why nothing in the carrier or the harness mentions it and why a fresh session has no way to learn
it exists.

*** THE MEASURED PAYOFF, on the day it was noticed. ***  Working `lcaconfbus1kill`, I wrote into the
ledger that whether `ioc_conf & 1` is a bus selector or a cycle type is *"a statement about the
21066 ... not CHECKED here"*, because `_scratchpad/` holds no LCA datasheet.  The codex seat then
cited `_guest-src-openbsd22/sys/arch/alpha/pci/lca_pci.c`, and reading it settled the question
outright:

    :103   *bp = (tag >> 16) & 0xff;      /*  bus      */
    :106   *dp = (tag >> 11) & 0x1f;      /*  device   */
    :127   if (secondary) { ... REGVAL(LCA_IOC_CONF) = 0x01; ... }

That is the fix's decode verbatim, plus proof that the register selects the configuration FORMAT.
**And it converted the row's own caution -- "NOT CLAIMED: that any shipped guest issues this
sequence" -- into the opposite finding: the sequence IS the driver's secondary-bus path.**

> **WHY THIS BEATS A DATASHEET FOR THIS PROJECT'S QUESTIONS.**  The recurring question here is not
> *what does the hardware do* but *what does a guest actually do* -- is a path travelled, is a
> register written, does a driver depend on this behaviour.  The witness ladder itself ranks a boot
> above a probe for exactly that reason ("a probe proves a path CAN be reached; a boot proves it IS
> travelled").  **A contemporary driver for the emulated chipset answers that class directly, and it
> is greppable in seconds.**

**PROPOSED, NOT DONE: a carrier line.**  `CLAUDE.md` tells a reader to `ls _scratchpad/*.pdf` before
reasoning from first principles about a device, and records that an absent-source note was
load-bearing and wrong for twelve days.  **This is the same shape one directory over**, and the
analogous line would be: *before calling a guest-behaviour or chipset question unanswerable, grep
`_guest-src-openbsd22/sys/arch/<arch>/`.*  Editing the carrier is an owner-facing act and section J
checks its tracked copy, so it is **filed as a candidate for the 2026-09-09 adjudication** rather
than done unilaterally.

**A CAUTION THAT BELONGS WITH IT:** OpenBSD 2.2 is ONE guest at ONE version.  What it does is
evidence that a real driver does it; what it does NOT do is not evidence that no guest does.  And
the fork's models are not obliged to match this driver -- they are obliged to match the HARDWARE, of
which this is a well-informed second-hand reading.  *Cite it as "the OpenBSD 2.2 driver does X", never
as "the hardware does X".*


### `armbfiwidth` (med) -- filed 2026-09-07

cpu_arm_instr.c X(bfi): `(1 << width) - 1' where width = msb - lsb + 1 ranges [-30,32] -- 468 of 1024 encodable (msb,lsb) pairs reach an undefined shift on a 32-bit-int host (a DIFFERENT 496 have architecturally invalid field ordering) [2026-11-02, records: the two sets OVERLAP -- 465 of the 468 are among the 496, as this row's ledger title and the 2026-09-08 correction below say].  #510 fixed the SAME expression at UBFX and SBFX and left this third site fifty lines below, and its `== 32' form covers none of the negative widths

FILED 2026-09-07.  **`#510` fixed TWO of THREE sites of one idiom and left the third, whose undefined
domain is WIDER than either it repaired.**  Found by reading an UNREAD codex answer
(`regress/artifacts/queueunrated/codex_bitsbytes_20260907.txt`) that had been sitting on disk,
cited nowhere.  Every element below was VERIFIED by opening the file, not taken from the seat.

*** THE DEFECT. ***  `src/cpus/cpu_arm_instr.c`, `X(bfi)` (Bit-Field Insert):

    int lsb = (uint8_t)ic->arg[2];
    int msb = ic->arg[2] >> 16;
    int width = msb - lsb + 1;
    x <<= lsb;
    uint32_t mask = (1 << width) - 1;        <-- UNDEFINED over most of its domain

**THE DECODE GIVES msb AND lsb INDEPENDENTLY, each 0..31** (verified at the `bfi` arm of the
decoder, `(iword & 0x0fe00070) == 0x07c00010`):

    int lsb = (iword >>  7) & 31;
    int msb = (iword >> 16) & 31;
    ic->arg[2] = (msb << 16) + lsb;

so **`width` ranges over [-30, 32]** and `1 << width` is undefined three separate ways:

    width <= 0    negative shift count                       C99 6.5.7p3
    width == 32   count >= width of the promoted type        C99 6.5.7p3
    width == 31   1 is `int'; 2^31 is not representable       C99 6.5.7p4 (signed overflow)

*** THE DENOMINATOR, and it is nearly half. ***  Of the **1024** encodable (msb, lsb) pairs:

    496   nonpositive width  (lsb >= msb + 1)   -- of which 465 are strictly negative
      1   width == 32        (msb=31, lsb=0)
      2   width == 31        (msb=lsb+30)
    ---
    499   of 1024 pairs reach an undefined shift   [2026-11-02, records: 468 -- the 31 zero widths are defined; see the 2026-09-08 correction below]

**That arithmetic was INDEPENDENTLY DERIVED TWICE and the first attempt was mine and wrong.**  A
codex answer on a different brief (`codex_shiftub_20260907.txt`) corrected it: *"`msb - lsb + 1 < 0`
requires `lsb >= msb + 2`, giving 465 negative widths.  Another 31 pairs produce zero; 496 is the
number of nonpositive widths."*  Recomputed here from the decode: pairs with `lsb >= msb+1` sum to
31+30+...+1 = **496**, and `lsb >= msb+2` sums to 30+29+...+1 = **465**.  *The seat was right.*

*** WHY THIS IS A SIBLING MISS AND NOT A NEW CLASS. ***  `#510` repaired the identical expression at
the UBFX and SBFX handlers, which now read:

    uint32_t mask = (width == 32) ? 0xffffffffU : ((1U << width) - 1);

**`X(bfi)` sits about fifty lines below the second of those, in the same file, and was not touched.**
The carrier's mechanical rule 2 -- *when correcting a claim, grep for its siblings before calling it
fixed* -- is exactly the rule that was missed, and it is recorded there with a prior instance where
an "un-fakeable" claim was corrected in one place and survived in three.  **The BFX round's own
detector cannot see this**: `regress/arm_bfx_width_probe.py` plants UBFX/SBFX words only.

**AND THE BFX FIX DOES NOT TRANSFER UNCHANGED.**  BFX decodes `width = 1 + ((iword >> 16) & 31)`, so
its domain is {1..32} and a `width == 32` special case is sufficient.  **BFI's width can be zero or
negative, which no `== 32` test catches.**  A repair copied from the sibling would close one third of
this site's undefined domain and look right.

*** WHAT IS NOT ESTABLISHED, and it is the next step rather than a caveat. ***  **No witness has been
built and no host misbehaviour has been measured.**  UB is not by itself a defect this project ships
a fix for without a measurement -- `#510` shipped on a UBSAN differential (1 diagnostic pre-fix, 0
post-fix) plus a source pin, and this row owes the same.  The vehicle is cheap and already exists:
`arm_bfx_width_probe.py` plants instruction words and executes them on an unmodified machine, so the
witness is a planted `bfi` with `msb < lsb` under a UBSAN build.

**ARM architecturally leaves `msb < lsb` UNPREDICTABLE for BFI**, so a conforming guest does not emit
it.  *That is an argument about which guests reach it, not about whether the emulator may invoke host
UB when one does* -- which is the same argument `#510` made and shipped on.

**PROPOSED FIX (not adjudicated -- no panel has seen this):**

    uint32_t mask = (width <= 0) ? 0 :
        (width == 32) ? 0xffffffffU : ((1U << width) - 1);

with `mask = 0` for the nonpositive case leaving `rd` unchanged, which is a defensible reading of
UNPREDICTABLE and the only one that inserts no bits.  **The `x <<= lsb` on the line above is SAFE**
(`lsb <= 31` by construction) and must not be "fixed" alongside it.

*** CORRECTED 2026-09-08 BY THE codex SEAT, AND THE ERROR WAS MINE.  Re-verified by brute force
before this edit. ***

**499 WAS WRONG.  THE TRUE FIGURE IS 468, AND I HAD CONFLATED TWO DIFFERENT QUANTITIES.**

    width < 0     465   UNDEFINED -- negative shift count
    width == 0     31   *** DEFINED.  `(1 << 0) - 1' is 0.  A shift count of ZERO is legal. ***
    width 1..30   525   defined
    width == 31     2   UNDEFINED -- signed left-shift result, 6.5.7p4
    width == 32     1   UNDEFINED -- count >= width, 6.5.7p3
    ----
                  468   pairs reaching UNDEFINED BEHAVIOUR
                  496   pairs with ARCHITECTURALLY INVALID field ordering (msb < lsb)

**Those are different sets and I summed the wrong one.**  Every nonpositive width is an invalid
BFI encoding, but only the strictly NEGATIVE ones are undefined C.  *Three derivations agreed on 496
earlier -- and 496 was the right answer to a question I was not asking.*

**FOUR MORE CORRECTIONS FROM THE SAME ANSWER:**

* **P4 was partly wrong.**  `ddi0100i.txt` DOES contain zero `BFI`/`BFC` occurrences, but **its own
  architecture list includes ARMv6** (verified: *"ARMv4, ARMv4T, ARMv5T, (ARMv5TExP), ARMv5TE,
  ARMv5TEJ, and ARMv6"*), so calling it "the ARMv5 manual" is inaccurate.  BFI/BFC arrive with
  ARMv6**T2**, which is why they are absent.  And *"the broader claim that no other local reference
  exists remains unestablished."*
* **P5 CONFIRMED from the architecture, externally.**  ARM's BFI A1 description makes
  `msbit < lsbit` UNPREDICTABLE, and its constrained behaviour permits **an undefined instruction, a
  NOP, or an unknown destination value** -- so `mask = 0` is architecturally PERMITTED, not merely
  defensible.  **That settles Q1.**
* **P6 needs a host qualification, and it improves the FIX.**  `1U` is `unsigned int`, which C99
  permits to be 16 bits, so `(1U << width)` is not universally portable either.  codex recommends
  **`1UL` / `0xffffffffUL`**.  *** NOTE THIS MAKES `#510`'s SHIPPED REPAIR SUBOPTIMAL TOO -- it uses
  `1U` -- though harmless on every host this project builds on. ***
* **An early `return` IS sound here**, unlike the case the sketch rule was minted from: codex checked
  the macros -- `X` declares a void function and `Y` generates separate conditional wrappers -- so
  **there is no handler epilogue for a return to skip.**  *The sketch rule says to check the
  enclosing control flow, not that early returns are always wrong; here the check comes back clean.*

*** REACHABILITY IS ESTABLISHED: the BFI decoder branch has NO CPU-model or architecture-version
gate ***, and `machine_test.c` registers `testarm` defaulting to SA1110 -- so the site is reachable
in the simulator even though that CPU model predates the instruction.

**THE WITNESS DESIGN, from Q2, and it kills my one-word plan:**
* negative and excessive counts produce **DIFFERENT UBSan messages** (`shift exponent -1 is
  negative` vs `shift exponent 32 is too large for 32-bit type 'int'`), and width 31 is a *signed
  result* failure that plain shift-exponent checking MISSES;
* **one instruction encoding cannot exercise both count failures** -- the immediate fields fix
  `width`, and no register contents change it.  So the probe needs SEPARATE planted words per class.
* **Two apparatus traps, and the first is the error I made twice this session:** *"`session()`
  consumes child output through its PTY, while callers print parsed results.  Grepping the Python
  process's stderr can miss the sanitizer messages completely."*  And: UBSan suppresses repeat
  reports at an already-reported location, **so diagnostic totals are not execution counts** --
  require the intended site and diagnostic CLASS, not a total.

*Still outstanding before this can land, in codex's own words: "a fresh BFI sanitizer differential
and integration results from binaries tied to this exact tree.  I have not measured those or
established any host-visible wrong BFI result."*


### `armbfcdecode` (low) -- filed 2026-09-08

cpu_arm_instr.c: the bfi decoder accepts source field 15 and passes r[15] to X(bfi), but the architecture assigns that encoding to BFC (Bit Field Clear) -- so BFC is decoded as `BFI with Rn = PC'

FILED 2026-09-08 from the codex `armbfiwidth` design answer.  **BFC is BFI with Rn = 15**, and the architecture defines it as clearing the field rather than inserting from a register.  This fork's decoder does not distinguish them, so a BFC would insert bits taken from `r[15]` -- the PC -- instead of clearing.

**NOT VERIFIED HERE.**  It comes from one seat's source reading, and neither the decoder arm's exact guard nor the architectural claim has been re-derived by me. *The round-scope rule keeps it separate from `armbfiwidth`: same file and adjacent lines, but a different defect with a different fix and a different oracle, so it is a candidate ROUND rather than a rider.*

### `guardfailsopen` (med) -- filed 2026-09-08

the brief-launch guard FAILS OPEN on a missing file: `[ "$N" -lt 3 ]` with an empty N is a bash syntax ERROR, which `if` grades as FALSE, so the refusal branch is unreachable in exactly the case it exists for -- and the stale panel dir was pass 1's, so pass 1 could have been graded as pass 2

FILED 2026-09-08.  **A guard written SPECIFICALLY to stop a panel launching on an empty brief launched
a panel on a brief that did not exist** -- and it is a NEW MECHANISM for the check-that-cannot-fail
class, not another instance of the recorded one.

*** THE CASCADE, in order. ***

1.  The diff was written to git-bash's `/tmp/d512.diff` and READ by **Windows** python
    (`C:/Users/.../Python312/python.exe`), which resolves a DIFFERENT `/tmp`.  *The carrier already
    records `git-bash /tmp != WSL /tmp`; this is the same trap with a third interpreter.*
2.  The brief generator raised `FileNotFoundError`, so **no brief was written**.
3.  *** THE GUARD FAILED OPEN. ***  It read:

        N=$(grep -cE '^@@' "$BRIEF")
        if [ "$N" -lt 3 ]; then echo "REFUSING TO LAUNCH"; exit 1; fi
        echo "ok -- launching"

    On a MISSING file `grep -c` prints nothing, so `N` is the EMPTY STRING.  `[ "" -lt 3 ]` is not
    false -- it is a **bash syntax error**, `integer expression expected`, which exits NON-ZERO, and
    an `if` reads a non-zero exit as FALSE.  **So the refusal branch was skipped and execution fell through to the next line, which printed "ok -- launching".** [corrected 2026-11-02, records: said "So the else-branch ran" -- the quoted guard has no `else`]
4.  `panel.sh` printed `no such brief` and launched **nothing** -- and exited 0, so the background
    task reported SUCCESS.

*** WHY IT IS WORSE THAN A WASTED RUN: the newest panel dir was still PASS 1's. ***  Had the seat
files been read without checking the directory timestamp, **pass 1's answers would have been graded
as pass 2** -- a whole review stage discharged by the stage before it.  That is the carrier's own
warning about a relative `./panel.sh` launch ("a SILENT zero-seat failure that looks like a completed
run, so you review the previous round's stale seat files by mistake") reached by a different road.

> *** THE CLASS EXTENSION, and it contradicts something the carrier asserts. ***  The
> check-that-cannot-fail section concludes that in this project such a check *"is almost never a
> badly-written assertion -- it is a claim that some cheap observable stands in for an expensive
> one"*, and reports a hunt over 251 gate rows that found ZERO unguarded self-comparisons.
>
> **This is a badly-written assertion, and it is in a guard whose entire purpose was to prevent the
> failure it permitted.**  The mechanism is specific to shell: **a comparison against an EMPTY
> variable is an ERROR, not a FALSE, and `if` grades an error as false -- so the guard's refusal
> branch is unreachable in exactly the case it exists for.**
>
> The generalisation: **test EXISTENCE before you test a PROPERTY.**  A property test on a
> non-existent object cannot fail closed, because there is nothing to measure.

**THE FIXED FORM, used on the relaunch:**

    [ -s "$B" ] || { echo "REFUSING: brief missing or empty"; exit 1; }
    N=$(grep -cE '^@@' "$B" 2>/dev/null)
    [ "${N:-0}" -ge 3 ] || { echo "REFUSING: only ${N:-0} hunk markers"; exit 1; }
    grep -q "<a token from the diff body>" "$B" || { echo "REFUSING: diff body absent"; exit 1; }

Three properties, and each is load-bearing: `-s` catches missing AND empty; `${N:-0}` makes the
comparison well-formed whatever grep did; and the CONTENT grep catches a brief that has hunk markers
but lost the body.

**NOT MECHANISED, deliberately.**  This guard is written ad hoc at each launch rather than living in
`panel.sh`, and moving it there is a change to the script every panel runs -- which owes two negative
controls (prove it refuses a missing brief, prove it does NOT refuse a good one).  **That is its own
harness round.**  Note `panel.sh` ALREADY refuses correctly (`no such brief`); what is missing is
that the CALLER believes it launched.

*Provenance: my own guard, written earlier in the same session, in the same shell block, on the
belief that it made the launch safe.  It had worked on three previous briefs -- because they
existed.*

*** THE FIXED GUARD CAUGHT A REAL DEFECT ON ITS FIRST USE, AND IT WAS THE **CONTENT** CHECK THAT
FIRED -- not the existence test and not the count.  2026-09-08. ***

Building the `sgirekills` round-design brief, I inlined the arm cascade as lines 420-545 and the
guard refused:

    REFUSING: cascade truncated before LINEAR_B

**The range was wrong.**  `LINEAR_A`'s arm alone runs to line 585 and `LINEAR_B` starts at 588, so
the true cascade is 420-660 -- **241 lines, not 126.**  The brief would have said *"the FULL arm
cascade, VERBATIM"* while omitting the sixth of the six windows it was about, and the seat would
have answered a question about five arms believing it had seen six.

> **THE COUNT CHECK WOULD HAVE PASSED IT.**  126 inlined lines is a perfectly healthy-looking
> number; the file existed and was 11 KB.  **Only asking "is the thing I claim to have inlined
> actually in here?" could fail.**
>
> That is the denominator rule's own limit, restated: a denominator proves the apparatus SELECTED
> something, never that it selected the RIGHT something.  A content assertion is the only check that
> distinguishes them.

**So the three-part guard has now earned each of its parts by a different failure:** `-s` was minted
by the missing-file cascade that filed this row; `${N:-0}` by the empty-variable comparison; and the
CONTENT grep by this truncation, which the other two pass cleanly.

*Recorded because the guard was written defensively an hour earlier with no expectation of firing,
and the thing it caught was mine.*


### `pcc2genctlc040alias` (low) -- filed 2026-09-08

mvme_pcctworeg.h defines C040 TWICE with DIFFERENT values -- PCC2_C040 = 0x04 (right, and what the model uses) and PCC2_GENCTL_C040 = 0x03 (wrong; 0x03 is FAST|MIEN).  The wrong alias has no consumers today, so it is a loaded trap rather than a live defect

FILED 2026-09-08.  **`#512` verified `PCC2_C040 = 0x04` against the MVME187 board manual and shipped on it.  The header ALSO carries `PCC2_GENCTL_C040 = 0x03` sixty lines down.**  0x03 is `FAST|MIEN` -- two unrelated control bits -- so an edit reaching for the second spelling would test the wrong bits entirely and would look plausible doing it.

**NOT A LIVE DEFECT: a fork-wide grep finds ZERO consumers of the 0x03 alias.** It is upstream residue, inherited from OpenBSD's own `mvme88k/include/pcctworeg.h`, which carries the same wrong value.

*The disposition question -- DELETE the dead alias, or CORRECT it to 0x04 -- is an option-set question and is not settled here.  Deleting is the additions-licence-consistent move (a dead define is not load-bearing); correcting it leaves a second spelling for a future edit to pick.*


### `rulingnotinrow` (med) -- filed 2026-09-08

a STANDING flagship DO-NOT-CODE ruling lived in the CHANGELOG and another row's artifact but not in the row it governs, and a full round was designed against it before a seat caught it -- the population is NOT mechanically enumerable (two greps gave 0 and 9, the 9 mostly noise)

FILED 2026-09-08, from a MEASURED near-miss: I spent a round preparing to code `sgitexindex` against a
STANDING FLAGSHIP RULING that said DO NOT CODE, and a seat stopped it by opening a record I had not
read.

*** THE DEFECT IS NOT THAT THE RULING WAS UNRECORDED.  IT IS THAT IT WAS RECORDED SOMEWHERE THE
DECIDER DOES NOT LOOK. ***

    where the ruling was   CHANGELOG.md, and an artifact under ANOTHER row's directory
                           (regress/artifacts/pcc2widthkills/fable_adjudication_20260902.md)
    where I looked         the LEDGER ROW, which said `state: open, sev: low` and carried no note
    result                 a full round of design, a nine-seat brief, and a panel fired against a
                           question that had been adjudicated six days earlier

**The ruling even contained the finding I re-derived**: *"the proposed `>> 1` fix would IMPORT the
siblings' overrun."*  I enumerated that from scratch and wrote it up as new.

> **A STANDING DISPOSITION THAT LIVES ANYWHERE EXCEPT THE ROW IT GOVERNS WILL BE RE-OPENED BY THE
> NEXT PERSON WHO READS THE ROW -- which is exactly the population that might re-open it.**

*** THE POPULATION IS NOT MECHANICALLY ENUMERABLE, AND I TRIED. ***  Two greps disagreed:

    narrow (a close-word within ~120 chars AFTER the row id)      0 rows
    broad  (any ruling word within 400 chars either side)         9 rows

Spot-reading three of the nine: `wdcbeoddtail`'s hit is a SEVERITY assignment in an audit table
(noise); `sgirandomskipput`'s is a FILING decision (*"filed as X rather than dropped"*), not a
do-not-code; `m88kmxmkill`, `m88ktbnd` and `m88kexctaildefault` are *"filed now as documented-only
LOW rows"*, which IS a disposition worth carrying.  **So the broad check is a CORRELATE -- "a ruling
word near the row id" -- and not the class**, which is *a disposition decided elsewhere that the row
does not carry*.  That distinction needs READING, not grepping.

*This is the deriver rule landing on my own audit within the hour of my citing it: before writing a
deriver, ask what makes a member a member.  Here the answer is a property no regex tests.*

**NAMED CANDIDATES for a proper read, not a claim about them:** `m88kmxmkill`, `m88ktbnd`,
`m88kexctaildefault` -- all three cited in one sentence as filed documented-only, none carrying that
in the row.  **The other six flagged rows are probably noise and are NOT claimed.**

**NO CHECKER PROPOSED.**  A proximity grep would fire on ~9 rows with a majority false-positive rate,
which is how a check gets switched off -- this project's own recorded reason for declining the
stale-count checker.  What is cheap and reliable is a HABIT at the point of decision: **before
opening a round on any row, grep the CHANGELOG and `regress/artifacts/*/` for the row id and read
what comes back.**  It cost one command here and would have saved the round.

*Related in shape, one row over: `sgilinearoob` carried a bare title and an EMPTY note while the
2026-09-02 adjudication referred to "the siblings' overrun" as known -- the class was known to the
adjudication and not findable from the row that carries it.*

## 2026-09-08 — `#513 sgirekills`: five modelled registers ended the host when read back, and the panel refused my detector before the table did

**THE DEFECT.**  `dev_sgi_re.c` carried SIX read arms of the form

    } else {
            fatal("TODO: read from CRIME_RE_TLB_A\n");
            exit(1);
    }

each on the `else` of a `writeflag == MEM_WRITE` test, inside a window whose WRITE path is fully
modelled.  **A guest could store a value to `CRIME_RE_TLB_A` and reading the same address back ended
the emulator** -- one `ld` on an unmodified `-E sgi -e ip32`.

**FIVE BECAME ACCEPT** (option-set member 4: the write arm already computes and stores the value, so
the read returns it -- a decline would have shipped a wrong record in product code, announcing
"unimplemented" about a register the model implements).  **`CRIME_RE_TEX` became a latched DECLINE**
on its own new bit, because `sgitexindex` records its write index as a missing factor of four, only
31 of 112 cells are reachable, `re_tex` has NO consumer anywhere in the file, and that row carries a
standing do-not-code ruling.  Accepting it would publish a mapping the project has recorded as wrong.

**THE ORACLE-CORRECTION ORDERING, run rather than asserted.**  Six shipped rows asserted that a
len == 8 READ still ends the host.  The fix makes them false *by succeeding*, so the rows were
re-pinned FIRST and the committed build measured RED under the new expectations:

    committed build, re-pinned oracles   30/44    PREFIX_RED_20260908.out
    after the fix, SAME script           44/44   POSTFIX_20260908.out

Every red row on the pre-fix run was a NEW row; all pre-existing rows stayed green and all three
controls were green.

**KILL TABLE: 12 of 12 mutants killed, NONE escaped** (scratch clone, frozen
instrument, `killtable_20260908/TABLE1.txt`).

*** THE PART WORTH RECORDING IS THAT THE DESIGN PANEL REFUSED MY ROW SET, AND THE TABLE THEN MEASURED
BOTH OF ITS OBJECTIONS. ***  I proposed one row per window at the window BASE plus a `#499`-style
decline row for TEX.  grok refused it with two floor-shaped holes:

* **the FAR BOUND was unpinned** -- an accept row at a window's base tests the near bound twice and
  the far bound never.  Hence TWO rows per accepting arm, base AND last slot;
* **a load-only TEX decline row would have been VACUOUS** -- it wants `v0 == 0`, and a later ACCEPT
  of TEX would read back the ZEROED array and yield 0 as well, so the row could not redden at the
  very edit it exists to catch.  The TEX rows therefore STORE a non-zero value first.

**Measured afterwards, and both would have swept clean under my design:**

    M4_readshift  43/44   read-side index re-map    caught ONLY by the last-slot row
    M7_farbound   43/44   far-bound window shrink   caught ONLY by the last-slot row
    M8_texaccept  40/44   TEX -> ACCEPT             caught by all four store-first TEX rows

**THE `odata` TRAP.**  The function's common tail is
`if (writeflag == MEM_READ) memory_writemax64(cpu, data, len, odata);`, so a read arm filling
`data[]` is overwritten before the guest sees it.  A first draft of this fix did exactly that and
**would have returned zeroes while looking correct**; it is now mutant `M2_datafill`.  Caught by the
sketch rule -- an edit is not a fix until it has been run against the enclosing function's real
control flow.

**RECORDS.**  Two comment paragraphs in this file asserted the six read kills were "still untouched"
-- true when `#497` and `#499` wrote them, false the moment this round landed.  Both corrected in
place beside their originals rather than rewritten, so a reader arriving from those rounds can see
which half moved and when.  `gate_arm.sh` went 35 -> 44 rows in the same commit
(35 - 6 retired + 14 re-pinned + 1 new 64-bit liveness control).

**SEATS.**  grok, glm, deepseek, minimax and kimi (via the `kimi-k3:cloud` substitute) answered the
design pass.  **codex was REFUSED TWICE by the provider content filter on this subject**, once
unscoped and once with the `codexsubjectrefusal` scoping remedy applied deliberately -- a controlled
negative now recorded on that row, whose diagnosis is that scoping reading to `src/` cannot help when
`src/` IS the flagged content.  agy DELIBERATELY NOT FIRED (measurement reserve); Opus 5 and Fable 5
DELIBERATELY NOT FIRED (preserved for the 2026-09-09 adjudication).

## 2026-09-08 — `gateworktree` UPDATE: codex audited all 21 sections, and section D is VACUOUS ON A CORRECTLY-STAGED COMMIT

`regress/artifacts/gateworktree/codex_assess_20260908.txt` (14,102 b).  **The row was filed as
"validates the working tree, not the staged content".  That is right and it is not the worst of
it.**

**THE GATE SELECTS FILES FROM THE INDEX AND READS THEIR CONTENTS FROM THE FILESYSTEM.**  There is
no `git show :<path>` anywhere in the invoked checking paths; `git ls-files` tests MEMBERSHIP, not
content.  codex marks 18 of 21 sections false-green/false-reject on content.

*** SECTION D FAILS IN THE OPPOSITE DIRECTION AND IT WAS MEASURED ON `#513` ITSELF. ***  Its input
is `git diff -U0` — **UNSTAGED** additions — so the more completely you stage, the less it checks.
At `#513`'s gate run the only tracked-modified-but-unstaged file was `regress/sgi_de_primop_probe.py`,
which is deliberately excluded from every commit; `git show --stat e302c98 | grep -c
sgi_de_primop_probe` is **0**.  **D's two green rows were computed entirely from a file that is not
in the commit, while 129 staged files were invisible to it.**

**A SHIPPED INSTANCE, from history rather than from argument:** commit `2956c7e` added
`regress/sgi_mte_fill_probe.py` while its own `check_probe_wiring.py` carried **zero** manifest
entries for it.  (codex did not verify the historical gate output; the violation is established
from the commit contents.)

**TWO CORRECTIONS TO MY OWN FILING, both load-bearing for section J:** the project-root carrier
originals are **outside the git repository**, so J compares an UNTRACKED external file against a
tracked copy — update both and omit the copy from staging and J passes while the commit keeps the
old carrier; and J's tracked-copy existence test is a bare `-f`, which does not check index
membership.

**THE FIX IS NOT A FLAG.** Replacing reads with `git show ":$path"` inspects the WRONG version
before staging, because *"nothing staged" means the index equals HEAD, not that it is empty*.  The
shape: announce a SNAPSHOT MODE (index vs working-tree preview) before the first pipeline
invocation; keep the deliberately external inputs separate; and note the helpers derive paths from
`__file__`, so redirecting `ROOT` is insufficient — an isolated worktree carrying unchanged
dependencies is the practical route.

**SEVERITY LEFT AT `med`, DELIBERATELY, AND THE QUESTION IS REFERRED RATHER THAN DECIDED.**  It
changes no product behaviour; what it changes is what a GREEN GATE MEANS on every round on record.
*I raised one row's severity myself today and flagged it as my judgment; raising a second on one
seat's reading, in the same session, is exactly the habit the panel exists to check.*  It goes to
the 2026-09-09 adjudication with the evidence above.

**Negative controls this owes when it is built, in both directions:** prove a staged-only defect
REDS in index mode, and prove a working-tree-only artefact does NOT.

## 2026-09-08 — a probe-writing hazard: debugger `put` is a NO-OP against a `DM_DEFAULT` device

Found while diagnosing why a witness attempt did not fire. The mechanism, three lines:

    debugger_cmds.c:1461, :1507   memory_rw(..., MEM_WRITE, CACHE_NONE | NO_EXCEPTIONS)
    memory_rw.c:584               if (!no_exceptions || (flags & DM_READS_HAVE_NO_SIDE_EFFECTS))
    dev_ns16550.c:353             memory_device_register(..., DM_DEFAULT, NULL)

`DM_DEFAULT` is 0, the debugger passes `NO_EXCEPTIONS`, so **the device handler is never called**.
The write is absorbed and the debugger still echoes it back, which is what makes this look like it
worked.

**The carrier already records the READ half** — `dump` bypasses a `DM_DEFAULT` handler, hence
"read SH4 device state with guest loads". **The WRITE half is the same line of `memory_rw.c` and
was not written down.**

> **RULE: device access in a probe must be made by GUEST INSTRUCTIONS. `put` is for RAM only.**

**Population checked before filing: the in-tree probes already do this correctly.**
`lca_confbus_probe.py` seeds RAM with `put d` and reaches the device with guest `STQ`/`LDQ`;
`alpha_swpctx_v0_probe.py` uses `put` for RAM and `call_pal` only. The one violation was my own
un-shipped attempt, preserved as evidence and classified NOT a detector. **So this is filed as a
hazard for future probe authors, not as a live defect in anything committed.**

## 2026-09-08 — `probecolorprompt` (MED, filed): 53 of 61 pty probes omit `-A`, and a coloured prompt defeats every anchored parser

`use_colorized_output()` gates colour on `isatty(STDIN) && isatty(STDOUT)` — **a pty satisfies
both**, so every probe in this tree is the case where colour turns on. With `CLICOLOR` set the
prompt arrives as `\x1b[34;1mGXemul> \x1b[0m...` and no `^GXemul>` anchor matches.

**MEASURED both ways, same probe and binary:** `CLICOLOR=1` without `-A` → **53 escapes, zero
parsed responses, a CORRECT build scoring 1/5**; with `-A` → 0 escapes, 5/5. `-A` sets
`enable_colorized_output = false` (`main.c:317`).

**Population derived, not estimated: 61 probes call `pty.fork()`, 53 omit `-A`, and the 8 that
pass it are all the ARM ones.** The tree already holds the defence; it was applied to one family
and never carried.

**It does not fire on this machine** — `CLICOLOR` is unset, measured at 0 escapes — so no current
gate result is wrong. It is a latent environment dependence. **And the failure shape differs by
parser: a prompt-anchored parser fails CLOSED and is loud; a loose one may still match and
mis-attribute, silently.** The loose ones are the more dangerous half.

**Fixed only in `#514`'s own probe**, which that round owns. The other 52 are a separate harness
round: one argument per file, but it changes what every probe launches and owes a re-parse check
on each.

## 2026-09-08 — `seattruncverdict` (MED, filed): a seat truncated MID-VERDICT reads as agreement

glm returned exactly **21 bytes**, cut mid-word:

    **VERDICT: RATIFY THE

**None of the five recorded seat-failure classes fits.** Daemon up and the model in `api/tags` (not
a refused connection); no quota text (not a wall); the response is non-empty (not a thinking burn);
and it is a verdict line rather than an opening intention (not the minimax stall).

> **The danger is the word it stopped on.** This project's own VERDICT-LINE-FIRST policy exists so
> an answer survives truncation — and that is exactly what makes this shape harmful: the surviving
> fragment is `RATIFY`. A verdict-line extractor scores agreement; a size check scores a tiny file
> whose content reads positive. Neither can tell it from a seat that ratified in one line.

**The re-fire caught it and changed the answer's shape, not just its length:** 6,425 bytes, verdict
*"CLOSES AT PASS 6 ... fund no pass 7"* **with a stated contingency**. A contingent close is not the
unqualified ratification the fragment implied.

**Cause NOT established** — one occurrence, daemon healthy either side, re-fire immediately
successful. This row does not guess.

**Cheap defence, proposed not built:** a seat file whose entire content is shorter than its own
verdict line — no newline, no body — is mechanically detectable, and reporting it as TRUNCATED
rather than as a verdict costs one test in `seat_verdicts.py`. That tool is read by every panel, so
it owes negative controls in both directions and ships as its own harness round.

## 2026-09-08 — two seat answers preserved while the seat was still streaming, and one held the stopping answer

A truncation census over **200 seat answers written today** flagged 11. Six are the known
`codexcyberflag` zero-byte class (two of those still in flight), two are the `seattruncverdict`
glm fragment, and **three were grok answers preserved mid-stream** [2026-11-02, records: the list below names two truncated grok answers, pass 3 and pass 5, as the heading and "both artifacts" say; 6 + 2 + 3 = 11 matches the census total, so the third flagged grok answer is not named here]:

    pass 3   1,017 of 10,649 bytes preserved   (10%)
    pass 5   1,340 of 11,718 bytes preserved   (11%)
    pass 4 and 6                                complete -- grok had finished

**The live `_scratchpad` copies were also incomplete when I read them** (709 and 1,030 bytes), which
is why the verdicts never reached the record.

**grok's pass-3 verdict was `CHAIN CLOSES` with an explicit stopping rule** — *"do not open another
pass to chase apparatus hypotheticals this binary does not emit"* — **three passes before I asked
the panel for exactly that rule.** Its pass-5 verdict independently confirmed codex's finding, while
my receipt called that pass "unanimous among the landed seats".

**Passes 4–6 were not wasted** — each bought a real defect, and one (the coloured prompt) is
something the binary *does* emit. What was lost is that grok's discriminator was sharper and
earlier: it separates the colour case (emitted, worth a pass) from the order variants (synthetic
transcripts the pty never produces).

**Repaired:** both artifacts re-copied at full length and verified by their closing sentences, and
both verdicts recorded as ANSWERED.

**The general defect is a copy timed against nothing.** The carrier already requires a completion
sentinel before citing a preserved log; a panel dir has no single sentinel, and the seats finish at
different times. **Proposed, not built:** the panel launcher already `wait`s for all seats — copying
after that wait, rather than when the main loop next looks, removes the window entirely.

### `sgiretlbshiftub` (LOW; it said med until #554 re-graded it, 2026-10-02) -- filed 2026-09-10

`dev_sgi_re.c` `horrible_getputpixel()`, anchor `tileptr = d->re_tlb_a[tile_nr] << 16`: the three TLB
arrays are `uint16_t`, which promotes to `int`, so this is a SIGNED left shift and any entry with bit 15
set overflows `INT_MAX` -- undefined behaviour. **It is the only path that works**: two lines below, the
model accepts a tile pointer only `if (tileptr & 0x80000000)`, and bit 31 can only come from bit 15 of
the `uint16_t`, so every ACCEPTED pointer overflows and every non-overflowing one is REJECTED. The three
arrays are written by ordinary guest register writes, so the guest picks the value. `re_linear_a` is
`uint32_t` and is NOT affected (unsigned wrap, defined). Fix: three casts to `uint32_t`. Found by the
codex seat under the found-something-else licence while answering a `#519` test-coverage question
(`regress/artifacts/sgirandomcolour/codex_coverage_20260910.txt`); verified by reading before filing.
Witness OWED as an ATTEMPT: a `-fsanitize=undefined` build in `build-asan/` is the first thing to try,
since a rung-3 guest witness may be impossible for UB that behaves as intended on every compiler here.

### `mk48nvramkill` (HIGH) -- filed 2026-09-10 -- *** FIXED AND SHIPPED AS `#521`; see the CHANGELOG round block. The reading below stands and was CONFIRMED at rung 3 before the edit. ***

`dev_mk48txx.c`, anchor `default:if (writeflag == MEM_READ)`: **EIGHT offsets inside the device's own
mapped range end the emulator process, and a guest reaches them by reading ordinary NVRAM.**

Enumerated rather than reasoned. The device registers `MK48TXX_LEN` = `MK48T08_CLKSZ` = **8192** bytes, so
`relative_addr` spans `[0, 0x2000)`. The accept block passes everything OUTSIDE
`[MK48T08_CLKOFF, MK48T08_CLKOFF + MK48TXX_ISEC)` straight to the RAM path with a `goto ret`. With
`CLKOFF = 0x1ff0` and `ISEC = 9`, the `switch` is reached for exactly nine offsets, `0x1ff0..0x1ff8` -- and
it has exactly ONE case, `CLKOFF + MK48TXX_ICSR` = `0x1ff8`. **The other eight, `0x1ff0` through `0x1ff7`,
fall to `default:` and call `exit(1)`.**

**Reachability is not theoretical.** `machine_mvme88k.c` attaches it unconditionally --
`mk48txx addr=0xfffc0000` -- in the same block as the PCC2 SCSI this project has been running rounds
against all week. Those eight are ORDINARY BYTES of the chip's clock/NVRAM page; nothing unusual is
required to touch them, and firmware that checksums or dumps the NVRAM sweeps the whole 8 KB and walks
straight in. No guard, no validation, and no way for a guest to learn the region is fatal first.

**AND THE BOUNDARY LOOKS DELIBERATE, WHICH IS WHY IT SURVIVED.** The accept block's own comment says
*"Reads and writes to the RAM part of the mk48txx, or the clock registers, are OK"*, and the test reads as
though it means *everything except the clock registers*. But its upper bound is `CLKOFF + ISEC`, the
SECONDS register -- so it hands the real time-of-day registers (`ISEC..IYEAR`, `0x1ff9..0x1fff`) to the RAM
path, which is harmless because `mk48txx_update_regs()` writes into that same `d->reg[]` array, and it
captures `0x1ff0..0x1ff7` into the fatal switch, which is not. *The bound is one constant away from correct
in the direction nobody checks.*

Fix shape NOT adjudicated -- no panel has seen this. Members 3 (decline + latched announce) and 6 (backed
accept) both fit, and BACKED ACCEPT is probably right because **`d->reg[]` already has storage for those
offsets**: the array is `MK48TXX_LEN` bytes, so the bytes exist and the handler simply refuses to use them.
That makes this closer to a boundary correction than to a new policy. The round owes a check of WHICH
constant is right against `mk48txxreg.h` rather than assuming. **Witness OWED as an ATTEMPT**: mvme88k is
an in-tree machine and a debugger byte read at `0xfffc1ff0` looks like a cheap rung-3 probe, but none has
been built and this entry claims none.

Found by the GPT-6 Astra exit audit (`regress/artifacts/queuetriage/codex_exitaudit_20260910.txt`), which
ranked it first on BOTH axes out of 76 unowned runtime error-exit sites across 24 files. Every element
above was re-derived locally by opening the files.

### `mipsextshift` (MED) -- filed 2026-09-10 -- *** CORRECTED 2026-09-10 BY THE DESIGN REVIEW IN FOUR PLACES; the corrections are at the end of this entry and the reading below is kept because it is what the row was filed from. ***

`cpu_mips_instr.c`, anchors `X(ext)` and `X(dext)`: the extraction shift count is computed from two
independently decoded instruction fields and **goes NEGATIVE for 496 of 1024 encodable pairs**.

`X(ext)` computes `int size = msbd + 1;` then `x = (rs << (32-lsb-size)) >> (32-lsb-size);`, with `msbd`
and `lsb` each decoded from the instruction word in `0..31`. Enumerating all 1024 pairs gives **496 with a
negative count** -- undefined, C99 6.5.7p3. `rs` is `uint32_t`, so the left operand is unsigned and the
signed-`1` form does not arise; **that is the trap**, because a reader checking *"is this unsigned?"* passes
the site, and a negative COUNT is undefined whatever the operand's type.

`X(dext)` is the same shape at 64 bits and is worse in a way that reads as a precaution: the count is CAST,
`(rs << (uint64_t)(64-lsb-size))`. **The cast does not rescue it** -- a negative `int` converted to
`uint64_t` becomes an enormous positive value, so the count is then at or beyond the width of the type.
*A cast that converts one undefined form into another while reading as a fix is worth recording as a
pattern.*

**This is a FIELD-VALIDATION defect, not a cast defect, and that decides the fix.** MIPS requires
`lsb + size <= 32` for EXT and the corresponding bound for the `dext` family; an encoding violating it is
architecturally invalid. So the repair is probably to DECLINE or to raise the architectural exception, not
to paper the shift over -- a mask repair would give a defined answer to a question the guest was not
entitled to ask, and would make invalid encodings look supported. That is a panel question, which is why
this is filed MED rather than as an easy one-token repair.

Reachability: MIPS is this project's primary architecture with the most exercised rigs, and the count comes
straight from the instruction word with no CPU-model gate, so a guest need only execute one malformed EXT.
**Not measured, no witness built** -- what is established is the domain arithmetic and the decode, both
re-derived here.

**Distinct from `shiftubcensus`**, which is the SIGNED-1 family (`1 << n` with a plain-`int` literal). This
is the NEGATIVE-COUNT family: a different C99 clause and a different fix shape. Found by the GPT-6 Astra
fix-design review on `armbfiwidth` while looking for siblings of that round's idiom outside ARM.

### `mapledmaaddr` (HIGH) -- filed 2026-09-10

`dev_dreamcast_maple.c`, grep anchor `case 0x04:	/*  MAPLE_DMAADDR  */`: **the read arm computes the
correct value and then throws it away by terminating the process.** In order:

```c
fatal("[ dreamcast_maple: TODO: read from dmaaddr ]\n");
odata = d->dmaaddr;
exit(1);
```

The WRITE arm two lines above stores `d->dmaaddr = idata`, so the register is **fully modelled in both
directions**. A guest that writes the DMA address and reads it back -- the ordinary way to confirm a
controller programming step -- is killed on the read. `machine_dreamcast.c` adds `dreamcast_maple`
unconditionally, and nothing has to start DMA or build a command list to get there.

**This is option-set member 4 (ACCEPT) in its textbook shape**: the model already computes the right
answer and then discards it, so the disposition is to delete the kill and KEEP THE VALUE, with **no
latch** -- there is no event to announce, and a bounded announce would ship a wrong record in product code
(*"unimplemented; ignored"* about a read that is implemented and is not ignored). **Two deleted lines.**
FAULT is neither available nor appropriate: `memory_rw.c` converts a failed device callback into an
architectural exception for MIPS and M88K only, and this device is on an SH4 machine -- but the access is
implemented, so refusing it would be wrong even if the machinery existed.

Test carrier already exists: `regress/gdrom_default_probe.py` supplies a Dreamcast session with guest
load/store helpers. **The oracle must assert that a separately STORED value reads back EXACTLY and that
execution continues** -- observing a zero, or a surviving debugger prompt, is vacuous, since both are true
of several wrong implementations. Not measured, no witness built; the rung-3 attempt is owed.

### `xscaleinten` (HIGH) -- filed 2026-09-10

`cpu_arm_coproc.c`, grep anchor `void arm_coproc_i80321_6`, crm 0 / crn 0: the load arm reads

```c
cpu->cd.arm.r[rd] = cpu->cd.arm.i80321_inten;
fatal("TODO: XScale read from inten?\n");
exit(1);
```

The destination register receives the modelled value and the process then dies. The store arm immediately
below writes the same field and the i80321 interrupt controller consumes it, so the register is fully
modelled both ways.

*** THE DECISIVE EVIDENCE IS THE SIBLING CASE IN THE SAME SWITCH, one screen away. *** `case 4:`
(`i80321_isteer`) has the **identical structure** -- load arm assigns from the modelled field, store arm
writes it -- and carries **no `fatal()` and no `exit()`**. So `crn 0`'s kill is an OUTLIER inside its own
switch rather than a policy: the upstream-residue pattern this project has now found several times, where
the author hit the exit he happened to reach while developing and not the sibling he did not. *That is a
far stronger warrant than "it is a host kill", and it is one grep away* -- which is exactly what the
option-set rule's sibling check is for.

*[CORRECTED 2026-10-18 at the row's closure (the closure checks of GPT-6 Astra and Grok 4.7,
regress/artifacts/xscaleinten/close_20261018/, each finding it independently; verified at source): `case 4:`'s STORE
arm is not quiet -- a nonzero store calls `fatal()` and `exit(1)` (the `i80321_isteer` store in
src/cpus/cpu_arm_coproc.c).  Only its LOAD arm is quiet, and the load arm is the sibling this warrant needs; the
ledger's copy already draws that line.]*

Reachability is explicit rather than inferred: `machine_iq80321.c` installs it with
`cpu->cd.arm.coproc[6] = arm_coproc_i80321_6;`, and Iyonix does the same. Emulated firmware reading its
own interrupt-enable register is the natural consumer, and the generic coprocessor dispatcher enforces no
supervisor-only precondition.

Disposition: **member 4 (ACCEPT)**, two lines deleted, no latch, for the same reason as `mapledmaaddr`.
*** L4, CORRECTED 2026-09-11: THAT SENTENCE READ "FAULT is unavailable regardless -- the failed-device
exception path is MIPS and M88K only, and this is ARM."  **IT IS WRONG, AND IT REASONS FROM THE WRONG
MECHANISM.** ***  The MIPS/M88K claim is about `memory_rw.c`'s failed-DEVICE-ACCESS path, which is
irrelevant here: a coprocessor register transfer is not a device access and never reaches it.  **ARM has
undefined-instruction delivery and it is already used** -- `cpu_arm.c:2677`, in `arm_cdp()`:

    fatal("[ arm_cdp: pc=0x%08x, iword=0x%08x ]\n", (int)cpu->pc, iword);
    arm_exception(cpu, ARM_EXCEPTION_UND);      /*  LIVE, not commented out  */

and `arm_exception()` at `:616` handles `ARM_EXCEPTION_UND` at `:634`.  **So member 5 (FAULT) IS
AVAILABLE on ARM coprocessor sites.**  Note the near neighbour, which is the more interesting fact:
`arm_mcr_mrc()`'s missing-handler branch at `:2660` carries **the very same call, commented out** --
`// arm_exception(cpu, ARM_EXCEPTION_UND);` -- so an access to an UNINSTALLED coprocessor prints and
falls through silently today.

**THE DISPOSITION IS UNCHANGED AND ITS REAL WARRANT IS BETTER: ACCEPT (member 4) stands on its own
merits** -- the model already computes the correct value and then discards it, which is the footbridge
IRQEnable precedent, and FAULT would be wrong for a register the model implements.  What was wrong was
the claim that the alternative did not exist.

*** WHY THIS WAS WORTH CORRECTING RATHER THAN LEAVING: the false warrant is TRANSFERABLE, and there are
SEVEN sibling guest-reachable host kills in `cpu_arm_coproc.c` waiting to reuse it *** (CP6 `unknown`,
CP14 `unknown`, CP15 PID, CP6 ISTEER, CP15 endian, CP6 ISRC, CP15 `rd == ARM_PC`).  **For the two
`unknown:` default arms, UND is very likely the RIGHT member**, and a sentence saying FAULT is
impossible would have removed it from the option set before anyone looked.  Found by the fable5
adjudication of the held queue (`regress/artifacts/heldqueue/fable_adjudication_20260911.md`) reading
`codex_coproc_20260910.txt`, an answer on disk since 2026-09-10 that no record cited; **every element
re-verified here by opening `cpu_arm.c` before this edit was written.**

Not measured, no witness built for the FAULT alternative. Note the witness needs a **coprocessor read from an ARM guest**,
which is a different vehicle from the device probes this project mostly writes; `gate_arm.sh`'s decode
checks are the nearest existing machinery.
