## 2026-09-23 — GXEMUL [087a90]: `#545` fbdeclinefive CLOSES (five host kills declined, a 864-row detector); what its passes filed

### `armdesc3kill` (HIGH; it said MED until #554 re-graded it, 2026-10-02) -- an ARM L1 descriptor of type 3 (fine page table) ends the process
`src/cpus/memory_arm.c:252-254`: the `default:` of the L1 descriptor switch is `fatal("TODO: descriptor for vaddr ...
unimplemented type %i")` then `exit(1)`.  Type 3 is a LEGAL ARMv4/v5 descriptor (fine page table, 1 KB pages) a guest
writes into its own translation table, so any guest that uses fine page tables kills the host at its first translation.
Options: FAULT (member 5 IS available on the translation path -- `fs = FAULT_TRANS_S; goto exception_return`, the file's
own idiom at `:158`) as the cheap decline, IMPLEMENT (member 7) as the honest one.  Witness: rung 3, MMU ON (the sites
probe's arm T scaffold), one L1 entry with bits [1:0] = 11.  Found by the kimi CLI on fbdeclinefive pass 1; ranked by
fable5 Q5 (legal value beats reserved value).

### `armdacr2kill` (MED-LOW) -- DACR field value 2 (reserved) ends the process
`src/cpus/memory_arm.c:78-79`: `arm_check_access()` `case 2: fatal("arm_check_access(): 1 shouldn't be used"); exit(1);`.
`cpu_arm_coproc.c:203` stores MCR's operand into `dacr` unfiltered and `memory_arm.c:153` derives `dav` from it, so a
guest writing 0b10 into any domain field and touching that domain kills the host.  Architecturally reserved /
UNPREDICTABLE; the fix is one `case 2:` treated as no-access (or as `case 0:`).  Witness: rung 3, MMU ON, DACR written
by a guest mcr.  kimi CLI, fbdeclinefive pass 1; fable5 Q5.

Witness: rung 3, write +0x190, read +0x184 -> bit 1 (the ONLY guest-controllable route to a NONZERO irq_status under

### `fbirqstuck` (MED) -- the footbridge's CPU interrupt line can stick high while IRQ_STATUS reads 0
`footbridge_interrupt_deassert()` lowers `d->irq` only when `d->irq_asserted` is set, and the IRQEnableSet and
IRQEnableClear write arms call `INTERRUPT_ASSERT(d->irq)` without setting it.  So: a device line (cats ISA, line 10)
asserts while its enable bit is clear (no assert); the guest sets the enable (`W188 0x400` -> ASSERT, `irq_asserted`
still 0); the line deasserts -> no DEASSERT.  The CPU line stays 1 with nothing pending -- a guest can take interrupts it
cannot clear.  Found and measured by the Opus seat on #545's repair pass 2 (an in-process differential over every
access sequence of length 1-3 from reset; `regress/artifacts/fbd5/q2_20260923/p2r_20260923/opus_q2r/dom_witness.txt`, "model check").  Pre-existing:
the enable arms' bodies are upstream's.  Fix: the enable arms keep `irq_asserted` as the callbacks do.
*** AND THE PRODUCER PAIR'S OWN BIT LOGIC IS FILED HERE, BY OWNER RULING (2026-09-23), and it is a DIFFERENT defect
from the stuck-high line above (grok, #545 3c's pass): a round closing F13 can finish without touching it, so the round
that takes this item owes both. ***  #545's detector calls `footbridge_interrupt_assert()` only to raise one line from
an empty status (and checks that raise: irq_status 0x10, irq_asserted 1, one CPU assert -- PR09 reds it) and never
calls `_deassert()`.  So the pair's bit logic passes all 864 rows and is disclosed in the detector's contract: `|=` ->
`=` in the assert (PR01), the enable test weakened to `if (d->irq_enable)` (PR03), the `~` deleted from `_deassert`'s
`irq_status &= ~interrupt->line` (PR04; r3_20260923/t_deassert.txt).  READY DETECTOR: the Opus seat's q2e scratch rows
Y8-Y12 and its PR01/PR02/PR04/PR07 witnesses (q2_20260923/q2e_opus/).  OPTIONS the #545 passes named: a bounded
producer smoke block of five histories (repeated assert, a second line, a disabled line, deassert of one of two
pending lines, deassert of the last enabled -- codex); a one-row two-line raise pinning `|=` (minimax); a dedicated
`diff_footbridge_irq.c` (agy).  The owner chose none of them for #545: disclose and file.

`pad_kept()` -- the bytes above the width still hold the 0xa5 fill -- after X6's declined accesses and X9/X10's legal
reads.  Three shapes stay unobserved on the 864 rows:
(1) a FETCH past `len` whose value no channel uses -- at every declined write, and the Opus seat's FW03 (an 8-byte
fetch at len 4, measured green and equivalent for the guest) -- UNOBSERVABLE HERE BY CONSTRUCTION: the harness's memory
helpers do not record the length the device asks for;
(2) a STORE past `len` inside a legal write -- `data[len] = 0` in the Clear write (codex, 3e's pass; measured green,
`qwb_20260923/QDLEN.log`): X12/X13 poison the buffer before the write and do not re-check it after;
(3) the common tail's write-back past `len` at the legal reads outside X9/X10's five registers, among them VENDOR_ID
(+0x00), the timer value (+0x304; +0x324/+0x344/+0x364 fold onto it), FIQEnable (+0x288) and the FIQEnableClear read
(+0x28c) -- which X7 reads, and X3 three of them, with no check above the width -- and the timer LOAD and CLEAR reads
near the top of `diff_footbridge.c`, whose 4-byte harness buffer an 8-byte write-back overflows SILENTLY.  An 8-byte
write-back keyed on any one of them passes every row -- measured for all seven keys
(`regress/artifacts/fbd5/q2_20260923/qwb_20260923/`: three runs, predictions first -- `ORDER_NOTE.txt` says which file

Above #545's floor: the tail and the fetch are not predicates dominating the edited arms, so the round disclosed them

### `fbctrlportdebt` (MED, detector) — the two classes #549's probe discloses, and the measured one-diff close for both

The v6 probe (117 rows) discloses two classes it cannot see, each MEASURED at the full score by the Opus seat
(`regress/artifacts/fbctrlportkill_20260924/opus549_measured/f2v6/`): **the latch crossed with one bit** (NOT CLAIMED
(0): while `warned_port` is clear the compare ignores bit k -- 58 bits open, 4-7, 9-31 and 33-63; from bit 32 up the
escape is a SILENT truncation onto a legal port, `sd 2^40` selecting port 0, #549's own pre-fix defect -- and an accepted value does not set the latch,
so the escape remains possible while the latch is clear, not once: GPT-6 Astra, confirming `#549`)
and **a refusal that writes the constant equal to a value's only anchor** (NOT CLAIMED (3): 60 refused values are
observed at exactly one previous selector).  The flagship ruling (`pass_v6/fable5_f2_v6.md`) graded both clause (e),
not floor -- a relational compare's generating set is its three regions -- and filed the close with its measured delta:
* **the prototype** (`opus549_measured/f2v6/scripts/u_sessions.py.txt`): one fresh device per single-bit value,
  `PORT=7`, the store, one PORT read -- keep, announce once, name.  **61/61 on the fix in 9.7 s** (`TABLE_U.out`; gate
  16 would go from ~17 s to ~27 s).  It kills N1_mask4, N1_mask40 and MKB_40, and the `-> 5` forms of D2; **B at 5 plus
  U at 7 gives every single bit two anchors.**
* **its width rule (P1, three seats independently):** `sw` below bit 32 and `sd` from bit 32 up -- a 32-bit store of 2^k
  for k >= 32 delivers 0, which the fix ACCEPTS, so a `sw`-only row would be red on the correct build.
* **its anchor rule:** neither 5 (that is D2) nor 0 (a leaked 2^k >= 2^32 is stored as int 0 and would read as "kept 0");
  a SECOND anchor closes a value's constant form, a REPLACED anchor moves it (measured: B's sd group at 7 opens `-> 7`
  on bits 32 and 34-62), and per-width anchors do not close it.  **Include bit 32** -- the 58-bit list leaves it out, and
  `2^32 -> 5` then survives.
* **adoption re-predicts** `DSC_ann_hibits`, `CF2_KM_not16` and `CF2_DM_ge16` (U's announce and name rows red the
  first), and leaves the residue `0xffffffff` at 5 and `0x100000005` at 3 -- which a non-exhaustive selection of values cannot rule
  out in general (`idata == k`; the domain is finite, so exhaustive rows are impractical, not impossible).
The owner may pull it into `#549` as v7; if so it owes one pass.

## 2026-10-02 — GXEMUL [087a90]: `#529` crimewidthkill CLOSES (its chain closed 2026-09-26; the review of its text and records ran to 2026-10-02); what that review files

Evidence: `regress/artifacts/crimewidthkill/` -- the panels (durable copies beside each pass), the Opus records, the
dedicated jobs, the flagship rulings (the first-hand 09-25 re-ruling in `rerule_20260925/`; repair 15's pass 2 and
repair 16's F2 adjudication), GPT-6 Astra's confirmations, and every kill table with its PRETABLE.

### `crimectllane` (HIGH, device) — CRIME_CONTROL acts on the raw value of whatever width reaches the exact label 0x08

`dev_sgi_ip32.c`, `DEVICE_ACCESS(crime)`, `case CRIME_CONTROL:` (0x008) matches the EXACT label and acts on the RAW
`idata` of the access that reached it.  So a 32-bit `sw 0x800` to `+0x08` -- the HIGH half of the 64-bit register on this
big-endian machine -- carries bit 11 into `CRIME_CONTROL_HARD_RESET` and stops every CPU, while a 32-bit write to
`+0x0c`, the lane that holds bit 11 and the offset NetBSD 1.6.2 writes (the arm's own TODO says so), performs the
register store and reaches the default arm's log, bypassing CONTROL's reset and watchdog handling.  MEASURED by `#529`'s
pass-1 Opus seat (`crimewidthkill/opus_pass1_20260913/out/rows_base.out`: `sw CTL+08 0x800` halted; `sw CTL+0c 0x800`
did not halt, `dflt=1`).  (A draft of this entry said the `+0x0c` write "does nothing" -- GPT-6 Astra's records audit.)  `#529`'s detector USES this defect as a channel
(`sw08 halts`, `sw08 msg ctl`, the `sh08` rows) and says so; a round that fixes the lane owes those rows' re-derivation.
Needs a guest witness of what a real driver writes (the PROM's reboot path; NetBSD's watchdog) before choosing a lane
model.  **A probe comment and `gate_arm.sh` have called this row "filed" since 2026-09-13 (a second probe comment called
`crimebankorder` filed); the resumption dossier found neither filing, and the flagship's 09-25 re-ruling listed both.**  **Graded HIGH, not MED:** stopping
every CPU ends the emulation in ordinary single-machine execution without `debugger_enter_at_end_of_run` (`emul.c`
enters the debugger instead when it is set) and the process returns, so a guest store that on the header's
model reaches only reserved high-word bits ends the emulator -- the severity rule's HIGH.  GPT-6 Astra's confirmation of
the codex farm's adjudication (`codexfarm_20260926/adjudication/codex_astraconfirm_farm_f1c.txt`) overturned the Fable
seat's MED; that seat's argument -- the guest gains no capability it lacks through the legitimate 64-bit HARD_RESET --
bears on reachability ranking, not on severity.

### `crimebankorder` (LOW, device) — the CRIME prelude writes the bank-control registers contiguously; the header interleaves them

The prelude's bank loop writes `d->reg[CRIME_MEM_BANK_CTRL0 / sizeof(uint64_t) + bank]` -- CONTIGUOUS offsets
0x208..0x240 -- while `src/include/thirdparty/crimereg.h:141-148` defines the bank control registers INTERLEAVED (CTRL0
0x208, CTRL1 0x218, CTRL2 0x210, CTRL3 0x228, CTRL4 0x220, CTRL5 0x238, CTRL6 0x230, CTRL7 0x248; raised by the codex
pass-1 seat on 2026-09-13, re-read 2026-09-26).  If the header is right, banks 1..7 are reported at the wrong offsets
and a guest sizing memory from them reads the wrong layout.  **But the header is itself suspect:** CTRL7 (0x248) is the
same offset as `CRIME_MEM_REFRESH_CNTR` (`:149`), and no bank register sits at 0x240.  Needs a boot witness (the IP32
PROM's memory report, or NetBSD's or OpenBSD's own sizing) before any edit -- the header, not the code, could be wrong.
`#529`'s `top8 anchor` row pins the model's CURRENT layout and says a round re-ordering the banks owes its
re-derivation.  **Called "filed" in the probe since 2026-09-13; filed nowhere until now.**

The flagship's F2 ruling (`crimewidthkill/repair16_f2_20260926/fable5_f2_adjudication.md`, Q4) closed the chain with NO
row owed and FILED items 1-7; its final ruling (`crimewidthkill/final529r18_20260926/fable5_final.md`, C) added item 8.
Each is filed with its measured or derived kill and its re-run cost:
1. a value anchor BESIDE the prefix count in `ctldog`/`ctlrst` -- kills `D_dogbit0` (226/226 today); re-runs
   `D_nodogclear`'s red set.  (An anchor IN PLACE of the count loses `H_noresetclear`: `opus_f2/replay_ctl.out`.)
2. a latch-SET `sh 0x0201` in `sh08b` -- kills `P_ctl2wrc_set`; re-runs M8 and M1.
3. one free-running accepted `sw 0x0001` session -- kills `M_ctldebug` (the arm's `fatal()` demoted to `debug()`, which
   every stepped session prints either way: `opus_f2/disc_f2.out`).
4. an `lb` appended after the first refusal in the `istat`/`imask` sessions -- kills `W_istlb`/`W_imklb` (226/226,
   table 16, as predicted); re-runs M6 and M7.
5. six latch-CLEAR first-refusal sessions at INTSTAT/INTMASK -- kill the `C_` variants.
6. a refused `lb +0x10` while the interrupt line is asserted -- kills `P_istprev_set`.
7. an `sw 0x0801` last-store session -- the HARD_RESET x bit-0 member of the bit-conditioned family, only if (1) is taken.
8. entry 34 of the ACCEPTS-46 enumeration (`sd +0x40`, latch CLEAR): both of its latch-CLEAR drivers store 0 into a
   slot that holds 0, so a silent decline of that one access moves no row (k34C 226/226) -- clause (e), the
   unrowed-slot class, by the flagship's final ruling (2026-09-30), GPT-6 Astra confirming.  The cheap row: seed a
   nonzero value in the two value sessions' `sd +0x40` and re-want `acc 40 sw` / `p acc 40 sw`; its cost: S55 and S58
   carry entries 8-11, 14, 15, 19, 21, 23, 24, 30, 31 and 34-37, so every recorded kill touching them re-runs.
All are above-floor strengthenings: items 1, 2 and 4-7 cover state/value joints (the CONTROL arm reads no latch and
does not individually test or clear bit 0; the remaining joints are not distinguished by the decline); item 8 belongs
to the unrowed-slot class, with the {default label, 8-byte store, latch CLEAR} cell held at +0x278; item 3,
`M_ctldebug`, is separately a DIAGNOSTIC-TRANSPORT change in upstream code the fix does not touch (the ruling's X8).  (A draft called all
seven of the F2 items "joints" -- GPT-6 Astra's records audit; item 8 was ordered by the final ruling.)  Rank below any live defect in `dev_sgi_ip32.c`.

#### `closeassessrows` (MED, a CLASS row: a records defect of the LEDGER, found while checking which rows carry this file's prose) -- the 2026-08-27 sweep closed CLOSE (assess) rows that still name undone work, and each member needs a re-open decision
**What it is.**  On 2026-08-27 one sweep closed ledger rows that carried the adjudicator's note `CLOSE (assess)` -- "on the adjudicator's recorded authority", with "no independent re-verification of the underlying defect" (each row's own `state_note`).  That note signs off a row's ASSESS STAGE: seven rows carry it while held or in work.  For the 8 members below the grok seat found the work the row names NOT done and carried by no other row.  **Nothing is re-opened by this row or by `#555`**: whether each member is re-opened, re-filed or closed with a commit is this row's work, one decision per member.  Each member's ledger row carries a note saying so.

**Members (8):** `m8latch`, `gcsections`, `ns16550`, `pcchalt`, `wdcstandby`, `rtcnarrow`, `scunbacked`, `m437multi`.  *[2026-10-22, research TRIAGE.md T95: `rtcnarrow` also carries the uncapped RTCL1 backlog -- `dev_vr41xx.c:396` increments the pending count with no cap, acknowledged only at `:628-635`; port jroark bea47e2.]*

**Read by no seat (2):** `ledgerwitness`, `cmtattr` -- closed by the same sweep with no commit; they belong to this row's audit.

**The ruling seat's evidence, in its words** (`regress/artifacts/idless_20261002/grok/grok_grok_irule_d.txt`; the `ledger.json` line numbers are those of commit `1202d342`): `CLOSE (assess)` signs off the assess stage. The seven rows whose notes continue past it are still live: `i8253zero` held (`ledger.json:9278`), `idesync` in work (`:12953`), `wdcflood` in work (`:13498`), `landiskdisk` in work (`:13993`), `rtcflood` held (`:15096`), `floodclass` held (`:15480`), `isaorder` held (`:16315`). The sweep's own text, `ledger.json:10393`, closed the bare note and performed no re-check. Eleven is too many. Checked and still undone, with no later carrier: `m8latch` (`dev_m8820x.c:90-97`), `gcsections` (`gate_offline.sh:729`, `:820`), `ns16550` (`dev_ns16550.c:181`), `pcchalt` (no `regress/ppc*.py` page-crossing probe; halt comment only at `cpu_ppc_instr_loadstore.c:63-84`), `wdcstandby` (`WDCC_STANDBY_IMMED` is `0xe0` at `wdcreg.h:138` and still hits `default:` with `WDCE_ABRT` at `dev_wdc.c:1155-1156`), `rtcnarrow` (`dev_vr41xx.c:606` integer-divides `RTCL1_L_HZ / idata` and `:614` ignores the high half; `ledger.json:15084` says the core floor is the wrong fix site), `scunbacked` (`gate_offline.sh:2346-2349` still greps bare `@@SELFCHECK@@` while `diff_rtc_range.c:140` names that token in a comment), `m437multi` (`diskimage.c:1291-1292` still writes only the last overlay, and `:2395-2412` fails the sync if any overlay fsync fails). Checked and left out: `m8sarseq` is carried by open `m8sarrows` (`ledger.json:25702-25704`); `xfamscope`'s two edits are in `gate_crossfamily.sh:173-193` and `:207-218`; `m437rtmp` owes no code, and its scope statement is `OUTSTANDING_BUGS.md:5806-5810` with the `R:` unlink at `diskimage.c:177-182`. Evidence: `regress/artifacts/armmsrmodekill/` -- the panels (`panel_pass1_20261007` .. `panel_pass2r5_20261009`), the Opus 5.5 seat's answers and measurements (`witness_20261007/opus_*.md`,
`opus_pass2*_2026100*/`), the kill tables (`killtable_20261007/` .. `killtable5_20261008/`), and agy's MMU research
in `regress/artifacts/armmmuvehicle/`.

### `armusrstop` (MEDIUM, cpu) — a USR- or SYS-mode guest stops the CPU: `LDM {..pc}^` and `MSR SPSR_x` reach default: arms that set `running = 0`

USR32 and SYS32 have no SPSR, and two guest instructions select one by switching on the CURRENT mode with no arm for
them: `arm_pop`'s `^` restore (`bdt_load: unimplemented mode %i`, then `cpu->running = 0; next_ic = &nothing_call;
return;`) and `msr_imm_spsr` (`msr_spsr: unimplemented mode %i`, a pc sync, then `cpu->running = 0`) -- both in
`src/cpus/cpu_arm_instr.c`, found by `grep -n 'unimplemented mode' src/cpus/cpu_arm_instr.c`.  A guest reaches either
from USR32 with no debugger: one `MSR CPSR_c,#0x10` (a modelled mode, accepted) and then the instruction.  The
architecture makes an SPSR access from USR/SYS UNPREDICTABLE, which "must not halt or hang the processor"
(`_scratchpad/ddi0100i.txt:45064`).  `running = 0` stops THIS CPU; with no other CPU running, emulation ends.  `mrs_spsr`'s
`default:` is the third arm of the shape but answers 0 for USR/SYS and is reached only after a debugger `cpsr=` plant.
Found by the Opus 5.5 seat on #562's pass 1 (`witness_20261007/opus_pass1.md`); filed as its own row by owner ruling,
2026-10-07.  NOT witnessed; the rung-3 attempt is owed and is cheap -- `regress/arm_msrmode_probe.py`'s vehicle already
enters modes by MSR.  Option set: decline (no SPSR to read: leave CPSR unchanged, or treat `^` as a plain load) +
latched announce is the #562 shape; ARMv7 explicitly permits UNDEFINED (`_scratchpad/ddi0406.txt:143212`) --
earlier-version permission is not established here.

### `armspsrthumb` (MEDIUM, cpu) — an SPSR restore that sets T keeps decoding ARM words until the run loop is next entered

Both SPSR restores #562 touched (`arm_pop`'s `^`, the DPI S-to-PC in `cpu_arm_instr_dpi.c`) assign the whole SPSR to
CPSR, T included -- but the Thumb interpreter is chosen only at the ENTRY of the dyntrans run function
(`cpu_dyntrans.c`: `if (cpu->cd.arm.cpsr & ARM_FLAG_T) { arm_cpu_interpret_thumb_SLOW(cpu); return 1; }`).  The DPI path
breaks out of the loop (`abortdyntrans_call`) only for an ODD destination PC; `arm_pop` never breaks out, and loads the
PC as `r[ARM_PC] & 0xfffffffc`, dropping bit 1 of a halfword-aligned Thumb address.  So after a restore that sets T,
the CPU can go on decoding ARM words from a word-aligned PC until the loop is next entered -- the CPSR word and the
decoder disagree for an unspecified stretch.  (Read from the source on 2026-10-08, not measured.)  Raised
by codex on #562's §F2 pass (disposition 6: "Mode filtering alone does not make applying T safe or coherent") and
disclosed in `arm_msrmode_probe.py`'s NOT CLAIMED list (T-bit / execution-state coherence on restore); filed as its own
row by owner ruling, 2026-10-07.  The probe's `tbit` row pins the T BIT's provenance through all three paths; it does not
claim the decoder follows it.  NOT witnessed.

### `armmmuvehicle` (MEDIUM, harness) — a rung-3 ARM vehicle with the MMU ON, owed before `armthumbabortkill`

`armthumbabortkill`'s own reopen condition is "an MMU-on ARM vehicle built for a higher-ranked defect"; #562's probe
runs with the MMU off, so it does not meet it.  Owner ruling 2026-10-07: build this first, then `armthumbabortkill`.
agy's read-only research (`regress/artifacts/armmmuvehicle/agy_research_20261008.txt`; facts to re-derive, not
agreement): CP15 c1/c2/c3 cannot be set from the debugger, so the guest must `mcr` them; `put` writes VIRTUAL memory;
`step` keeps working with the MMU on; a one-section map is a descriptor 0x00000c02 at a 16 KB-aligned TTB with DACR 1;
and the vehicle MUST map the exception vectors, or a fault reaches `cpu_dyntrans.c`'s "could not find physical address
of the exception handler" `exit(1)` (`alphaifetchkill`). [2026-11-02, records: refuted by measurement -- the `armvecrecurse` entry below records that this exit never appears: `arm_exception()` ends in `quick_pc_to_pointers()` (987cb596 `cpu_arm.c:780-783`), whose failed translation takes another prefetch abort, so a fault with the vectors unmapped recurses until the emulator process ends]  It also found no per-CPU Thumb capability flag -- the T bit
alone selects the Thumb interpreter -- which answers this row's open question about testarm's default SA1110.  Of the
process kills and CPU stops agy listed on that path, these match existing rows by their titles: `armdesc3kill`,
`armdacr2kill`, `armcp15cp14exits`, `armendianexit`, `qharmexalign`, `alphaifetchkill`.  The mapping is NOT complete
and two of agy's entries were wrong as given (GPT-6 Astra's confirmation of #562): `armsa1110areset` is the reset
alignment-control default, not the `ARM_EXCEPTION_RESET` exit agy listed -- that exit may be unfiled -- and the CPU
stop agy called `wfi` in `cpu_arm_instr.c` is `X(reboot)`.  Witness kind for its round: `harness:`.

### `armmsrmodedebt` (LOW, detector) — #562's measured residue: latch-clear cells, msr label x latch, the cached translation; with measured closures for the five restore-flag escapes and the cached-translation mutants

commit, file the rest):

* **Latch-CLEAR x bits 31:8 at the restores.**  Each grid session has ONE latch-clear decline (its first), and every
  latch-clear restore decline that reads back the whole CPSR has SPSR bits 31:8 SET while the old CPSR's are 0 -- so
  `N_pop_forceN_first`, `N_dpi_forceN_first`, `N_pop_orold_first`, `N_dpi_orold_first` and `E_pop_forceN_clracc` all
  score 47/47 (the force-0 twins are killed, 41/47).  The bodies never test bits 31:8, so these sit outside the
  joint-cell floor; the contract claimed them and was narrowed comment-only.  **MEASURED CLOSURE:** move one
  polarity-2 accept and the first polarity-2 decline to the front of the DPI and pop grid sessions -- no observation
  added, no expected value changed: the fix stays 47/47 and all five go red at 46/47 (`KTR5W2_*.out`,
  `probe47r.py`, `mk_probe47r.py`).  It shifts carriers (`N_pop_clrN_first` 41/47 -> 42/47), so it owes a FULL
  re-table and its own pass.
* **msr label x latch.**  msr has no latch-clear decline at IRQ, ABT, UND or SYS (`msr lbl`'s first decline is FIQ's),
  and the restores' latch-clear mode-bit cells at IRQ/bit 1, ABT/bits 0-2 and UND/bits 0,1,3 are unobserved --
  `M_msr_clr0f_irq_first` and `M_msr_skip_irq_first` 47/47.  Static count, codex and the Opus seat agreeing: 126 of
  160 label x latch x mode-bit cells observed.
* **The cached translation (`M_msr_argmask`, 47/47).**  None of the shipped 47 rows detects a write to `ic->arg[]`:
  each of their re-executions crosses a debugger interaction, and `debugger()` clears every dyntrans translation when
  it interacts.  **MEASURED CLOSURE:** a 48th row that re-executes
  ONE translated register-form MSR and one translated `msr cpsr_c,#0x14` inside a single `step 72` (eight passes):
  fix 48/48, `M_msr_argmask` 47/48, `M_msr_arg0cur` (the immediate form's twin) 47/48, HEAD 18/48 (`probe48.py`,

* **`grid cov` asserts the G1 table only.**  Dropping 0x18-0x1a from G3, or SYS from the msr labels, still leaves it at
  0 uncovered (`gridcov_scope.py`); asserting the G2/G3/G4 sets in `grid cov` is cheap.
* **Gate 14 parser:** a dead vehicle (`CONTROL=DEAD` prints no REDS line) is reported as malformed output -- it fails

### `headerstaleobj` (MEDIUM, harness) — a HEADER change leaves stale objects, and neither propagation path nor the two-part clearance can see them

Found by #562's own gate 14.  #562 inserted `uint32_t mode_warned` into `struct arm_cpu` (`src/include/cpu_arm.h`)
ahead of `i80321_inten`/`i80321_isrc`, `tmr0`, `tmr0_irq`/`tmr1_irq` and `tisr`.  This build tracks no header
dependencies, and every #562 build rebuilt only `src/cpus/*.o` -- the carrier's recipe, the round's propagation script
and every kill-table clone -- so each linked a `dev_i80321.o` compiled against the OLD layout.  The device set `isrc` at
the old offset and the guest read 0: gate 14's xscale section (`-E iq80321`) went red, `ANCHOR_ISRC` and `ANCHOR_EXC`,
28/30, while a HEAD build scored 30/30 -- each twice (`regress/artifacts/armmsrmodekill/gate14_20261009/xscale_ab.out`).
**The two-part clearance PASSED on all three trees**: every binary was newer than every edited source.
The repo's `tools/propagate_all_trees.sh` can relink and report clearance success while header-dependent objects stay
stale: `rm -f "${F%.c}.o"` deletes nothing for a `.h`, and the link recipe relinks unconditionally (GPT-6 Astra's
confirmation; this entry first said the tool would report the header stale -- false).  Scope, measured by grep:
`dev_i80321.c` is the only object outside `src/cpus` that reads a field after the insertion point, and `cd` is the
last member of `struct cpu`, so no subsequent `struct cpu` member shifted and every other non-CPU ARM access precedes
the insertion; #562's
msrmode probe drives `-E testarm`, which attaches no i80321, so its kill tables are unaffected.  #562 itself was
rebuilt clean (every object deleted) before its final gate run.  Owed: when a propagated path is a header, delete every
object that includes it (or every object) and rebuild; and a THIRD clearance part -- no object older than any edited
header -- in the tool and in the checkpoint step.

### `armvecrecurse` (HIGH, cpu) — an abort with the vector page unmapped recurses until the HOST process dies

MEASURED by the Opus 5.5 seat on `armmmuvehicle`'s pass 1 (unmodified `-E testarm`, MMU on, section 0 through a coarse
table whose page 0 is unmapped, one data abort): **47,591 nested `{ arm memory fault ...}` lines and "Exception caused no
mode change?" warnings in 10.6 s, then signal 11** (`regress/artifacts/armmmuvehicle/pass1_20261009/opus5/opus5_meas/meas3_base.out`: `bytes=10473809 faults=47591 status=signal(11) elapsed=10.6s`, the status from `waitpid`; `T3_vec_unmapped.txt` beside it is the script's head-and-tail excerpt of that transcript).  The `cpu_dyntrans.c` exit "could not find physical address of the
exception handler" never appears: `arm_exception()` ends in `quick_pc_to_pointers()`, whose failed translation raises
`arm_exception(PREF_ABT)` again before the generic lookup's second chance runs -- unbounded recursion.  A guest that
unmaps its own vectors and takes any abort ends the emulator.  Guest-drivable process death, so it ranks above the
fidelity rows; the vehicle (`armmmuvehicle`) is its witness path.  The unlatched diagnostics are also a flood.

### `sysasicbitmask31` (LOW, device header) — `SYSASIC_EVENT_TO_BITMASK` is a signed `1 << 31` for events 31, 63 and 95

`src/include/thirdparty/dreamcast_sysasicvar.h`: `SYSASIC_EVENT_TO_BITMASK(e)` is `(1 << ((e) & 31))`.  For e = 31,
63 and 95 -- INSIDE the `[0,95]` domain `SYSASIC_EVENT_RANGE_OK` enforces -- that is a signed left shift into the sign
bit, undefined in C99; GCC yields `0xffffffff80000000` and UBSan reports it (both seats, MEASURED).  LATENT: no defined
event satisfies `e & 31 == 31`.  The ledger's recorded remedy (`+ SYSASIC_EVENT_RANGE_OK(e)`) is INERT for this --
it compiles at 31.  The fix is `1u << ((e) & 31)`; the 21 defined events' masks are unchanged.  Its witness can only
be `detector:` -- a compile-and-run UBSan row, red on `1 <<` and green on `1u <<` (both seats measured both ways) --
with the rung-3 attempt recorded as impossible by construction while no defined event has `e & 31 == 31` (a guest
path would need a new raise site, which is laundering).  Provenance: the kimi substitute and codex on `#466`'s pass 2
(2026-08-26).

### `armusrwarmap` (MEDIUM, cpu) — a USR-mode access through a translation warmed by a privileged access skips the AP check

ARM dyntrans: `cpu_arm_instr_loadstore.c`'s fast path indexes `host_load`/`host_store` by virtual page alone and
consults `is_userpage` only for the LDRT/STRT forms; nothing invalidates on a mode change.  MEASURED by Fable 5.1
(2026-10-09, `-E testarm` with the MMU on): in ONE `step N`, a privileged `LDR` of an AP=0 section (privileged
read-only under the reset S bit) succeeds and warms the page; `MSR CPSR_c,#0x10`; the same `LDR` in USR32 is SERVED
(no abort).  Cold, the USR load takes the architectural permission fault (FSR `0x0d`).  Red on HEAD, so it is not a
vehicle row; its own round, with `armmmuvehicle` as the vehicle and Fable's session S8 as the witness shape.

### `armthumbabtlr` (MEDIUM, cpu) — Thumb-state aborts save the wrong return address (data abort +7, prefetch abort +3)

`cpu_arm.c` `arm_exception()`: `retaddr = cpu->pc` (`+ 4` for a data abort) `+ (T ? 2 : 4)`, and in Thumb state
`cpu->pc` carries bit 0.  MEASURED by Fable 5.1 (2026-10-09): a Thumb `LDR` to an unmapped VA gives `LR_abt` =
instruction + 7, and a Thumb `BX` to an unmapped VA gives target + 3, where DDI 0100I gives + 8 (A2.6.6) and + 4
(A2.6.5) in both states.  IRQ and FIQ are also "+ 4 in both states", so the `T ? 2 : 4` term is right only for
SWI/UND.  grok read the same defect the same day.  A sibling of `armthumbabortkill` (same Thumb abort path) and
reachable only with the MMU on -- after `armmmuvehicle`.

### 2026-10-20 -- two PowerPC shift rows filed, both witnessed on HEAD 1a59a47e

* **`ppcshiftwide` (HIGH, open)** -- `X(slw)`/`X(srw)`/`X(sraw)` mask the shift amount `& 31`: Book I gives 0 (slw,
  srw) or 64 sign bits with CA = the sign (sraw) for shift amounts 32..63, the multi-word shift idiom compilers emit for
  `long long` on 32-bit PowerPC; in the 64-bit build slw and srw also leak into RA's high word.  Rung-3 witness
  `regress/artifacts/ppcshiftwide/witness_20261020/shift_witness.py`: 3/15 on HEAD (PPC970 and PPC603), the sh4
  control correct on PPC603.  Argon confirmed all twelve failing rows against Book I and sketched the fixes.
* **`ppcsrdmissing` (HIGH, open)** -- srd, srad and sradi have no decoder case; a 64-bit guest executing one stops the
  emulation ("cpu: UNIMPLEMENTED instruction", "emul: All machines stopped").  Witness
  `regress/artifacts/ppcshiftwide/witness_20261020/srd_witness.py`; the sld control runs.
* Whether ppcrlwhighhalf's 2026-10-09 owner block ("witness only") reaches these rows is the owner's call.


### 2026-10-21 -- `vmedefaultkill` fixed by `#568`; `vmewidthlanes` widened; three rows filed

* **`vmedefaultkill` (HIGH) -- FIXED by `#568`.**  `dev_vme.c`'s `default:` no longer ends the emulator: the 26
  header-named VME2 registers the model does not implement DECLINE with one latched announce per register (owner
  2026-10-09), and every other unmatched offset returns 0, which `memory_rw.c` turns into the m88k data-access exception
  for a guest data load or store (owner 2026-09-11 for the unnamed word starts; sub-word starts the same way only as
  an interim, which `vmewidthlanes` decides).  Rung-3 witness `regress/artifacts/vmedefaultkill/witness_20261020/`
  (7 of 7 guest access sites rc 1 on HEAD 5dbc000e); detector `regress/vme_default_probe.py` (38 rows), gated in gate 14
  and pinned at 38; kill table 2 and its addenda 2b, 2c and 2d in `regress/artifacts/vmedefaultkill/killtable2_20261021/`; the
  repair chain closed on the repair-diff pass (`r1_20261021/`).
* **`vmewidthlanes` (LOW, open)** -- widened: population-2 SUB-WORD starts (the probe pins three interims --
  `p3 interim`, `p2 int byte`, `p2 int half` -- that this row will re-derive) and cased-word `ld.d`/`st.d` lane
  placement (a 32-bit register served into, or stored from, the wrong half of an 8-byte access at 0x00, 0x60, 0x88).
* **`vmewarnedbit` (LOW, open)** -- new.  `dev_vme.c` writes its latch index `1ULL << (relative_addr >> 2)` twice, in
  the test and in the set; one shared macro (`dev_pcc2.c`'s shape) would make a one-sided index edit impossible and a
  two-sided relabel one edit.  D5 of `#568`'s pass-2 adjudication, filed rather than built.  The index edits kill table 2 built are
  TWO-sided -- M_LATCHONE (a constant index in both) and M_ONENARROW (a 32-bit literal in both) -- and die of a
  collision and an overflow; a ONE-sided edit (test and set disagreeing) was not built, only derived to re-announce;
  the two-sided relabels the repair-diff pass named (`1ULL` -> `2ULL`, `(relative_addr >> 2) ^ 1`) are equivalents.
* **`vmeprobedebt` (LOW, open)** -- new.  Three rows of `regress/vme_default_probe.py` carry no own-channel kill in kill
  table 2: `free quiet` (no leg reds it), `vbr rt` and `t1count inc` (red only as dependents of M_DROPTCTL).  The absent
  legs: a cased arm's `debug()` -> `fatal()` promotion; a VBR write-path break; a T1COUNT write-path break.  Also the
  clause-(e) cells the probe's NOT CLAIMED list names: the store-data slice (28 of 64 bits clear in every store value;
  bit 1 measured 38/38 in table 2b), the latch set skipped for a zero store (M_ZEROSET, 38/38 in table 2d: the sampled
  zero pins the announce's form, not the set), and `default:` serving 0xffd..0xfff (M_DFLTFFC, 38/38).  Coverage debt,
  ranked below live defects.
* **`m88kpsrmxm` (MED, open)** -- new.  A guest that sets PSR.MXM STOPS THE EMULATED CPU: `src/cpus/cpu_m88k.c`'s PSR
  write prints `stcr: TODO: MXM support` at ERROR level and sets `cpu->running = false` (the `M88K_PSR_MXM` arm of the
  control-register store).  The MC88100 manual (`_scratchpad/mc88100.txt:2047-2052`, `:9243-9245`) makes MXM the
  misaligned-access exception MASK: when set, a misaligned access does not trap and the processor rounds the address
  down to a consistent boundary.  Named on `#568`'s pass 1 (Fable) as an unmodelled divergence and adjudicated FILE,
  LOW, before anyone read the arm; the arm halts, so it is filed MED.  Whether an in-tree guest sets MXM is not
  established -- the reachability question that ranks it.  *[2026-10-22: alias `m88kmxmkill` (filed 2026-09-06 from #502, the same halt) is consolidated here; MED confirmed -- ADJ_RULINGS.md B T136.]*

### 2026-10-21 -- the of.c exit family scoped (Argon); `ofemulnodata`'s title corrected; `armrebootmagic` filed

* **`ofemulnodata` / `ofpeerexit` / `ofopenexit` (HIGH, open)** -- Argon's packet-fed scoping (`regress/artifacts/ofemulnodata/argon_scope_20261021/`, a reading,
  not a measurement): three rounds, not one -- of.c:1100, :394 and :448 differ in semantic class, fix design and
  detector; of.c:549, :577, :1120 and :1201 are unreachable.  For of.c:1100 it proposes gating the magic word at
  the two DECODERS on `of_data != NULL`, so a machine without OpenFirmware takes the architectural SWI / system
  call -- an early return inside `of_emul` would send the guest to its link register.  `ofemulnodata`'s title said
  `of_data` is NULL "on every machine except macppc"; macppc without PROM emulation is NULL too
  (`machine_macppc.c` returns before `of_emul_init`) -- corrected.
* **`armrebootmagic` (MED, open)** -- new.  The ARM decoder routes the word 0xef8c64eb to `X(reboot)`
  (`cpu->running = 0`) on every ARM machine at any privilege level; `machine_cats.c` plants it as the cats PROM's
  reboot entry.  One user-mode instruction stops the emulated CPU instead of taking the SWI it encodes.  No
  witness yet (READ at 7f48ea10).

byte-identical).  It ships `regress/m88k_buserr_probe.py`, a 31-row rung-3 detector on unmodified mvme187 and luna-88k

with its question; Argon not fired on pass 1 (seat failure) [corrected 2026-11-02, records: said "Argon not fired" with no pass named; it fired on pass 2 through agy, as the pass-2 list above and `#570`'s CHANGELOG block say].  The row's witness is the frozen rung-3 probe

### 2026-10-24 -- `ppcdsformxo` fixed by `#571` (held for Fable); `ppcdisasmxo`, `ppcdisasmfpupd`, `ppcldxabsent`, `ppc64on32gate` and `wiringwitnessclass` filed

`#571` makes `src/cpus/cpu_ppc_instr.c`'s D/DS-form arm decode primary opcodes 58 and 62 as DS forms: the two case
bodies re-assign the shared `imm` to `(int16_t)(iword & ~3)` -- EXTS(DS || 0b00), the XO bits no longer part of the
displacement -- and dispatch on `iword & 3`: `ld` / `ldu` (RA <- EA) / `lwa` (the sign-extended word, the existing
`ppc_instr_lwa` handler) and `std` / `stdu`, the reserved encodings (58 with XO 3, 62 with XO 2 or 3) taking the arm's
bare `goto bad` (the common tail's `UNIMPLEMENTED instruction` stop) and `ldu`/`stdu` with RA = 0 reaching the arm's
existing `ra == 0 && update` guard.  Before it every `ldu` loaded from EA+1 and performed no base update, every `lwa` loaded a DOUBLEWORD
from EA+2, and every `stdu` -- the instruction every PowerPC64 stack frame is pushed with -- stored at EA+1 and left the
stack pointer.  No handler changed (every form selects a slot the generated table already holds); the shared
assignment and the other 22 opcodes of the arm are untouched; 32-bit CPUs are disclosed (illegal opcodes, decoded
through the same arm, so their MODE32 decode and refusal behaviour change with this fix too; no width test -- filed as
`ppc64on32gate`).  It ships `regress/ppc_dsform_probe.py`,
a 39-row rung-3 detector on the unmodified `bareppc -M 64` (seven debugger-stepped guest sessions -- the loads, the stores
with every destination read back by the debugger's dump, five stop sessions -- and the bogus-machine control; every word from the
probe's own encoder; a census of all 108 placed words against the tree's current disassembler text), gated in gate 13
with every row identity, the four protocol keys and the census pinned.  Measured in
`regress/artifacts/ppcdsformxo/table1_20261024/` (pre-fix 22/39 with the 17 symptom rows red for the reason under test
-- the store half's clause-(a) artifact; fixed 39/39; the frozen 8-row witness 8/8; 16 of 16 kill-table legs red, 14 at
their written prediction, the identity body measured 17/39; clearance clean and fresh on every build tree; gate 13
PASS with 193 checks, the `#571` block 53 of 53).  Panel: Astra, Grok, Argon (through agy), GLM 5.3 and DeepSeek on
pass 1 (five READY WITH CHANGES, DeepSeek NOT READY twice on the 32-bit test and the store rows), adjudicated by Astra
(AMEND) and by Grok (AMEND; the one adjudicator disagreement -- the DS = 0 x RA = 0 refusal cells -- ruled for Grok on
the carrier's floor bound); pass 2 on the diff by the same five seats (seven answers, all LAND WITH CHANGES: records-only changes and three
docstring/comment-only detector revisions, each re-measured; Argon's Q2 confabulated and discounted), F2 adjudicated by Astra and
Grok (both AMEND, LANDING GO WITH THE CHANGES NAMED -- applied: the second and third docstring/comment-only detector revisions (each re-measured), the design row's severity left unset, two more PRETABLE claims in the erratum, the drafts' base-update wording; Astra's exact-text readings of the landed texts (`adj/final/codex_t2final*.txt`): reading 1 named twelve record corrections -- ten completed, one left incomplete and one wrongly rejected (the frozen witness copy's MANIFEST class: the checker's WITNESS/DETECTOR line governs, the copy asserts the repaired property, so it is CLASS_RESEARCH, and the mis-classed precedents are filed as wiringwitnessclass); reading 2 named ten -- nine applied, one (the stale count sentences) left incomplete; reading 3 named seven, applied; each later reading is recorded in PASS2_RULINGS.md, and the reading that says GO is the clearance this commit rests on); Fable HELD with its question. * **`ppcdisasmxo` (LOW, open)** -- new.  cpus/cpu_ppc.c:1495-1517: the disassembler folds the XO bits into the
  displacement and prints `ld`/`std` for every opcode-58/62 word (`ldu r5,-96(r21)` appears as `ld r5,-95(r21)`);

### 2026-10-24 -- `wdclbaaddr` fixed by `#572` (held for Fable); `wdclbaadvertise`, `wdcmediastatus` and `wdclbaimage` filed

`#572` makes `src/devices/dev_wdc.c` decode the select byte's LBA flag from bit 6 (`WDSD_LBA`; it was bit 5, which the
classic CHS select byte 0xa0 also sets), keeps bits 7 and 5 in the field renamed `sdh_resv` so the readback stays
byte-exact for all 256 values, and enables the LBA28 address arm in both `wdc__read()` and `wdc__write()` with the product
in 64-bit arithmetic (`512 * (int64_t)(((head & 0xf) << 24) + (cyl << 8) + sector)` -- the compiled-out `int` form
overflows for any nonzero head nibble); the two `printf`s in the old `#if 0` blocks are deleted.  Before it every LBA-mode
READ/WRITE SECTORS was served from the CHS reading of the same taskfile bytes (LBA 70 -> CHS sector 70 = index 69; LBA 256
-> index H*S-1; LBA 0 -> a negative offset, zeros).  IDENTIFY word 49 stays 0: LBA28 is honoured, not advertised -- the
advertisement is a guest-visible change on every word-49-honouring guest and has no measured warrant yet (the boot
battery cannot supply one: only landisk's optional all-zero disk reaches this model; the "five rigs" sentence in the
round's first design text was false and is retracted).  It ships `regress/wdc_lba_probe.py`, a 33-row
rung-3 detector on the unmodified `evbmips -e malta` (seven debugger-driven guest sessions on a tagged
4096-sector image: IDENTIFY, CHS reads, select-byte readbacks, LBA reads including head 1 and cylinder-high 1, and one write
session reading back both candidate destinations through valid CHS triples; every word from the probe's encoders, checked
against the disassembler; a `GATE` single-leg mode), gated in gate 10 beside `wdc_altdigin_probe.py` with the denominator
pinned by equality.  Measured in `regress/artifacts/wdclbaaddr/` (the rung-3 witness at 17:03 before any edit: 19/19 against
the HEAD column, the five LBA rows red against the FIX wants; the revised detector's two legs base 33/33 vs HEAD and fix 33/33 vs FIX; the frozen witness's fixed leg 19/19; GATE 33/33 CONTROL=OK; the dead run 0/33 CONTROL=FAIL; kill tables 18/18 and 9/9 killed plus the clause-(b) readback mutant 30/33, the two disclosed survivors V12 (equivalent) and V7 (blind on this image); gate 10 run end to end with the block in place; clearance clean and fresh on the trees touched).  Panel: Astra, Grok, Argon (through agy),
GLM 5.3 and DeepSeek on pass 1 (six READY WITH CHANGES, DeepSeek Q1-2 NOT READY on detector-spec points, all adopted;
Argon's confabulated wiring/trace sections not credited), adjudicated by Astra (CONFIRM WITH CHANGES) and Grok (CONFIRM
WITH CHANGES, one disposition corrected); pass 2 on the diff by the same five seats (seven answers, six LAND WITH CHANGES and one READY TO LAND; no product-code defect; fourteen record/contract findings applied, the clause-(b) readback mutant built and killed, the gate-10 block run end to end before landing -- the five wdc_lba checks OK, 33/33 CONTROL=OK, sentinel once; the gate's own verdict FAIL 1 of 405 on the peer session's uncommitted 62-row gdrom_default probe against HEAD's 60-row pin, not this round's file; PMAX = the fix clone, provenance measured in CLONE_PROVENANCE.txt; GATE10_RUN.txt), F2 adjudicated by Astra (CONFIRM WITH CHANGES) and Grok (CONFIRM WITH CHANGES); Fable HELD with its question.  `row_no_lba_claim()` in
`regress/diff_wdc_identify.c` and gate 2's comment re-authored in the same change (the assertion and the pin unchanged).
Not claimed: that any guest now uses LBA; ATA-2 conformance of the interim; coverage of cylinder-high destinations, head
shifts that miss the file, drive 1, MULTI counts, the 48-bit commands; a generalisable detection of the unwidened product.
Noted for the next round that touches the ATAPI path, not edited here: the comment at `dev_wdc.c:1662` says nothing resets the
phase, while `wdc_new_command_reset()` clears `atapi_phase` at `:917` (Astra, pass 2).

### 2026-10-25 -- `#573` lecsrmask: the LANCE model's CSR3 store masked to its three implemented bits; the round NARROWED

* **`lecsrmask` (MED, WRONG-RESULT) -- NARROWED by `#573`; the ledger row stays `held` (the Fable question and the owner's roster
  question) and closes NARROWED when they are discharged.**  The research row proposed rpajarola `e108b54`'s three masks.
  Only the CSR3 mask (`& 0x0007`) is established for the Am7990 the model names: its manual (TM1986 1734) says bits 15:3 "read as
  0" for CSR3 and for RAP (1539) and NOT for CSR1 bit 0 ("Must be zero", 1749) or CSR2 15:8 (bare "Reserved.", 1695); MAME keeps
  CSR1/CSR2 writable on the Am7990 for a MIPS RS2030 diagnostic's sake; the C-LANCE text reads CSR2's reserved bits as zero and says
  only "Must be zero" for CSR1 bit 0.  So CSR1 and CSR2 retain the model's existing behaviour (stored whole), pinned by three
  contract rows, and their read-back question is the new row below.  Witness: rung 3 on the unmodified `pmax -e 3100`
  (`regress/artifacts/lecsrmask/witness_20261025/`); detector `regress/le_csrmask_probe.py` (20 rows, `gate_arm.sh`); floor legs
  measured in `pass1_20261025/final_055141/` -- (a) the pre-fix build L0 17/20, (b) the BUILT reinstatement L4 17/20, (c) the null
  medium L3 0/20 -- and the fix legs L1 20/20, L2 20/20 + 20/20; the clause-(d) variant table OWED (below).
* **`lecsr12readback` (LOW, documented) -- new.**  CSR1 bit 0 and CSR2 bits 15:8 read-back: unspecified by the Am7990 manual;
  C-LANCE: CSR2 read-as-zero (1161-1163), CSR1 bit 0 "Must be zero" only (1138-1142); MAME `am79c90.cpp` stores CSR1 whole on
  both chips and CSR2 whole on the Am7990 ("MIPS RS2030 diagnostic requires these bits to be writable"); rpajarola `e108b54`
  masks all three for a 3MIN port this fork lacks ("which 3/ni/regs checks"), naming no chip.  A per-chip model flag (MAME's
  `type()`) is the port if a C-LANCE instance is ever added; the chip of the KN230, PMAD-AA and luna88k instances is unverified
  (the KN01 is the Am7990).  Not a defect of the Am7990 model as it stands.
* **`lestopgate` (LOW) -- new.**  Both manuals: CSR1-3 "Accessible only when the STOP bit of CSR0 is a ONE" (TM1986 1733; C-LANCE
  1123-1124, 1146-1147, 1197-1198); the model accepts reads and writes in either state (its comments, corrected by `#573`, keep the old
  comment's report that Ultrix accesses them with STOP set -- the in-spec case; with STOP clear both manuals say a read returns
  undefined data and a write is ignored: TM1986 1572-1582, C-LANCE 915-924).  Gating is a behaviour change owing its own witness.
* **`lecsr3stopclear` (LOW) -- new.**  "CSR3 is cleared by RESET or by setting the STOP bit in CSR0" (C-LANCE 1199-1200; TM1986
  2854); the model clears CSR3 only at init.  And no preservation guarantee for CSR1/CSR2 across STOP: TM1986 1513 requires a reload,
  2853-2857 says "normally not affected ... recommended to reload", the Am79C90 datasheet's Table B-1 (3411, right column; 3686-3687) characterises the Am7990
  as NOT preserving them -- the sources differ; all three readings recorded, no replacement value asserted.  The model leaves
  CSR1-3 untouched by a STOP write (CSR3 never cleared, CSR1/CSR2 trivially kept); `#573` adds no STOP behaviour.  Research row 9 (CSR0 STOP/STRT) does not carry this.
* **`lediagfmt` (LOW, records/robustness) -- new.**  `dev_le.c` passes `uint64_t` values to narrower conversions: `idata` to `%i`
  (1019-1020), `relative_addr`/`odata` to `%x` (1039-1040), the SRAM offset to `%05x` (911, 921) (lines of 9ac43a17^, the pre-#573 file; at 987cb596 `%i` :1039-1040, `0x%06x`/`0x%08x` :1059-1060, `%05x` :928, :938) -- a variadic-format mismatch
  (undefined under C99 7.19.6.1p9; prints the low bits on this ABI).  Not this round's edit.
* **`lecsr3inert` (LOW, documented) -- new.**  The three implemented CSR3 bits (BSWP, ACON, BCON -- DMA byte lanes and bus
  signalling) are stored and never consulted by the model; `#573` pins their read-back only.
* **`srclistsubdir` (LOW, carrier) -- new.**  The carrier's primary-source inventory is derived by `ls _scratchpad/*.pdf`, which does
  not descend into `_scratchpad/lance/` (two Am7990/Am79C90 manuals and four reference drivers, present since 2026-07-25); this

**MED (37)**

#### `mipseidicu0` (MED, WRONG-RESULT) -- the Release-2 EI/DI handler writes Status.IE with no cop0 availability check, so user mode gets no Coprocessor Unusable exception
src/cpus/cpu_mips_instr.c:2719-2726 at 987cb596: `X(ei_or_di)` copies Status into rt and then sets or clears `STATUS_IE` (`:2721-2725`) without calling `cop0_availability_check()`, so a user-mode EI or DI with CU0 clear changes the interrupt enable where the manual signals a Coprocessor Unusable exception (`mips32_volII.txt:597`, `:630`); the R5900 forms do make the check (`:3241`, `:3248`). Reach: user mode on the Release-2 CPUs (4KEc, 24KEc, 5KE; the decode gate is `:4984-4985`); a sibling of `mipscop0cpu`. Source: CODE_CANDIDATES_v2.md C4 and ASTRA_VS_FABLE.md C4 (consensus FILE). Witness: none (research filing).

#### `mipscop3isa3` (MED, WRONG-RESULT) -- on ISA III CPUs opcode 0x13 raises Coprocessor Unusable for coprocessor 3, where MIPS III removed COP3 and a Reserved Instruction exception is owed
src/cpus/cpu_mips_instr.c:5139-5142 at 987cb596: the opcode-0x13 arm installs a Coprocessor Unusable exception for coprocessor 3 (`instr(cpu)`, `arg[0] = 3`) whenever `coproc[3]` is NULL, with no ISA-level test. MIPS III removed the Coprocessor 3 instructions (`mips-iv.txt:1366`; Table A-43 at `:1426`), so on an ISA III CPU the word is reserved and a Reserved Instruction exception (RI) is owed. Reach: user mode on ISA III CPUs off the pmax machines (the arc machine's R4000/R4400); the MIPS IV/64 half of this opcode is `mipscop1xcpu`. Source: CODE_CANDIDATES_v2.md N18 and ASTRA_VS_FABLE.md N18 (consensus FILE). Witness: none (research filing).

#### `mipscop3pmaxstop` (MED, CPU-STOP) -- every pmax machine allocates coproc[3], so every COP3 word except 0x4d00ffff reaches goto bad with no Status.CU3 test
src/cpus/cpu_mips_instr.c:5145-5152 at 987cb596: on the pmax machines `coproc[3]` exists (`src/machines/machine_pmax.c:81`, `:170`), so the arm skips its Coprocessor Unusable branch, and any COP3 word other than the R2020 write-buffer word `0x4d00ffff` prints `COP3 iword=` and takes `goto bad` (`:5150-5152`), which stops the emulated CPU (`cpu_dyntrans.c:2014`). With Status.CU3 clear a Coprocessor Unusable exception is owed (`mips-iv.txt:236`); what a CU3-enabled word owes is not established (Astra's narrowing, P3:15). Reach: any privilege on the pmax machines, the pmax rig included. Source: CODE_CANDIDATES_v2.md N19 and ASTRA_VS_FABLE.md N19 (consensus FILE). Witness: none (research filing).

#### `mipsllzero` (MED, CPU-STOP) -- a load-linked into $zero prints HM... unusual load linked and reaches goto bad, a legal if unusual encoding on ISA II and later
src/cpus/cpu_mips_instr.c:5486-5490 at 987cb596: LL and LLD with rt = $zero print `HM... unusual load linked` and take `goto bad`, which stops the emulated CPU. The encoding is legal (`mips64_volII.txt:1023`, `:1031`): the load and its link must still happen, with the loaded value discarded, and execution must not stop (Astra P3:17). Reach: any privilege on ISA II and later CPUs (LLD on the 64-bit ones). Source: CODE_CANDIDATES_v2.md N20 and ASTRA_VS_FABLE.md N20 (consensus FILE). Witness: none (research filing).

#### `mipsspecialrsvd` (MED, CPU-STOP) -- reserved SPECIAL function codes reach the SPECIAL default goto bad instead of raising RI
src/cpus/cpu_mips_instr.c:4679 at 987cb596: the SPECIAL switch has no case for the reserved function codes 0x05, 0x0e, 0x15, 0x35, 0x37, 0x39 and 0x3d (and 0x28/0x29 off the R5900), so each takes `default:goto bad;` and stops the emulated CPU, where a reserved encoding owes a Reserved Instruction exception (RI). On the R5900, 0x28/0x29 are its MFSA/MTSA (`opcodes_mips.h:209-210`, never decoded); they reach the same default and are left to the held R5900 MMI/MFSA/MTSA widening. Reach: user mode on every MIPS CPU; MOVCI (0x01) is `mipsmovciundec`. Source: CODE_CANDIDATES_v2.md N21 and ASTRA_VS_FABLE.md N21 (consensus FILE). Witness: none (research filing).

#### `mipsspecial2rsvd` (MED, CPU-STOP) -- on MIPS32/64 CPUs SDBBP and the reserved SPECIAL2 codes reach the default goto bad while the model has no EJTAG, where RI is owed
src/cpus/cpu_mips_instr.c:5271 at 987cb596: on a MIPS32/64 CPU the SPECIAL2 switch decodes only MADD/MADDU/MSUB/MSUBU, MUL and CLZ/CLO/DCLZ/DCLO, so SDBBP and every reserved code take `default:goto bad;` and stop the emulated CPU. The model advertises no EJTAG (Config1 bit 1 is 0 at `cpu_mips_coproc.c:105`), and an unencoded or subsetted-out encoding must raise an exception (`mips64_volII.txt:2039`, `:129`), not stop. Reach: user mode on malta (5Kc), testmips/baremips (5KE) and vocore (24KEc). Source: CODE_CANDIDATES_v2.md N22 and ASTRA_VS_FABLE.md N22 (consensus FILE). Witness: none (research filing).

#### `mipsspecial3undec` (MED, CPU-STOP) -- DINS/DINSM/DINSU have no case and the reserved SPECIAL3 function codes reach the SPECIAL3 default goto bad
src/cpus/cpu_mips_instr.c:5699 at 987cb596: the SPECIAL3 switch has no case for DINS, DINSM or DINSU or for the reserved function codes, so each takes `default:goto bad;` and stops the emulated CPU. On the 5KE (MIPS64 Release 2) the DINS family is legal; on the MIPS32 Release-2 CPUs it is reserved, and a reserved code owes a Reserved Instruction exception (RI). Reach: user mode on the Release-2 CPUs (SPECIAL3 is gated to them at `:5584-5585`). The empty BSHFL/DBSHFL entries (`:5656`, `:5670`) are held separately and are not claimed here. Source: CODE_CANDIDATES_v2.md N23 and ASTRA_VS_FABLE.md N23 (consensus FILE). Witness: none (research filing).

#### `mipsdrotrundec` (MED, CPU-STOP) -- DROTR, DROTR32 and DROTRV are not decoded and reach goto bad
src/cpus/cpu_mips_instr.c:4446, :4461 at 987cb596: the Release-2 rotate decode handles only the 32-bit forms (SRL with rs = 1 as ROTR, `:4443-4444`; SRLV with sa = 1 as ROTRV, `:4455-4458`), so the doubleword rotates DROTR, DROTR32 and DROTRV fall to `default:goto bad;` and stop the emulated CPU. #### `mipsx64missing` (MED, WRONG-RESULT) -- DCLZ/DCLO, DEXT*, DSBH/DSHD and LWU set no x64, so these MIPS64-only instructions run on MIPS32 CPUs instead of raising RI
src/cpus/cpu_mips_instr.c:5262, :5435 at 987cb596: a 64-bit-only instruction is refused on a 32-bit CPU only when its decode sets `x64`, which the MODE32 tail (`:5712-5725`) turns into a Reserved Instruction exception (RI); DCLZ/DCLO (`:5262-5263`), DEXT/DEXTM/DEXTU (`:5625`), DSBH/DSHD (`:5665`, `:5668`) and LWU (`:5435`, with its own TODO at `:5427`) never set it, so they execute on 32-bit CPUs. Reach: user mode on the MIPS32 CPUs (the vocore 24KEc); LWU, a MIPS III load, also executes on ISA I/II CPUs, which the same tail covers (`cpu_mips.c:116-118`). Source: CODE_CANDIDATES_v2.md N26 and ASTRA_VS_FABLE.md N26 (consensus FILE). Witness: none (research filing).

#### `ppcxo64stop` (MED, CPU-STOP) -- on a 64-bit CPU model (PPC620, PPC970) nine XO arithmetic forms and addic/addic. reach `goto bad` keyed on the model width cpu->cd.ppc.bits rather than MSR[SF], so the emulated CPU stops in either mode
src/cpus/cpu_ppc_instr.c:5172, :4207 at 987cb596: `if (cpu->cd.ppc.bits == 64 && n64)` at :5172 refuses the nine XO forms that set n64 at :5120-5131 (divw, divwu, addc, adde, addme, addze, subfe, subfme, subfze), and `if (cpu->cd.ppc.bits == 64)` at :4207 refuses addic/addic.; both test the CPU model's width and never MSR[SF], so on PPC620 and PPC970 these instructions, which Book I defines in both modes, reach `goto bad` whatever mode the guest runs in. Reach: any privilege, from the first instruction, because cpu_ppc.c:102-103 leaves SF clear at start-up; bareppc and testppc default to PPC970 (src/machines/machine_test.c:448-456). Witness: none (research filing).

#### `ppcbranch32width` (MED, WRONG-RESULT) -- the CTR branch condition uses all 64 bits in 32-bit mode and branch targets are sign-extended into the high half that 32-bit mode clears

#### `ppcmull64` (MED, WRONG-RESULT) -- mulli stores a 32-bit product zero-extended and mullw a 32-bit product sign-extended, where Book I places the 64-bit product (mullw) or the low 64 bits of the 128-bit product (mulli) in RT on a 64-bit model
src/cpus/cpu_ppc_instr.c:2955-2957, :3199-3202 at 987cb596: X(mulli) truncates its product to 32 bits and zero-extends it (:2957) and X(mullw) keeps a 32-bit product and sign-extends it (:3201-3202); that is right for a 32-bit model (Book I's programming note, ppc_uisa_book1_v201.txt:3298-3300), but on a 64-bit model Book I v2.01 places the low 64 bits of the 128-bit product in RT for mulli (:3250-3256) and the full 64-bit product for mullw (:3279-3283). #### `ppcsrr1sf` (MED, WRONG-RESULT) -- SRR1 is saved as `msr & 0x87c0ffff`, which drops MSR[SF], so rfid restores SF=0 and truncates the PC
src/cpus/cpu_ppc.c:327 at 987cb596: ppc_exception() saves `cpu->cd.ppc.msr & 0x87c0ffff` into SRR1 (:327), a 32-bit mask that clears MSR[SF] (bit 63), and X(rfid) restores SF from SRR1 and then truncates the PC to 32 bits when SF is clear (cpu_ppc_instr.c:2845-2854), so a 64-bit guest that takes any interrupt returns in 32-bit mode at a truncated address. #### `ppcprogvector` (MED, MISSING-MECHANISM) -- the PPC model has no Program exception, so the undecoded-instruction rounds cannot deliver the architected Program interrupt and ppctwundec cannot close
src/include/cpu_ppc.h:251-257 at 987cb596: the exception list (:251-257) defines DSI, ISI, external, FP-unavailable, decrementer and system call only, and no ppc_exception() call in src/ raises a Program interrupt, so no instruction can take the architected Program interrupt (illegal instruction, privileged instruction in user mode, or trap); the undecoded ones stop the emulated CPU instead. Reach: every model; ppctwundec cannot close without it. Owner decision 9 (fable5_adj.md:338): keep the stops now and build the vector as its own round. Related: ppcenabldeliv; OUTSTANDING_BUGS.md:1747-1750 names 'the missing exception model'. Source: RANKED_OPEN_v2 row 127 and fable5_adj row 127 (FILE). Witness: none (research filing).

#### `m88kr0overflow` (MED, WRONG-RESULT) -- with destination r0, register add and the immediate add, sub, div, divu and mulu forms are replaced by a NOP, dropping their exceptions
src/cpus/cpu_m88k_instr.c:3733-3742,3155-3156 at 987cb596: the translator replaces a register-form instruction whose destination is r0 with `instr(nop)` unless its opcode is on the exemption list at `:3735-3741`, and register add (0x70, which traps on signed overflow at `:695-697`) is not on it; the immediate group does the same for every destination-r0 form at `:3155-3156`, so the overflow trap of add/sub (`:583-585`, `:637-639`), the divide-by-zero trap of div/divu (`:610-612`, `:622-624`) and the FPU-disabled exception of div/divu/mulu are lost. The MC88100 raises the integer-overflow exception whenever a signed result does not fit, whatever the destination (mc88100.txt:9305-9308). Reach: any privilege. Register sub never reaches this fold (no case 0x74; `m88kcarryundec`), and register div/divu are exempt. Source: CODE_CANDIDATES_v2 N39 and ASTRA_VS_FABLE N39 (FILE, as narrowed there). Witness: none (research filing).

#### `m88ksfudecodestop` (MED, CPU-STOP) -- undefined FP opcodes, SFU2-SFU7 opcodes, SFU 2-7 control-register forms and fxcr stop the CPU instead of raising the SFU precise exception

#### `nanencoding` (MED, WRONG-RESULT) -- a generated double NaN is stored with the host's sign and an all-ones fraction

#### `kn230irqwrong` (MED, WRONG-RESULT) -- the SII/LANCE condition (assert3) asserts and deasserts mips_irq_2 instead of mips_irq_3, so those interrupts arrive on MIPS interrupt 2 and the deassert can drop line 2 while a DZ or option-slot source is still pending
src/devices/dev_kn230.c:72-75,89-92 at 987cb596: The file's own comment says the KN230 interrupts MIPS interrupt 2 or 3 depending on the source (:143-144), and both lines are connected (:146-149), but kn230_interrupt_assert() and kn230_interrupt_deassert() drive mips_irq_2 for the SII/LANCE condition too (:74-75, :91-92). So SII and LANCE interrupts arrive on the wrong MIPS line, and when the SII/LANCE sources clear, :91-92 deasserts line 2 even while a DZ or option-slot source (assert2) is still pending. Guest-visible on the DEC MIPSMATE 5100 (src/machines/machine_pmax.c:663, :680). Source: _scratchpad/fanout_20261030/ARGON_FILE_AUDITS.md section 1 row 23. Witness: none (research filing).

#### `mpipimemmove` (MED, WRONG-RESULT) -- the IPI queue shift passes an element count to memmove() where a byte count is needed, so with two or more IPIs pending the entries left in the queue are wrong
src/devices/dev_mp.c:225-228 at 987cb596: On a DEV_MP_IPI_READ with more than one IPI pending, the queue is shifted down with memmove(&ipi[0], &ipi[1], n_pending) (:225-228), but ipi is an int array (:60), so only the first n_pending BYTES move, not n_pending entries, and the entries left in the queue are wrong (with two IPIs pending, the remaining entry keeps three of the old entry's bytes and gets one new one). The next IPI read then returns a wrong value. Guest-visible on the test machines that attach dev_mp (src/machines/machine_test.c:148, :333). Source: _scratchpad/fanout_20261030/ARGON_FILE_AUDITS.md section 1 row 29. Witness: none (research filing).

#### `mipstlbpfnhigh` (MED, WRONG-RESULT) -- pmask is uint32_t, so ~pmask zero-extends and ((pfn << pfn_shift) & ~pmask) clears physical-address bits 32 and up on every R4000-style TLB translation, while EntryLo carries a 24-bit page frame number

EntryLo's PFN field is 24 bits (src/include/cop0.h:63-64), so a TLB entry can name a physical address up to 2^36; every such translation is folded onto the low 4 GB. Guest-reachable through EntryLo. #### `ecoffclampdead` (MED, OOB-WRITE) -- the clamp of the last chunk to s_size is dead code because the next line reassigns len from fread(), so each section loads in whole chunk_size pieces and can write up to chunk_size - 1 bytes of the following file data past s_vaddr + s_size into emulated memory
src/file/file_ecoff.c:513-534 at 987cb596: The section loader picks chunk_size 1, 0x10, 0x100 or 0x1000 from the alignment of s_vaddr (:514-517) and clamps the last chunk to the section size (:519-521), but the next line overwrites len with fread(buf, 1, chunk_size, f) (:522), so the clamp has no effect and every chunk is written whole (:530-531). The last chunk of a section can therefore carry up to chunk_size - 1 (at most 4095) bytes of whatever follows in the file into emulated memory past s_vaddr + s_size. buf is 8192 bytes (:76), so host memory is not touched. Source: _scratchpad/fanout_20261030/ARGON_FILE_AUDITS_2.md section 1A N10. Witness: none (research filing).

#### `kn01bytewrite` (MED, OOB-WRITE) -- a CSR read that is not two bytes wide only prints a message and then writes data[0] and data[1], so a byte load writes one byte past the caller's one-byte stack buffer
src/devices/dev_kn01.c:89-101 at 987cb596: The KN01 CSR read path tests len != 2 || relative_addr != 0 but only prints a message (:89-92), then always writes data[0] and data[1] (:96-102). memory_rw() hands the caller's buffer straight to the device (src/cpus/memory_rw.c:587-589), and the MIPS load slow path's buffer is uint8_t data[LS_SIZE] (src/cpus/cpu_mips_instr_loadstore.c:46), one byte for a byte load, so data[1] lands one byte past it on the host stack. KN01 is attached on the DECstation 3100 (src/machines/machine_pmax.c:148) and registered DM_DEFAULT (:263-264), so loads take that slow path. Guest-reachable. Source: _scratchpad/fanout_20261030/ARGON_FILE_AUDITS_2.md section 1B R10. Witness: none (research filing).

Near the top of the int range the sum cur_rgb_offset + 16*i at :91 overflows (undefined), the usual result is negative, and % 0x300 keeps it negative, so the stores at :103-106 land before rgb_palette. It needs about 2^31 data-port writes without an addr_cmap write. Source: _scratchpad/fanout_20261030/ARGON_FILE_AUDITS.md section 1 row 12. Witness: none (research filing).

#### `fbscaledownoob` (LOW, OOB-READ) -- the tick clamps update_y2 to the last visible row and then rounds it up to a multiple of the scale-down factor, so the redraw loop can reach the row at visible_ysize and the scale-down redraw reads past the end of the framebuffer
src/devices/dev_fb.c:634-656 + src/devices/fb_include.c:232-239 at 987cb596: With q = vfb_scaledown above 1, the tick clamps update_y2 to visible_ysize - 1 (:634-635), adds q - 1 (:639) and rounds down to a multiple of q (:644). When visible_ysize is a multiple of q the result is visible_ysize itself, so the loop at :652 calls the redraw for that row, and the scale-down redraw reads framebuffer rows from there on with no bound (src/devices/fb_include.c:232-239 for depths below 8, :272-276 for depth 8, :300-312 above 8). The framebuffer is exactly ysize * bytes_per_line (:904-907), and ysize equals visible_ysize in several configurations (:886, :892, and after every dev_fb_resize() at :200). The pixels read are dropped by macro_put_pixel's y < x11_ysize test (src/devices/fb_include.c:85), so the effect is a host heap over-read. Needs a WITH_X11 build and a scale-down factor above 1 (:902). Source: _scratchpad/fanout_20261030/ARGON_FILE_AUDITS.md section 1 row 19. Witness: none (research filing).

## 2026-11-02 -- `#578` jazzvecdeassert (OB-22, the oldest open entry): a Jazz interrupt-source access no longer drops the CPU's pending IRQ3

* **FIXED** -- `jazzvecdeassert` (OB-22; LOW, WRONG-RESULT -- a dropped level interrupt that heals on the next line assert, tick or
  mask transition): `src/devices/dev_jazz.c`, `DEVICE_ACCESS(jazz_jazzio)`, ended EVERY access to the pica_jazzio register (physical
  0xf0000000: offset 0 the local-bus interrupt-source vector, offset 2 PICA_SYS_LB_IE stored as `jazz_timer_value`) with an unconditional
  `INTERRUPT_DEASSERT(d->mips_irq_3)` under "This is needed by Windows NT during startup".  With a second JAZZ line still pending, the
  guest's vector read for the first dropped IRQ3 while a level interrupt was outstanding.  The statement is DELETED (both twins; the
  function is byte-identical in `est/`) and a `#578` comment stands where it was.  Warrant: the CPU line is kept EQUAL to
  `(int_asserted & 0x7fff) && (int_enable_mask & R4030_EXT_IP3)` by its only three writers -- `jazz_interrupt_assert()`,
  `jazz_interrupt_deassert()` and the EXT_IMASK arm (transitions only) -- so a conditional deassert at the tail (pass 1's form) could never
  fire with an effect: measured EQUIVALENT (M_del 13/13 on the witness, M_cond 22/22 and 26/26 on tables 2 and 3) and entailed by the
  invariant; est keeps its pre-#69 per-line predicate and the same induction holds over it (est UNMEASURED: no binary).  Witness (rung 3,
  unmodified `-V -e pica`, the rig kernel for construction only): `regress/artifacts/jazzvecdeassert/witness_20261102/` 11/13 on HEAD
  (`jz ip after`, `jz ip com1` red) and 13/13 on the fix with the same script.  Detector `regress/jazz_vector_probe.py` (26 rows,
  self-contained pty driver with a failure flag; gate 4's `#578` block, rows run by EQUALITY): 17/26 on HEAD, 26/26 on the fix, 0/26 on
  the null medium; kill tables `killtable_20261102/` (13-row witness, 7 forms), `killtable2_20261102/` (22 rows, 8 forms) and
  `killtable3_20261102/` (the shipped 26 rows, 15 forms: every prediction of `PRETABLE3.out` matched in score and red set; the two
  equivalent/disclosed forms 26/26 by construction).  Heal paths on HEAD, so the severity is LOW: a fresh line assert (a still-enabled
  UART's tick, the interval timer's tick -- the "Linux?" arm that a nonzero LB_IE write arms is the same timer line -- or a new device
  assert) or an EXT_IMASK transition into the enabled state re-raised the line (the assert handler raises on every call made while the
  predicate holds, so a tick re-asserting a still-pending line heals);
  OpenBSD's `pica_iointr` loops on the vector until it reads 0 and arms its timer, so the fix is expected invisible to that guest (gate 4's
  boot, run with the fix before the landing, says so for the rig's kernel); NT unmeasured (no image).  Six carriers of OB-22 above
  (:2037, :2509, :2605, :2869, :2926, :2965 at 50f9c601) are marked in place; the :2965 remedy wording is corrected there.  Panel
  (owner roster 2026-11-02 20:5x: Grok 4.7, the four Ollama cloud seats, Opus 5.5, GPT-6 Astra; Fable 5.1 adjudicating in the main loop):
  pass 1 seven answers, all PROCEED or PROCEED WITH CHANGES, five seats preferring the conditional and the Opus seat the deletion -- ruled
  DELETION on the checked writer census; pass 2 (the deletion, the 22-row detector, both tables) six answers, all SHIP WITH CHANGES, and
  every seat found the detector's contract false -- the (default, write) label cell was unrowed -- which was repaired in-round as a floor
  cell (L2/L4) with five more families closed for free (`idata`, `len`, `jazz_timer_value`, the guest's own BYTE vector read, the page's
  other default byte); the repair's own pass (F2): Opus RWC (4), Grok RWC (1), GLM 5.3 RWC (2), agy RWC (5), kimi RWC (2), minimax RWC (2) -- zero floor
  breaches on every answering seat, so the repair chain closes; their records corrections are applied (the contract's guest-access, level-
  handler and value-disclosure wording; the product comment made twin-neutral because est's enable predicate is per-line).  Astra was WALLED through pass 2 and F2 (hotmail login, "try again at
  Nov 3rd 01:10"); its pass-1 answer stands.  Agy and the Gemini web route were not fired (roster).
* **NOT CHANGED (assessed)**: LB_IE (offset 2) is still stored as `jazz_timer_value` and consulted only by the "Linux?" tick arm -- the
  enable BITS are unmodelled (`jazzlbmask`), and that is where the Windows-NT startup risk now lives: if NT relied on the blanket deassert
  as a stand-in for LB_IE masking, neither the deletion nor pass 1's conditional keeps that case (noted under `jazzlbmask`); the vector
  scan at offset 0 ignores `int_enable_mask` (`jz vec masked` pins it as current behaviour; noted under `jazzlbmask`); the default arm's
  `fatal()` stays unlatched (filed below); `DEVICE_TICK(jazz)`'s "Linux?" arm is inert under single-step (its count is produced by a
  `timer_add` callback the debugger stops) and unchanged.
* **`jazziodfltflood` (LOW, floodclass) -- new.**  `dev_jazz.c` `jazz_jazzio`'s `default:` arm prints an unlatched `fatal()` on every
  byte access to offsets 1 and 3 of the 4-byte page (guest-drivable; the detector itself prints two per run); `jazz_20`, `jazz_a0` and
  `jazz_led` carry the same shape (agy, F2).  House idiom `(once)` per device instance.  Named by the kimi and Opus seats at pass 2.
* **`ns16550out2hold` (LOW, device-model wart) -- new.**  `dev_ns16550.c:92-100`: clearing `MCR.IENABLE` while the IER/IIR condition is
  still true takes the assert branch's outer test and neither asserts nor deasserts, so a Jazz line stays held until IER is cleared
  (OpenBSD clears IER before MCR, so unobserved there).  Named at pass 1 (F9); not a reason to keep the blanket deassert.
* **`jazzvecrowsowed` (LOW, coverage debt + harness) -- new.**  Three one-line strengthenings of `regress/jazz_vector_probe.py`
  named by the F2 pass and FILED because that pass closed the repair chain with zero floor breaches and the shipped instrument is the one
  table 3 measured: (1) OpenBSD/arc's two LB_IE halfword stores are not rowed -- `out16(PICA_SYS_LB_IE, 0)` at initcpu (a zero halfword
  store; lbiew stores 0x0f) and `out16(PICA_SYS_LB_IE, local_int_mask)` at intr_establish (COM enable bits 0x0100 and 0x0200; lbiew's
  0x0f has neither), so a re-introduction keyed to `writeflag == MEM_WRITE && relative_addr == 2 && (idata & 0x0100)` is predicted to keep
  every row green and is guest-visible (Grok F2, from the guest's source; the rows: a zero halfword store with an IP3 check, and lbiew at
  0x0300, which also closes Opus's `idata & 0xff00` slice); (2) the 30 s startup prompt wait's result is not checked, so a late first
  prompt could shift every later command by one without setting `JAZZVEC_DRIVER=bad` (Opus F2; the 26-row EQUALITY pin would almost
  certainly red).  Each owes a table-3 re-run (about two minutes) and its own pass.
* **Harness, in this commit:** `tools/precommit_check.sh` section B now compares a divergence-set `src/` file (`tools/est_divergence.txt`)
  against est/, which build/ compiles, instead of SEC -- the first edit to such a file since the section existed would otherwise have been
  refused on a clean tree (the carrier's 2026-08-31 note predicted exactly this); `SCORE_CLAIMS_MANIFEST` 42 -> 43; `gate_hygiene.sh`
  `EXPECT_PTY_PROBES` 80 -> 81 (`derive_hygiene_pins.sh --write`; the probe is prompt-detecting, not promptless); `check_probe_wiring.py`
  gains the detector's MANIFEST key and one entry per artifact script.
* **Landed** as `2a24d9b7` (2026-11-02 22:10; the hook 0 hard, 5 soft); the pass-2 receipt keyed to it in `regress/pass2_ledger.tsv`; the row stays `held` (see its hold question: Fable as adjudicator rather than seat; Astra walled through pass 2 and F2; the deletion ruling).

## 2026-11-02 -- `#577` shblreset: a SuperH general exception taken with SR.BL set stores the manual-reset code (H'020) and keeps the multiple-hit code

* **FIXED** -- `shblreset` (MED, WRONG-RESULT): `src/cpus/cpu_sh.c`, `sh_exception()` (987cb596 :910-918): with SR.BL set the block printed its

## 2026-11-04 -- `#579` ppcllscrcexit: the PowerPC load-reserve / store-conditional handler no longer ends the emulator process

* **FIXED** -- `ppcllscrcexit` (HIGH): `src/cpus/cpu_ppc_instr.c`, `X(llsc)` ended the process -- `fatal()` + `exit(1)` -- on lwarx/ldarx with bit 31 set and on stwcx./stdcx. with it clear, both delivered by an opcode-31 decoder that keys on the extended opcode alone.  The two guards are DELETED and the unread `rc` dropped: the load pair's bit 31 is a reserved field the processor ignores (Book I v2.01 :432-433, Book II :1264), so the word runs the one body and writes no CR bit; the store pair's bit-clear word is an invalid form, and executing the defined store-conditional, CR0 update included, is one of its permitted outcomes (Book I :1116-1120, Book II :1305/:1307). See the `#579` round block in CHANGELOG.md.

## 2026-11-05 -- `#582` qhslowifetch: a failed slow-path instruction fetch on the PowerPC no longer ends the emulator process

* **FIXED** -- `qhslowifetch` (HIGH): `src/cpus/cpu_ppc_instr.c`, `X(to_be_translated)` printed `read failed: TODO` and called `exit(1)` when the slow-path fetch failed.  The failed read now returns on read-ahead, refreshes next_ic after an exception already delivered, parks the CPU on a -T halt, and takes a machine check (MSR[ME] set) or checkstops (clear) when a device declines the fetch while running; `src/include/cpu_ppc.h` gains `PPC_EXCEPTION_MC`. See the `#582` round block in CHANGELOG.md.

* **Filed, new (all LOW):** `ppcvecaddr` (arm (b) skipped when the exception vector equals the failing fetch: the fix's #MMM); `ppcmpcheckstop` (the checkstop on a multiprocessor: #PPP); `ppcifetchibinit` (zero-initialise ib, so the build-dependent variants decide deterministically); `ppcbranchlowbits` (X(bclr_20) keeps pc's low two bits; Book I clears them); `ppcifetchdeclineprod` (ROW 5: no measured machine produces arm (d), pending an X11 build or a window sweep on bebox, prep, macppc and mvmeppc); `memrwtreadahead` (memory_rw's -T halt fires on a read-ahead fetch the guest has not reached: the final ruling's F4); `vgagfxwindowend` (dev_vga's `>=` declines the vga_gfx window's last word: ROW 5's producer).
